definition_zh: 生态平衡；生态系统内部各要素之间的稳定协调状态
definition_en: a stable condition in which the living and non-living parts of an ecosystem keep one another in check
core_image: 一片水塘里，水草、小鱼与捕食的鸟各自维持在差不多的数量，水面既不清瘦也不浑浊
scene: 这片海湾限制捕捞量，鱼群、海草和捕食者都维持在原来的规模。 Fishing quotas help keep an ecological balance in the bay.
sceneCN: 这里指生态系统各要素之间维持稳定协调（第 1 个义项：生态平衡的总体状态）；句意为捕捞配额有助于维持湾内的生态平衡。图中可辨识物件：水塘、水草、小鱼、捕食的鸟。

pos.zh: 生态平衡；生态系统各要素间的稳定协调

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「住所」与「学问」合成，义为「生态学」
由「生态学」加形容词词尾构成，义为「生态的；生态学的」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「在生态方面」
由「生态学」加表示从事者的名词尾构成，义为「生态学家」
由否定前缀加「平衡」构成，义为「失衡」，与本词构成反义对照

senses.title: The overall stable state
senses.definition: the general condition in which an ecosystem stays stable over time
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统在较长时期内保持稳定的总体状况
senses.example: The wetland still shows a remarkable ecological balance after the restoration.
senses.exampleCN: 修复之后的湿地仍呈现出显著的生态平衡。
senses.why: The compound joins the study of the household to the image of a two-pan scale, and the whole is the state where both pans hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把「家园的学问」接到两盘天平的画面上，整体就是两盘都端住的状态。

senses.title: Balance among species numbers
senses.definition: a condition in which the populations of different species stay within ranges that support one another
senses.definitionCN: 不同物种的种群数量各自保持在互相支撑的范围内
senses.example: Predators and prey kept an ecological balance on the island for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者与猎物在这个岛上维持了数百年的生态平衡。
senses.why: Species are the weights on the scale, and balance means no single one runs away with the total.
senses.whyCN: 物种是天平上的重量，平衡意味着没有哪一个把总量带走。

senses.title: Stability of the food web
senses.definition: a condition in which energy passes through the food chain without any link being exhausted
senses.definitionCN: 能量沿食物链传递，而没有哪一环被耗尽
senses.example: Removing one link in the chain upset the ecological balance of the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 去掉链上的一环，打乱了这片湖的生态平衡。
senses.why: A chain is stable when each link can feed the next, which is the balance seen as flow rather than as weight.
senses.whyCN: 链条稳定在于每一环都喂得饱下一环，这是把平衡看作流动而非重量。

senses.title: Balance between resources and consumption
senses.definition: a condition in which what an area produces is matched by what its inhabitants take
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区生产的东西与居民取用的东西大体相抵
senses.example: Grazing levels were cut to restore an ecological balance between grass and cattle.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧量被削减，以恢复草与牛之间的生态平衡。
senses.why: This is the accounting face of the compound: what grows is entered against what is eaten.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个复合词的会计面孔：长出来的与吃掉的对着记账。

senses.title: Balance between human activity and nature
senses.titleCN: 人类活动与自然的平衡
senses.definition: a condition in which human use of land and water does not overwhelm natural renewal
senses.definitionCN: 人类对土地与水的使用没有压过自然更新的能力
senses.example: The plan tries to hold an ecological balance between tourism and the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案试图在旅游与珊瑚礁之间维持生态平衡。
senses.why: Modern usage puts people on one pan, which is why the phrase appears so often in planning disputes.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把人放上天平的一端，所以这个短语常出现在规划争议里。

senses.title: Self-regulation of an ecosystem
senses.definition: the capacity of an ecosystem to correct small disturbances through its own feedback
senses.definitionCN: 生态系统通过自身反馈修正小扰动的能力
senses.example: The forest recovered because its ecological balance still had room to adjust.
senses.exampleCN: 森林得以恢复，是因为它的生态平衡还有调整的余地。
senses.why: Feedback is the mechanism behind the metaphor: a change triggers a counter-change.
senses.whyCN: 反馈是这一比喻背后的机制：一个变化引出反向的变化。

senses.title: Balance between load and carrying capacity
senses.titleCN: 环境承载力与压力的平衡
senses.definition: a condition in which pressure on a habitat stays within the limit it can absorb
senses.definitionCN: 对栖息地的压力保持在其可承受的限度之内
senses.example: Nutrient runoff pushed the river past its ecological balance.
senses.exampleCN: 营养物径流把这条河推过了它的生态平衡。
senses.why: Carrying capacity is a ceiling, and balance is living under it without touching it.
senses.whyCN: 承载力是一个上限，而平衡是在它下面生活而不去顶到它。

senses.title: A conservation goal
senses.definition: a target that environmental policy tries to maintain or restore through management
senses.definitionCN: 环境政策试图通过管理来维持或恢复的目标
senses.example: The reserve was created to protect the ecological balance of the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 设立这个保护区，是为了保护三角洲的生态平衡。
senses.why: Policy turns a description into an aim, and the phrase becomes something to keep rather than merely to observe.
senses.whyCN: 政策把描述变成目标，于是这个短语成了要去维持而不只是去观察的东西。

intro.en: Ecological balance joins ecology, coined by Haeckel in the nineteenth century from Greek oikos, house, and logia, study, to balance, from Late Latin bilanx, having two scales. The compound itself is modern and its first date is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把「生态学」与「平衡」接在一起：前者由海克尔在十九世纪用希腊语 oikos「住所」与 logia「学问」合成，后者来自晚期拉丁语 bilanx「有两副秤盘」。复合词本身属现代，首见年代不确定。

items.en: Oikos meant house or dwelling, and ecology began as the study of the household of nature.
items.cn: 这个词意为住所、家宅，生态学最初就是研究自然这个「家」的学问。

items.en: Logia meant the study or account of something, and it supplies the second half of ecology.
items.cn: 这个词意为对某事的学问或论述，提供「生态学」的后半部分。

items.en: Haeckel coined the German term for ecology in the nineteenth century, and English adopted it soon after.
items.cn: 海克尔在十九世纪造出德语的生态学术语，英语随后采用。

items.en: Balance came from bilanx, having two pans, from bi-, two, and lanx, a pan or scale.
items.cn: 「平衡」来自 bilanx「有两副秤盘」，由 bi-「二」与 lanx「盘、秤」构成。

items.en: The phrase ecological balance belongs to twentieth-century environmental writing; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个短语属二十世纪的环境写作，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Conservation law turned the phrase into a management target, so it now names something to be kept, not merely described.
items.cn: 保护法规把这个短语变成管理目标，于是它现在指要维持的东西，而不只是被描述的状态。

note.en: The first group shares the balance or ecology element but means something else; the second group names neighbouring environmental ideas.
note.cn: 第一组共享「平衡」或「生态」这一成分但意思不同；第二组是与「环境稳定」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The study of relationships between organisms and their surroundings.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究生物与其环境之间关系的学科。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指与生态学相关的。

entries.definition: A state of equal weight, used far beyond ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 指重量相等的状态，用法远超生态领域。

entries.definition: A state of unequal weight, the direct negation.
entries.definitionCN: 指重量不均的状态，是本词的直接否定。

entries.definition: A state of balance, usually in physics or chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 指平衡状态，多用于物理或化学。

entries.definition: The capacity to keep going without exhausting resources.
entries.definitionCN: 指不耗尽资源而持续下去的能力。

entries.definition: The variety of living things in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地方生物的多样性。

entries.definition: A balanced state in a system, often measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统中的平衡状态，常可测量。

entries.definition: The self-correcting stability of an organism.
entries.definitionCN: 指生物体自我修正的稳定状态。

entries.definition: The largest load an environment can support.
entries.definitionCN: 指环境能支撑的最大负荷。

entries.definition: The protection of nature from damage.
entries.definitionCN: 指对自然的保护，使之不受损害。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the household at the root of ecology, the two pans at the root of balance, and the policy phrases that keep the compound in use.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用生态学词根里的「家宅」、平衡词根里的「两副秤盘」，以及让这个复合词保持活跃的政策搭配。

normal.en: Oikos is house, so ecology is the study of nature as one household.
normal.cn: oikos 是「家宅」，所以生态学是把自然当作一个家来研究。

normal.en: Balance comes from two pans, and an ecosystem balances when no single pan runs away.
normal.cn: 平衡来自两副秤盘，生态系统平衡就是没有哪一盘跑掉。

normal.en: The phrase is a noun, so it takes maintain, keep, disturb, restore and break as its verbs.
normal.cn: 这个短语是名词，常与维持、保持、扰乱、恢复、破坏这些动词搭配。

normal.en: Imbalance is the direct opposite and is far more common in headlines.
normal.cn: 失衡是直接反义词，在新闻标题里更常见。

normal.en: Carrying capacity is the ceiling; balance is what keeps a population under it.
normal.cn: 承载力是天花板，平衡就是让种群待在天花板下面。

abstract.en: An ecological balance is not a frozen picture but a set of corrections that never stop.
abstract.cn: 生态平衡不是一张冻结的图画，而是一组永不停止的修正。

abstract.en: Every pan that rises pulls the other down, which is why the system looks still while moving.
abstract.cn: 一端上升必然拉低另一端，所以系统看着不动，其实一直在动。

abstract.en: To protect a balance is to accept that human beings are also one of the weights.
abstract.cn: 保护一种平衡，就是承认人类自己也是天平上的一份重量。

examples.en: The national park was enlarged to protect the ecological balance of the valley.
examples.cn: 国家公园被扩大，以保护山谷的生态平衡。

examples.en: Draining the marsh broke the ecological balance that had held for generations.
examples.cn: 排干沼泽破坏了维持数代的生态平衡。

examples.en: Farmers and biologists worked together to restore an ecological balance in the lake.
examples.cn: 农民与生物学家合作，恢复湖里的生态平衡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「伊扣勒吉扣 巴伦斯」——水塘里草、鱼、鸟各守其量：生态平衡

root: 希腊语 oikos「住所」+ logia「学问」合成 ecology（海克尔，十九世纪）；balance 来自晚期拉丁语 bilanx「有两副秤盘」（bi-「二」+ lanx「盘」）。复合词属现代，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a system holding steady: the general state, species numbers, the food web, resources, human use, self-correction, carrying capacity and a policy goal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述系统保持稳定：总体状态、物种数量、食物链、资源、人类使用、自我调节、承载力与政策目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pondweed, small fish and hunting birds each keep their share, so the water is neither bare nor cloudy.
core.cn: 核心意象：水草、小鱼与捕食的鸟各守其量，水面既不清瘦也不浑浊。

branches.en: THE WHOLE HOLDS: the ecosystem as a single household stays within its range.
branches.cn: 整体端住：生态系统作为一个家，保持在它的范围内。

branches.en: THE WEIGHTS AND THE FLOW: species numbers and the links of the food chain keep one another fed.
branches.cn: 重量与流动：物种数量与食物链各环互相喂饱。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT AND THE CEILING: what grows is matched by what is taken, and pressure stays under capacity.
branches.cn: 账目与上限：长出的与取用的相抵，压力待在承载力之下。

branches.en: THE HUMAN PAN: people are placed on one side of the scale and must not sink it.
branches.cn: 人的那一盘：人被放上天平一端，不能把它压沉。

branches.en: THE CORRECTION AND THE AIM: feedback fixes small shocks, and policy turns the state into a target.
branches.cn: 修正与目标：反馈修正小冲击，政策把状态变成目标。

intro.en: The compound draws one half from Greek through modern science and the other from Latin through French, which is why its pieces look so different.
intro.cn: 这个复合词一半经现代科学取自希腊语，另一半经法语取自拉丁语，所以部件看起来差别很大。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies oikos and logia, Latin supplies bilanx, bi- and lanx; the modern compound itself has no single classical source.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供 oikos 与 logia，拉丁语提供 bilanx、bi- 与 lanx；现代复合词本身没有单一的古典来源。

definition_zh: n. 蜂箱；蜂巢；忙碌喧闹之所（喻）；蜂巢式高蓬发型
definition_en: a box or domed structure in which bees live; a place full of busy activity; a tall rounded hairstyle shaped like a straw hive
core_image: 草编的圆顶蜂箱，门口进出不停，里面一片嗡嗡
scene: 办公室里人人都在跑，电话一直没停。 The office was a beehive, with everyone moving and the phones never quiet.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：beehive 比喻忙碌喧闹的场所；句意是办公室里人人奔忙、电话不断。

pos.zh: 蜂箱；忙碌之所；蜂巢发型

senses.title: Where bees live
senses.definition: a man-made box or a traditional straw dome housing a colony of bees
senses.definitionCN: 人工蜂箱或传统草编圆顶，容纳一个蜂群
senses.example: He lifted the lid of the beehive without smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 他不用烟就掀开了蜂箱盖。
senses.why: The compound is transparent: bee plus hive, where hive already meant a vessel.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词一目了然：bee「蜂」加 hive「巢」，而 hive 本就意为容器。

senses.title: A busy place
senses.definition: a place where many people work busily and noisily together
senses.definitionCN: 许多人一起忙碌喧闹地工作的地方
senses.example: The newsroom became a beehive before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 截稿前编辑部忙成了一片。
senses.why: A colony has many workers in one small space, which is exactly the picture of a busy office.
senses.whyCN: 一个蜂群是在狭小空间里挤满劳作者，这正是忙碌办公室的画面。

senses.title: A tall hairstyle
senses.definition: a hairstyle piled high and rounded on the head, popular in the 1960s
senses.definitionCN: 在头顶高高堆起、盘成圆蓬的发型，1960 年代流行
senses.example: She wore a beehive pinned with a silver comb.
senses.exampleCN: 她梳着蜂巢头，别了一把银梳。
senses.why: The shape of a straw dome is the whole point of the name, so this sense is pure outline.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字全靠草编圆顶的外形，因此该义项纯粹取自轮廓。

intro.en: Beehive joins two very old words: bee, unchanged for a thousand years, and hive, which once meant any rounded vessel.
intro.cn: beehive 拼合了两个极古老的词：bee 千年未变，hive 则曾泛指任何圆形容器。

items.en: The root meant a hollow or rounded container, the idea behind hive.
items.cn: 该词根意为空腔或圆形容器，是 hive 背后的构想。

items.en: Old English beo names the insect, a word unchanged for a thousand years.
items.cn: 古英语 beo 指这种昆虫，千年未变。

items.en: Old English hyf means a vessel or hive, kin to a word for a ship hull.
items.cn: 古英语 hyf 指容器或蜂巢，与「船体」一词同源。

items.en: Middle English joins the two into a single word for the vessel that holds bees.
items.cn: 中古英语把两者合成一词，指盛蜂之器。

items.en: A crowded busy place is called a hive of activity.
items.cn: 拥挤忙碌的场所被称作 a hive of activity。

items.en: A tall rounded hairstyle takes the name from its shape.
items.cn: 一种高耸圆蓬的发型因形状得名。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps bee compounds and the near-homophone behave; the near-meaning group moves from the beekeeper technical terms to the plain word nest.
note.cn: 形近组保留 bee 复合词与近音的 behave；近义组由养蜂专业术语过渡到最朴素的 nest。

entries.definition: A direct straight path to a target.
entries.definitionCN: 直奔目标的直线路径。

entries.definition: To act in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 以某种方式行事。

entries.definition: To lift or pull something heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 用力举起或拖拽重物。

entries.definition: Wax made by bees for building comb.
entries.definitionCN: 蜜蜂造脾所用的蜡。

entries.definition: A place where many hives are kept.
entries.definitionCN: 放置许多蜂箱的养蜂场。

entries.definition: The wax cells built inside a hive.
entries.definitionCN: 蜂箱内筑起的蜡质巢室。

entries.definition: A traditional domed hive made of straw.
entries.definitionCN: 传统的草编圆顶蜂箱。

entries.definition: A structure where animals lay eggs or live.
entries.definitionCN: 动物产卵或栖居的构造。

normalIntro.en: Beehive is bee plus hive, and hive once meant a rounded vessel. One shape gives you all three senses: box, busy office, tall hair.
normalIntro.cn: beehive 就是 bee 加 hive，而 hive 曾意为圆形容器。一个形状给出全部三义：蜂箱、忙碌办公室、高耸发型。

normal.en: A straw dome with a small door at the base.
normal.cn: 底部开小门的草编圆顶。

normal.en: Thousands of workers in one small space.
normal.cn: 狭小空间里的成千上万劳作者。

normal.en: A newsroom before deadline is a beehive.
normal.cn: 截稿前的编辑部就是一片蜂箱。

normal.en: Hair piled into the same dome is a beehive.
normal.cn: 头发堆成同样的圆顶也叫 beehive。

normal.en: An apiary is where many beehives stand.
normal.cn: apiary 是摆放许多蜂箱的地方。

abstract.en: Order produced by many small selfish acts.
abstract.cn: 许多微小自利行为合出的秩序。

abstract.en: Noise that turns out to be work.
abstract.cn: 原来就是劳作的喧闹。

abstract.en: A shape borrowed by insects, offices and hairdressers.
abstract.cn: 一个被昆虫、办公室与理发师依次借走的形状。

examples.en: The beehives stood in a row along the orchard wall.
examples.cn: 蜂箱沿果园墙排成一列。

examples.en: By nine the kitchen was a beehive of activity.
examples.cn: 到九点厨房已忙成一片。

examples.en: Her beehive added a hand span to her height.
examples.cn: 蜂巢头让她高出足足一掌。

root: bee 出自古英语 beo，hive 出自古英语 hyf「容器」，与「船体」一词同源，深层为「空腔、圆形容器」之义。约 1300 年合成 beehive；18 世纪生出「忙碌之所」的比喻义，1960 年代因发型形似草编圆顶而再增一义。

definition_zh: 负债状态；负债总额；受恩之情；道义上的亏欠
definition_en: the state or extent of owing money, or the state of being under an obligation of gratitude
core_image: 年末账房里，先生把各家欠款抄成一页总数，纸角压着一枚镇纸
scene: 年末账房里，先生把各家欠款抄成一页总数，纸角压着一枚镇纸。 The family's indebtedness forced them to sell the farm.
sceneCN: 这里 indebtedness 指「负债状态」（第 1 个义项：处于欠债之中的状况）；句意为这家人的负债状态迫使他们卖掉了农场。图中可辨识物件：总账页、镇纸、算盘、封蜡。

pos.zh: 负债状态；负债总额；受恩之感（不可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多种负债情形）

senses.title: The state of owing money
senses.definition: the condition of being under a financial obligation to repay money
senses.definitionCN: 处于须偿还资金的财务义务之下的状况
senses.example: The family's indebtedness forced them to sell the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人的负债状态迫使他们卖掉了农场。
senses.why: indebted is the adjective for being placed under a debt, and -ness turns that condition into a noun.
senses.whyCN: indebted 是「被置于债务之下」的形容词，-ness 把这种状况变成名词。

senses.title: The total amount owed
senses.definition: the aggregate sum a person, firm or country owes at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 个人、企业或国家在某一时点所欠的总额
senses.example: The report measured the indebtedness of the whole sector.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告衡量了整个行业的负债总额。
senses.why: the state noun is also used for the size of the state, because an aggregate is easiest to discuss as a condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个状态名词也用来指状态的规模，因为总量最便于当作一种状况来讨论。

senses.title: An obligation to return a favour
senses.definition: the state of being bound to repay a kindness received
senses.definitionCN: 因受人之惠而须回报的状态
senses.example: Her indebtedness to the mentor shaped every later choice.
senses.exampleCN: 她对恩师的亏欠影响了此后每一个选择。
senses.why: the metaphor of debt extends to kindness: a favour is received and a return is expected.
senses.whyCN: 债务的比喻扩展到善意：受了恩惠，就有回报的期待。

senses.title: A feeling of gratitude
senses.definition: the emotion of gratitude that accompanies a favour one cannot easily repay
senses.definitionCN: 因受惠而难以轻易回报所伴随的感激之情
senses.example: He spoke of his indebtedness with tears in his eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 他谈起自己的受恩之感时眼里含着泪。
senses.why: indebted came to mean grateful in the seventeenth century, and the noun carried that feeling with it.
senses.whyCN: indebted 在 17 世纪获得「感激」义，这个名词也带着那份感情。

senses.title: Leverage in economics
senses.definition: the ratio that shows how much of an entity's activity is financed by borrowing
senses.definitionCN: 显示某实体的活动有多少由借入资金支撑的比率
senses.example: Rising indebtedness made the airline vulnerable to a rate rise.
senses.exampleCN: 杠杆水平上升使这家航空公司在利率上升时变得脆弱。
senses.why: economics prefers the state noun because it measures a condition rather than a single loan.
senses.whyCN: 经济学偏爱这个状态名词，因为它衡量的是状况而非单笔贷款。

senses.title: Legal liability status
senses.definition: the position of being legally answerable for a debt, as in a balance sheet
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上对债务负有责任的地位，如资产负债表所列
senses.example: The audit questioned the indebtedness recorded for the subsidiary.
senses.exampleCN: 审计对子公司账上的负债地位提出疑问。
senses.why: law and accounting care about who is answerable, so the state of being bound is the relevant fact.
senses.whyCN: 法律与会计关心谁负有责任，因此「被约束的状态」才是相关事实。

senses.title: A bond of service in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧时受惠而形成的服役束缚
senses.definition: historically, the condition of being bound to a lord or patron by gifts or favours received
senses.definitionCN: 历史上因受赠或受惠而对领主或赞助人形成的束缚
senses.example: The old chronicle describes the indebtedness of the tenants to the abbey.
senses.exampleCN: 这部旧编年史记述了佃户对修道院的受惠束缚。
senses.why: before money credit was common, favours and gifts created lasting ties that were also called debts.
senses.whyCN: 在金钱信贷普及之前，恩惠与赠礼造成持久关系，也被称作欠。

senses.title: Being beholden to an influence
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：受某种影响所困
senses.definition: figuratively, the state of owing one's ideas or success to a person, a school or an age
senses.definitionCN: 比喻上指自己的思想或成就归功于某人、某学派或某个时代的状态
senses.example: The painter's indebtedness to the northern masters is plain in every canvas.
senses.exampleCN: 这位画家对北方大师的亏欠在每幅画上都显而易见。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the structure of owing while the creditor becomes an influence rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了欠的结构，只是债权人从一个人变成了一种影响。

intro.en: Indebtedness is built inside English from in-, debt, -ed and -ness; debt itself is Latin. The compound may have been helped by Medieval Latin indebitatus. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: indebtedness 由英语内部用 in-、debt、-ed、-ness 构成；debt 本身是拉丁词。这个复合形式可能受中世纪拉丁 indebitatus 影响。年代均为约数。

items.en: Debitum 'that which is owed' is the base of debt, borrowed through Old French dette with the b later restored in spelling.
items.cn: debitum「被欠之物」是 debt 的词基，经古法语 dette 借入，后来在拼写上补回 b。

items.en: The prefix in- here means 'in a state or condition', not 'not': indebted is being placed in debt, not being free of it.
items.cn: 这里的前缀 in- 意为「处于某种状态」，而非否定：indebted 是陷入债务，不是免于债务。

items.en: The participial ending -ed turns the noun into an adjective meaning 'placed under', giving indebted.
items.cn: 分词词尾 -ed 把名词变成表示「被置于……之下」的形容词，形成 indebted。

items.en: Medieval Latin indebitatus is generally thought to have supported the English form, though English could have built it independently.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 indebitatus 一般认为支持了英语形式，尽管英语也可能自行构成。

items.en: The ending -ness is the native suffix for a state, so indebtedness names the condition rather than any single debt.
items.cn: 词尾 -ness 是本族表示状态的后缀，因此 indebtedness 指状况，而非任何一笔具体的债。

items.en: From the seventeenth century indebted also meant grateful, and indebtedness followed, adding a sense no accounting book contains.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，indebted 也指感激，indebtedness 随之获得一层任何账簿都不包含的意思。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same debt family; group two holds measures and states of owing that differ in scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出债务词族的形式；第二组是范围不同的欠债状态与度量。

entries.definition: The adjective for owing money or gratitude; the noun adds -ness to name the state.
entries.definitionCN: 表示负债或受恩的形容词；名词加 -ness 指这种状态。

entries.definition: A specific obligation; indebtedness is the condition of having such obligations.
entries.definitionCN: 具体的偿付义务；indebtedness 是拥有这类义务的状况。

entries.definition: The party who owes; the state noun describes that party's position.
entries.definitionCN: 欠债的一方；状态名词描述这一方的处境。

entries.definition: A bookkeeping entry on the left side; it is a record of a change, not a state of owing.
entries.definitionCN: 账簿左侧的分录；它记录变动，而非欠债状态。

entries.definition: The proportion of debt used to finance assets; indebtedness is the raw condition, leverage the measured ratio.
entries.definitionCN: 用债务为资产融资的比例；indebtedness 是原始状态，leverage 是测得的比率。

entries.definition: All amounts a firm must pay, including non-debt items such as provisions; indebtedness usually counts only borrowings.
entries.definitionCN: 企业须支付的全部金额，包括拨备等非债务项；indebtedness 通常只计借入款项。

entries.definition: The ability to meet obligations as they fall due; it is the test applied to indebtedness.
entries.definitionCN: 按期履行义务的能力；它是对负债状态所施加的检验。

entries.definition: Thankfulness for a kindness; indebtedness in its emotional sense is gratitude mixed with a sense of owing.
entries.definitionCN: 对善意的感谢；情感义的 indebtedness 是感激夹杂着亏欠感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'in a state' + debt + -ed + -ness: the condition of being placed under a debt.
normal.cn: in-「处于状态」+ debt + -ed + -ness：被置于债务之下的状况。

normal.en: The family runs debt, debtor, indebted, indebtedness, indebt and debit.
normal.cn: 同族包括 debt、debtor、indebted、indebtedness、indebt 与 debit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: household indebtedness, corporate indebtedness, a sense of indebtedness.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：家庭负债、企业负债、受恩之感。

normal.en: The in- here is not a negative: indebted means in debt, not free of it.
normal.cn: 这里的 in- 不是否定：indebted 意为陷入债务，不是免于债务。

normal.en: Indebted also means grateful, so indebtedness can name an emotion.
normal.cn: indebted 也指感激，因此 indebtedness 可以指一种情感。

examples.cn: 高负债使新投资几乎没有空间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（陷入）+ debt（债）+ ness（状态）」——陷在债里的那种状态 → 负债、受恩

root: 英语内部构成：in-（处于某种状态）+ debt（债务，来自拉丁 debitum）+ -ed + -ness。中世纪拉丁 indebitatus 一般认为对形式有支持作用。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one condition: a person or body is placed under an obligation, and that condition is then measured, extended to kindness, felt as gratitude, read in accounts, tied to old service and finally owed to an influence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种处境展开：人或机构被置于某项义务之下，这种处境再依次被计量、扩展到恩惠、感受为感激、在账上读取、联系到旧时服役，最后归欠于一种影响。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of totals pressed under a paperweight, sealed but not settled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页总数压在镇纸下，封了蜡却仍未结清。

branches.en: THE CONDITION AND ITS SIZE: being in debt and the total owed are two views of one state.
branches.cn: 处境与规模：处于负债与负债总额是同一状态的两种视角。

branches.en: A FAVOUR OWED: kindness received creates a return obligation.
branches.cn: 欠下的恩惠：受人之惠产生回报义务。

branches.en: THE FEELING: gratitude is the emotional form of owing.
branches.cn: 感受：感激是「欠」的情感形态。

branches.en: MEASURED AND LEGAL: leverage ratios and balance-sheet liability turn the state into a figure.
branches.cn: 计量与法律：杠杆比率与资产负债表负债把状态变成数字。

branches.en: OLD BONDS AND NEW MASTERS: service to an abbey and debt to a school of painting share the shape.
branches.cn: 旧束缚与新师承：对修道院的服役与对某画派的亏欠形状相同。

intro.en: The word stacks an English prefix, a Latin noun, an English participial ending and an English state ending, a clear case of mixed stock.
intro.cn: 这个词叠了一个英语前缀、一个拉丁名词、一个英语分词词尾与一个英语状态词尾，是成分混杂的明显例子。

latinIntro.en: Only the noun debt is Latin, from debitum; in-, -ed and -ness are English, so the family mixes a Romance core with Germanic grammar.
latinIntro.cn: 只有名词 debt 是拉丁语，来自 debitum；in-、-ed 与 -ness 都是英语，因此这个词族把罗曼语词核与日耳曼语法混在一起。

definition_zh: 多样化；分散投资；业务多元化
definition_en: the process of adding variety, especially by spreading investments or activities
core_image: 一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分装到许多只篮子，每只篮子走向不同的方向
scene: 理财顾问把客户的资金分到不同行业与地区，以避免单一市场崩盘带来的冲击。 Diversification reduced the fund's loss when one sector collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里指「分散投资」，对应第 2 个义项：把资金分散到不同资产以降低风险；句意为一个行业崩盘时，分散化降低了基金的损失。画面要点：多只篮子、行业标签、下跌曲线。

pos.zh: 多样化；分散化；分散投资；业务多元化

forms.label: 复数（少见，指多次分散过程）

derivatives.zh: 分散风险者；多元化经营者

senses.title: The general process of adding variety
senses.definition: the act of making something include a wider range of types
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物包含更广泛类型的行为
senses.example: Diversification of the curriculum widened student choice.
senses.exampleCN: 课程多样化扩大了学生的选择。
senses.why: The noun names the act of turning one kind into many, the most general reading of the verb behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指把一种变成多种的动作，是背后动词最一般的读法。

senses.title: Spreading investments
senses.definition: the practice of spreading money across assets so that one failure does not sink the whole
senses.definitionCN: 把资金分散到不同资产，使单一失败不至于拖垮整体
senses.example: Diversification cannot remove risk, only redistribute it.
senses.exampleCN: 分散投资不能消除风险，只能重新分配风险。
senses.why: In finance the many kinds are many holdings; the purpose is not variety for its own sake but spreading the chance of loss.
senses.whyCN: 在金融中，多种类就是多项持有；目的不是为多样而多样，而是分散损失的可能性。

senses.title: Entering new lines of business
senses.definition: a company's expansion into products or markets different from its original one
senses.definitionCN: 公司扩展到与原业务不同的产品或市场
senses.example: Diversification into software saved the publisher.
senses.exampleCN: 向软件业务多元化拯救了这家出版商。
senses.why: A firm with one product is a basket with one egg, so the word describes adding other baskets of revenue.
senses.whyCN: 只有一种产品的公司就像只放一枚鸡蛋的篮子，这个词因此指增添其他收入篮子。

senses.title: Spreading across regions
senses.definition: the expansion of activity into different countries or regions
senses.definitionCN: 把活动扩展到不同国家或地区
senses.example: Geographic diversification protected sales during the home slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 地域分散化在本国放缓期间保住了销售。
senses.why: The many kinds here are many places: a collapse in one region is offset by activity elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这里的多种类是多个地方：一个地区的崩塌可由别处的活动来抵消。

senses.title: Crop diversification
senses.definition: the practice of growing several crops instead of relying on one
senses.definitionCN: 种植多种作物而不是依赖单一作物的做法
senses.example: Crop diversification improved the soil and the farmer's income.
senses.exampleCN: 作物多样化改善了土壤，也提高了农民收入。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the financial logic to the field: several crops hedge against weather and price swings.
senses.whyCN: 农业把金融逻辑搬到田里：几种作物共同对冲天气与价格波动。

senses.title: Economic diversification
senses.definition: the broadening of a regional or national economy beyond one industry
senses.definitionCN: 把地区或国家经济扩展到单一产业之外
senses.example: Oil revenue funded the country's economic diversification.
senses.exampleCN: 石油收入资助了这个国家的经济多元化。
senses.why: A whole economy can be a single basket, so the word scales up from a firm to a state.
senses.whyCN: 整个经济体也可以是一只单一的篮子，于是这个词从公司放大到国家。

senses.title: Biological diversification
senses.definition: the increase of variety among species or genes over time
senses.definitionCN: 物种或基因随时间增加多样性
senses.example: Island isolation drove rapid diversification of the birds.
senses.exampleCN: 岛屿隔离推动了这些鸟类的快速分化。
senses.why: Biology uses the same shape without human choice: one ancestral form branches into many forms.
senses.whyCN: 生物学使用同样的形状，却没有人为选择：一个祖型分化为许多类型。

senses.title: The resulting mixed state
senses.titleCN: 分散之后形成的混合状态
senses.definition: the condition of being made up of varied parts rather than one
senses.definitionCN: 由多种成分而非单一成分构成的状态
senses.example: The portfolio's diversification made its returns smoother.
senses.exampleCN: 这个组合的分散状态使其回报更平稳。
senses.why: The word can name not only the act but the result: a whole that is now visibly made of many parts.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅能指动作，也能指结果：一个如今明显由许多部分构成的整体。

intro.en: Diversification is an English noun built on Latin roots meaning to turn apart and to make. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: diversification 是英语名词，建立在表示「转向别处」与「制造」的拉丁词根上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vertere meant to turn, and it underlies divertere, convertere and a large family of English words about turning.
items.cn: vertere 意为转动，是 divertere、convertere 以及一大批表示「转」的英语词的底层。

items.en: Diversus meant turned in different directions, hence various or separate, the source of diverse and diversity.
items.cn: diversus 意为被转向不同方向，因此指多样或分开，是 diverse 与 diversity 的来源。

items.en: The verb joined diversus with facere 'to make', literally to make things turn apart, that is, to make them varied.
items.cn: 这个动词把 diversus 与 facere「制造」结合，字面是使事物转向不同方向，也就是使之多样。

items.en: French carried the verb into ordinary use, and English borrowed the verb in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词带入日常使用，英语在十七世纪借入了该动词。

items.en: The noun ending -ification names the process of making, so diversification is literally the making of variety.
items.cn: 名词后缀 -ification 表示「使……的过程」，所以 diversification 字面上就是「使多样」。

items.en: Twentieth-century finance and management gave the noun its specialized readings: spreading holdings, markets and products.
items.cn: 二十世纪的金融与管理学赋予这个名词专门含义：分散持有、市场与产品。

note.en: The first group is built from the same turning root; the second group names the result or a neighboring strategy.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「转」的词根上；第二组指结果或相邻策略。

entries.definition: The state of having many different kinds; diversification is the act of producing that state.
entries.definitionCN: 具有许多不同种类的状态；diversification 是产生这种状态的动作。

entries.definition: Varied or different; it describes the parts, while diversification names the change that creates them.
entries.definitionCN: 多样的、不同的；它描述各个部分，而 diversification 指创造这些部分的变化。

entries.definition: To turn something aside or to entertain; it shares the turning image but has no sense of adding variety.
entries.definitionCN: 使转向一旁，或使娱乐；共享「转」的意象，但没有增加多样的意思。

entries.definition: A change of route or an amusement; it turns one thing away rather than multiplying kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 改道或消遣；它是把一样东西转开，而不是增加种类。

entries.definition: Distributing something over a wider area; in finance it is the practical effect of diversification.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物分布到更广的范围；在金融中它是分散化的实际效果。

entries.definition: Making a range wider; it stresses extent, while diversification stresses the addition of different types.
entries.definitionCN: 使范围更宽；强调广度，而分散化强调加入不同类型。

entries.definition: Growth in size or reach; expansion can stay in one line, while diversification must cross into another.
entries.definitionCN: 规模或范围的扩大；扩张可以停留在同一业务线，而多元化必须跨到另一条。

entries.definition: Taking an offsetting position to reduce risk; hedging is one reason to diversify, not the same action.
entries.definitionCN: 建立对冲头寸以降低风险；对冲是分散化的一个理由，而不是同一动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real turning root, the real making suffix and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「转动」词根、真实的「制造」后缀与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The first half means turned apart, the second half means making, so the word is making things turn apart.
normal.cn: 前半意为转向不同方向，后半意为制造，所以这个词就是使事物分向多处。

normal.en: Finance applies it to eggs and baskets: many holdings instead of one.
normal.cn: 金融把它用到鸡蛋与篮子上：多项持有而不是只有一项。

normal.en: Business applies it to products and regions; agriculture applies it to crops.
normal.cn: 企业把它用到产品与地区；农业把它用到作物。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: portfolio, product, geographic, economic, crop.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出尺度：组合、产品、地域、经济、作物。

normal.en: Diversity is the state; diversification is the act that produces it.
normal.cn: diversity 是状态，diversification 是产生该状态的动作。

abstract.en: Picture one egg in one basket, then the same egg copied into many baskets walking in different directions.
abstract.cn: 想象一只篮子里放一枚鸡蛋，随后同一枚蛋被分装到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a single road splitting into many roads, so no closure can stop all travel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路分成许多条，任何一处封闭都无法阻断全部通行。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree branching outward, the same shape as a portfolio spreading outward.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家谱树向外分枝，与投资组合向外分散是同一个形状。

examples.en: Diversification is the first rule taught to new investors.
examples.cn: 分散投资是教给新投资者的第一条规则。

examples.en: The region's diversification away from mining took a decade.
examples.cn: 该地区摆脱对矿业的依赖、走向多元化花了十年。

examples.en: Genetic diversification helps a species survive a new disease.
examples.cn: 遗传多样化帮助物种挺过新的疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「分成许多样」——把鸡蛋分到许多篮子里 → 分散投资、多样化

root: 由拉丁语 diversus「转向不同方向的、多样的」与 facere「制造」结合，经法语进入英语；名词后缀表示「使……的过程」，故字面义为「使多样」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general act of adding variety to its financial, business, regional, agricultural, economic and biological applications, and finally to the mixed state it produces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般的「增加多样」动作，转到金融、企业、地域、农业、经济与生物上的应用，最后落在它所产生的混合状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eggs from one basket distributed among many baskets heading in different directions.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子里的鸡蛋被分到许多只走向不同方向的篮子。

branches.en: GENERAL ACT: one kind is deliberately turned into many kinds.
branches.cn: 一般动作：一种被有意变成多种。

branches.en: INVESTMENT AND RESULT: money is spread across assets, and the portfolio ends up visibly mixed.
branches.cn: 投资与结果：资金分散到各种资产，组合最终呈现为可见的混合体。

branches.en: BUSINESS AND PLACE: a firm adds new lines and new regions so no single market decides its fate.
branches.cn: 企业与地点：公司增添新业务线与新地区，使单一市场无法决定其命运。

branches.en: FIELD AND STATE: crops and whole economies are diversified for the same hedge against one failure.
branches.cn: 田地与国家：作物与整个经济体为同样的「防单一失败」而对冲。

branches.en: NATURAL BRANCHING: evolution produces variety without a human planner.
branches.cn: 自然分枝：演化在没有人类规划者的情况下产生多样性。

intro.en: Diversification is built from Latin pieces that still work productively in English: a turning root, a making suffix and a process ending.
intro.cn: diversification 由仍在英语中能产的拉丁成分构成：一个「转」的词根、一个「制造」的后缀与一个表过程的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin vertere 'to turn' gives divert, convert and reverse; diversus adds the idea of turning apart, and facere supplies the making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vertere「转」衍生 divert、convert 与 reverse；diversus 增添「转向别处」的意思，facere 提供「制造」。

senses.title: The long wave of the tide
senses.definition: the very long wave by which the tide propagates into an ocean, sea or bay, with a wavelength of hundreds of kilometres
senses.definitionCN: 潮汐借以传入大洋、海或海湾的极长水波，波长可达数百公里
senses.example: The tide enters the bay as a slow tidal wave, not as a breaking wall.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水是以一道缓慢的潮汐波进入海湾的，并非一堵破碎的水墙。
senses.why: the tide is not a current but a wave so long that its crest may span an ocean; older oceanography called that wave a tidal wave before the term drifted.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐不是一股水流，而是一道长得波峰可横跨大洋的波；较早的海洋学就把这道波叫作 tidal wave，后来这个词才漂移。

senses.title: The bore in an estuary
senses.definition: the steep front of the advancing tide in a narrow estuary, seen as a single wall of water moving upstream
senses.definitionCN: 窄河口里推进的潮水形成的陡立波前，看上去是一道向上游移动的水墙
senses.example: At the head of the estuary the tidal wave stood like a wall of water.
senses.exampleCN: 在河口顶端，那道潮波像一堵水墙立了起来。
senses.why: in a narrowing channel the tide's front steepens until it becomes one breaking step, and that visible step is what people first named a tidal wave.
senses.whyCN: 在收窄的河道里，潮水的前缘越来越陡，直到变成一级破碎的台阶，人们最初就是用 tidal wave 指这道看得见的台阶。

senses.title: Any huge wave, loosely
senses.definition: in casual speech, any exceptionally large wave, whatever its cause
senses.definitionCN: 日常口语里指任何特别大的浪，不问成因
senses.example: A tidal wave lifted the dinghy onto the pier.
senses.exampleCN: 一道巨浪把小艇托上了码头。
senses.why: a casual speaker notices size before cause, so an overwhelming wave inherits the label even when no tide is involved.
senses.whyCN: 随口说话的人先注意到大小、后追问成因，因此哪怕与潮汐无关，压过来的大浪也会被安上这个名称。

senses.title: The misnomer for a tsunami
senses.definition: a popular but inaccurate name for a tsunami, the sea wave generated by an earthquake, landslide or volcanic collapse
senses.definitionCN: 对海啸的通俗而不准确的称呼；海啸由地震、滑坡或火山崩塌引起
senses.example: The headline called the earthquake's tsunami a tidal wave, though no tide was involved.
senses.exampleCN: 标题把那场地震引发的海啸称作「潮汐波」，尽管根本没有潮汐参与。
senses.why: the phrase already meant 'a great wave coming in from the sea', so news language kept it after seismology supplied the accurate Japanese-derived word tsunami.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语本来就有「从海上压来的巨浪」之意，因此海洋学给出准确的日源词 tsunami 之后，新闻语言仍沿用旧说法。

senses.title: A surge of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden, overwhelming rush of emotion that seems to sweep a person or group away
senses.definitionCN: 突然涌来、仿佛把人或群体卷走的情感
senses.example: A tidal wave of relief swept through the crowd when the doors opened.
senses.exampleCN: 门一开，一阵如释重负的浪潮扫过人群。
senses.why: an emotion that arrives all at once and cannot be resisted is pictured as water that overwhelms the shore, so the sea phrase becomes a feeling phrase.
senses.whyCN: 一下子涌来、无法抵挡的情绪，会被想象成淹没岸线的水，于是海的短语变成了情感的短语。

senses.title: A surge of people
senses.definition: a very large number of people arriving or moving together faster than the place can absorb them
senses.definitionCN: 大批人一起到来或移动，速度超过当地所能承受的程度
senses.example: A tidal wave of migration changed the town within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 一股移民洪流在一年之内改变了这座小镇。
senses.why: large movements of people are counted like water: one continuous mass arriving faster than the shore can take it.
senses.whyCN: 人口的大规模移动被当作水来计量：一整团连续不断的来者，快到岸来不及承接。

senses.title: A surge of messages or events
senses.titleCN: 投诉、消息等事件的洪流
senses.definition: a sudden mass of complaints, requests or news arriving at one time
senses.definitionCN: 投诉、请求或消息在同一时间大量涌来
senses.example: A tidal wave of complaints followed the new timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 新时刻表一公布，投诉便如潮水般涌来。
senses.why: the metaphor counts separate items as one mass, which is exactly how a flood of identical messages feels to the person receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把一件件分开的东西算作一整团，而这正是收件人面对成堆同样消息时的感受。

senses.title: A landslide in politics
senses.definition: a sweeping electoral victory that carries a party past its opponents everywhere at once
senses.definitionCN: 一举把对手在各处同时冲垮的选举大胜
senses.example: The opposition rode a tidal wave to a majority.
senses.exampleCN: 反对党乘着一股浪潮取得了多数席位。
senses.why: electoral language borrows the sea for swings that erase the previous map, and a wave that covers everything is the natural image for that.
senses.whyCN: 选举语言借用海洋来描写抹掉旧版图的摆荡，而一道覆盖一切的浪，正是这种事最自然的意象。

senses.title: A category in warnings and policies
senses.titleCN: 警报与保险条款中的类别名
senses.definition: used before another noun as a fixed category in hazard warnings, insurance exclusions and old emergency notices
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，在灾害警报、保险除外条款与旧式紧急通告中作固定类别名
senses.example: The policy excludes loss from tidal wave and earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单把潮浪与地震造成的损失列为除外责任。
senses.why: before another noun the phrase stops describing water and hardens into a category name that a warning or a contract can list.
senses.whyCN: 放在另一个名词之前时，短语不再描写水，而固化为一个可以被警报或合同逐条列出的类别名。

intro.en: Tidal wave joins two native Germanic words: tidal is tide plus -al, and wave descends from Old English wǣg 'billow'. The compound named the tide's own wave and the bore before newspapers extended it to tsunamis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tidal wave 由两个日耳曼本族词组成：tidal 是 tide 加 -al，wave 则出自古英语 wǣg「巨浪」。这个复合词先指潮汐自身的波与涌潮，后来报纸把它扩展到海啸。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wǣg meant a moving ridge of water, 'billow'; it is the noun that survives as wave and the base of the compound.
items.cn: wǣg 指水中移动的脊，即「巨浪」；它就是留存为 wave 的名词，也是这个复合词的基干。

items.en: Tidal was formed from tide and -al when tide tables needed an adjective for the phenomenon itself; the compound followed once the adjective was available.
items.cn: 潮汐表需要指现象本身的形容词时，tidal 由 tide 加 -al 构成；形容词一旦有了，复合短语随之出现。

items.en: Eighteenth- and nineteenth-century sailing and tide writing used tidal wave for the long wave of the tide and for the bore that runs up a river.
items.cn: 18 与 19 世纪的航海与潮汐写作中，tidal wave 指潮汐的长波，也指逆流而上的涌潮。

items.en: From the nineteenth century, and above all in twentieth-century newspapers, the phrase was attached to seismic sea waves; seismologists objected and adopted tsunami, from Japanese tsu 'harbour' plus nami 'wave'.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，尤其到 20 世纪的报纸上，这个短语被安到地震海啸上；地震学家反对这一用法，转而采用源自日语「津波」（港湾之浪）的 tsunami。

items.en: In the twentieth century the phrase also became a standard metaphor for surges of feeling, people, complaints and votes, where nothing watery is involved.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个短语又成为情感、人群、投诉与选票等涌动的标准比喻，与真正的水已毫无关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (root relation and dates): whether Old English wǣg and the verb wafian descend from one root is disputed, and the exact date when tidal wave was first applied to tsunamis is not fixed; *wēgaz is a reconstructed Germanic form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根关系与年代）：古英语 wǣg 与动词 wafian 是否同出一根有争议；tidal wave 首次用于海啸的确切年代也没有定论；*wēgaz 是重构的日耳曼形式。

note.en: Group one holds the phrase's own parts, one derivative of its head, and a sound-alike with a different root; group two holds the precise terms that the phrase is often confused with.
note.cn: 第一组是本短语自身的构件、其中心词的一个派生词，以及一个词根不同的同音形近词；第二组是常与本短语混淆的精确术语。

entries.definition: the adjective alone means 'of the tide'; it does not name a wave and cannot stand for the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词单独用时意为「潮汐的」，不指任何波浪，也不能代替整个短语。

entries.definition: the head noun alone covers sea waves, hand gestures and physical waves; only the modifier narrows it to the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 中心名词单独使用时涵盖海浪、挥手与物理波；只有加上修饰语才收窄到潮汐。

entries.definition: wave plus -y, 'having waves in its shape'; it describes hair or lines, never a body of water in motion.
entries.definitionCN: wave 加 -y，意为「呈波浪形的」；它描写头发或线条，从不指运动中的水体。

entries.definition: from Old French weyver 'to abandon', of Scandinavian origin; it sounds exactly like wave but means to give up a right or fee.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 weyver「放弃」，源头在斯堪的纳维亚语；它与 wave 同音，却意为放弃权利或费用。

entries.definition: a sea wave generated by a sea-floor earthquake, landslide or eruption, able to cross an ocean; the correct word where tidal wave is a misnomer.
entries.definitionCN: 由海底地震、滑坡或喷发引起的海浪，可跨越整个大洋；在 tidal wave 属误用之处，它才是正确词。

entries.definition: the steep front of the tide running up a narrow estuary; it is what the original tidal wave often meant, named more exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 潮水在窄河口逆流而上形成的陡立波前；它常是 tidal wave 原义所指，是更精确的名称。

entries.definition: a rise of sea level pushed ashore by storm winds; it is a raised water surface, not a travelling wave.
entries.definitionCN: 风暴风把海水堆向岸边造成的水位上涨；它是被抬高的水面，不是行进中的波。

entries.definition: an exceptionally large single wave arising from the overlap of wave trains; it has no link to tides or earthquakes.
entries.definitionCN: 由多列波叠加而偶然出现的异常单个大浪；与潮汐或地震都无关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two parts: tidal 'of the tide' plus wave 'billow'; the compound first meant the tide's own long wave.
normal.cn: 两个构件：tidal「潮汐的」加 wave「巨浪」；复合词最初指潮汐自身的长波。

normal.en: The family runs tide, tidal, wave, wavy, wavelength, microwave.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tide、tidal、wave、wavy、wavelength、microwave。

normal.en: The precise term for the estuarine version is tidal bore; the precise term for the seismic version is tsunami.
normal.cn: 河口那一种的精确说法是 tidal bore；地震那一种的精确说法是 tsunami。

normal.en: Seismologists reject tidal wave because tides have nothing to do with earthquakes.
normal.cn: 地震学家不接受 tidal wave 这一说法，因为潮汐与地震毫无关系。

normal.en: The figurative use is countable in phrases: a tidal wave of relief, of complaints, of migration.
normal.cn: 比喻用法在短语中可数：一阵如释重负、一阵投诉、一股移民潮。

abstract.en: Picture a wave so long that its crest passes your boat for half an hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一道浪长到波峰从你的船边经过要半个小时。

abstract.en: Picture a river running backwards with a white line across its width.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河倒流，河面上横着一条白线。

abstract.en: Picture a headline that uses a sea word for something that happened underground.
abstract.cn: 想象一个标题，用海的词去说一件发生在地下的事。

examples.en: A tidal wave of praise greeted the young pianist.
examples.cn: 一片赞誉的浪潮迎接这位年轻钢琴家。

examples.en: Scientists avoid the term tidal wave because it confuses tides with seismic sea waves.
examples.cn: 科学家避免使用 tidal wave 这一说法，因为它把潮汐与地震海啸混为一谈。

examples.en: The bore is the visible tidal wave of a narrow estuary.
examples.cn: 涌潮就是窄河口里看得见的那道潮波。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「潮」加「浪」——潮水推上来的那道浪，像一堵水墙 → 潮汐波、涌潮（也常被误用来指海啸）

root: tidal（古英语 tīd「时间」+ -al）+ wave（古英语 wǣg「巨浪」，日耳曼语重构 *wēgaz）；18—19 世纪航海写作中固定为「潮汐波、涌潮」，19 世纪起被报纸误用于海啸；wave 另有动词来源古英语 wafian「挥动」，两源在现代英语合流。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses trace one phrase as it loosens: the tide's own long wave, its steep front in an estuary, any great wave in casual speech, the newspaper misnomer for a tsunami, and then the figurative surges of feeling, people, messages, votes and finally the category name in warnings and contracts.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项顺着同一个短语的松动过程展开：潮汐自身的长波、它在河口的陡立波前、口语里任何巨浪、报纸对海啸的误称，随后是情感、人群、消息、选票等比喻性涌动，最后是警报与合同里的类别名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall of water pushing upstream against the current, raising the whole surface behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堵水墙逆流向上游推进，把身后整个水面抬高。

branches.en: SEA WATER MOVING: the long wave of the tide, then its steep visible front in a narrow channel.
branches.cn: 海水在动：先是潮汐的长波，然后是它在窄河道里陡立的可见前缘。

branches.en: THE NAME LOOSENED: any great wave takes the label, and news keeps it for the seismic sea wave.
branches.cn: 名称松脱：任何巨浪都戴上这个标签，新闻又把它留给地震海啸。

branches.en: INWARD AND OUTWARD SURGE: feeling and messages arrive as one unresisting mass.
branches.cn: 向内与向外的涌动：情感与消息都作为一整团无法抵挡的东西到来。

branches.en: CROWDS AND VOTES: people and majorities move like water and erase the old shoreline.
branches.cn: 人群与选票：人与多数像水一样移动，抹掉旧日的岸线。

branches.en: IN CONTRACTS AND WARNINGS: the phrase hardens into a category that can be listed and excluded.
branches.cn: 在合同与警报里：短语固化为一个可以被列出、被排除的类别。

intro.en: Both halves of this phrase are native Germanic words, so the analysis is about compounds and suffixes rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两半都是日耳曼本族词，因此分析的是复合与后缀，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin cognate for either part: tide goes back to *tīdiz and wave to *wēgaz. Latin unda 'wave' is a different word altogether, which is why undulate is not a relative of wave, and the Latin entries stay empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都没有拉丁同族词：tide 上溯到 *tīdiz，wave 上溯到 *wēgaz。拉丁 unda「波浪」完全是另一个词，因此由它派生的英语词并非 wave 的同族，拉丁条目按实情留空。

items.example: The tide came at its appointed hour.
items.exampleCN: 潮水在约定的时辰到来。

items.example: The same suffix builds tidal from tide.
items.exampleCN: 同一个后缀把 tide 构成 tidal。

items.example: Tidal water fills the creek twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 潮水一天两次灌满这条小溪。

items.example: Old English wǣg named the billow that breaks on the shore.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 wǣg 指拍碎在岸上的巨浪。

items.structure: Old English wafian (verb, 'to move to and fro')
items.meaning: to wave the hand or an object
items.example: Old English wafian meant to move the hand to and fro.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 wafian 意为把手来回挥动。

items.meaning: a sea wave; to move the hand
items.example: She waved from the pier.
items.exampleCN: 她在码头上挥手。

items.example: The wavy line shows the tide's rise.
items.exampleCN: 这条波浪形的线显示潮水的上涨。

items.example: A tide's wavelength is measured in hundreds of kilometres.
items.exampleCN: 潮汐的波长以数百公里计。

items.meaning: the tide's long wave; loosely a tsunami
items.example: The old chart marks the tidal wave's arrival.
items.exampleCN: 旧海图上标着潮汐波的到达时刻。

definition_zh: 沉积；沉积物；宣誓证词；罢免
definition_en: the laying down of material; the material laid down; sworn testimony; or removal from power
core_image: 河水放慢，沙粒一层层落在河底
scene: 春天河湾水流变缓，细沙一层层落下来： The deposition of fine silt each spring keeps the delta fertile.
sceneCN: 这里 deposition 是「沉积作用」（第 1 个义项：物质被放下并堆积）；句意：每年春天细淤泥的沉积让三角洲保持肥沃。图中可辨识物件：河湾、缓流、沉降的细沙、层层叠起的河岸剖面。

pos.zh: 沉积；沉积物；宣誓证词；罢免

senses.title: Sediment laid down by water or wind
senses.titleCN: 沉积作用：颗粒一层层落下来
senses.definition: the geological process by which loose material settles out of water, wind or ice
senses.definitionCN: 松散物质从水、风或冰中沉降并堆积的地质过程
senses.example: Deposition of sand at the river mouth slowly built a new bar.
senses.exampleCN: 河口处的沙子沉积，慢慢堆出一道新沙洲。
senses.why: deponere means 'to put down'. When a current loses energy it puts its load down, so deposition is literally the putting-down of particles.
senses.whyCN: deponere 意为“放下”。水流失去能量时就把负载放下，因此沉积字面上就是颗粒被放下。

senses.title: The material that has settled
senses.titleCN: 沉积物：落下来的那一层
senses.definition: the layer or body of material produced by deposition
senses.definitionCN: 由沉积作用产生的那一层或那一堆物质
senses.example: The cliff exposes a thick deposition of volcanic ash.
senses.exampleCN: 崖壁露出厚厚一层火山灰沉积。
senses.why: The -ion noun can name either the act or its result. Once the particles are down, the same word points to the layer they form.
senses.whyCN: -ion 名词既可指动作，也可指结果。颗粒一旦落下，同一个词就指向它们形成的那一层。

senses.title: Sworn testimony taken out of court
senses.titleCN: 宣誓证词：法庭外的正式口供
senses.definition: a formal statement made under oath before a court officer, usually before trial
senses.definitionCN: 在法院官员面前宣誓作出的正式陈述，通常在开庭前进行
senses.example: The witness gave a deposition that contradicted her earlier statement.
senses.exampleCN: 证人作出的宣誓证词与她早先的说法相矛盾。
senses.why: Legal language borrowed deponere in the sense 'to set down in writing or on record'. A deposition is testimony put down so it cannot be changed later.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言借用了 deponere 的“记录下来”义。证词被“放下”固定住，日后就不能更改。

senses.title: Removal from office
senses.titleCN: 罢免：把掌权者从位子上拿下
senses.definition: the removal of a ruler, bishop or official from power
senses.definitionCN: 把统治者、主教或官员从权力位置上撤下
senses.example: The deposition of the king led to a decade of civil war.
senses.exampleCN: 国王被罢黜引发了一场十年内战。
senses.why: To depose is to put someone down from a seat. The noun keeps that physical picture: the person is lowered out of the position they occupied.
senses.whyCN: depose 就是把某人从位子上拿下。名词保留了这一物理画面：人被从所占据的位置上放下来。

senses.title: Thin films formed from vapour
senses.titleCN: 气相沉积：原子落到基片上
senses.definition: a manufacturing process in which a vapour condenses onto a surface to form a thin film
senses.definitionCN: 蒸气在表面凝结形成薄膜的制造工艺
senses.example: Chemical vapour deposition coats the tools with a hard layer.
senses.exampleCN: 化学气相沉积在刀具上覆上一层硬膜。
senses.why: The industrial sense is the geological sense at atomic scale: particles arrive and settle on a surface, building a layer.
senses.whyCN: 工业义就是地质义在原子尺度上的版本：粒子到达并落在表面，堆成一层。

senses.title: Metal laid down by current
senses.titleCN: 电沉积：金属离子在电极上落户
senses.definition: the electrochemical process in which dissolved metal ions form a solid coating on an electrode
senses.definitionCN: 溶解的金属离子在电极上形成固体镀层的电化学过程
senses.example: Electrodeposition of copper filled the narrow trenches on the chip.
senses.exampleCN: 铜的电沉积填满了芯片上的窄沟槽。
senses.why: Here the particles are ions driven to a surface by current. The word still means 'put down', only the force moving them has changed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的颗粒是被电流驱赶到表面的离子。词义仍是“放下”，只是推动它们的力变了。

senses.title: Pollutants settling on surfaces
senses.titleCN: 污染物沉降：脏东西从空中落下来
senses.definition: the transfer of airborne pollutants onto land, water or buildings
senses.definitionCN: 空气中的污染物转移到土地、水体或建筑物上的过程
senses.example: Nitrogen deposition from nearby farms changed the meadow's plant life.
senses.exampleCN: 附近农场带来的氮沉降改变了草甸的植物群落。
senses.why: Environmental science applies the old word to particles and gases leaving the air. What falls is no longer sand, but the motion is the same.
senses.whyCN: 环境科学把这个旧词用于离开空气的颗粒和气体。落下之物不再是沙子，但运动方式相同。

senses.title: The act of placing something down
senses.definition: the act of laying or placing an object somewhere, often in a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放置在某处的动作，常用于仪式场合
senses.example: The deposition of wreaths at the memorial takes place at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 纪念仪式上的花圈安放于黎明时进行。
senses.why: This sense stays closest to deponere: an object is put down at a chosen place. Ceremonial use preserves the literal gesture beneath all the technical senses.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项最贴近 deponere：物件被放到选定之处。仪式用法在所有技术义之下保留了字面动作。

intro.en: Deposition goes back to Latin depositio, from deponere 'to put down', itself de- 'down' plus ponere 'to place'. The geological, legal and political senses all preserve that basic downward placement.
intro.cn: deposition 可追到拉丁 depositio，来自 deponere“放下”，由 de-“向下”和 ponere“放置”构成。地质、法律与政治义都保留了“向下放置”这一基本动作。

items.en: ponere meant 'to put, place, set'. It is the source of position, positive, compose, expose and deposit, so the whole family is about placement.
items.cn: ponere 意为“放、安置、摆”。它是 position、positive、compose、expose、deposit 的来源，因此整个词族都围绕“放置”。

items.en: deponere adds de- 'down', giving 'to put down, lay aside, store'. Latin used it for laying down a burden as well as for depositing money or testimony.
items.cn: deponere 加 de-“向下”，意为“放下、搁置、存放”。拉丁语既用它表示放下重担，也表示存放钱款或证词。

items.en: The noun depositio names the act of putting down and, by extension, what has been put down. English takes the stem deposit- and adds -ion.
items.cn: 名词 depositio 命名“放下”的动作，并引申指被放下之物。英语取 deposit- 词干加 -ion。

items.en: From the idea of putting something on record comes the legal deposition: testimony set down under oath. The exact date of this extension is uncertain.
items.cn: 从“记录在案”的观念产生了法律上的 deposition：宣誓后记录下来的证词。这一引申的确切年代存疑。

items.en: Deposing a ruler is putting him down from a seat of power. The political noun appears in medieval and early modern English, again from deponere.
items.cn: 罢黜统治者就是把他从权力座位上拿下。这一政治名词出现于中世纪和近代早期英语，同样来自 deponere。

items.en: Geology adopted deposition for settling sediment in the 18th and 19th centuries; materials science later applied it to thin films. The physical image needed no change.
items.cn: 地质学在 18 至 19 世纪采用 deposition 表示沉积物沉降；材料科学后来把它用于薄膜。物理意象无需改变。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on deposit- with different endings; the near-meaning group separates the kinds of settling, recording and removal the word can name.
note.cn: 形近组由 deposit- 加不同词尾构成；近义组区分这个词所能命名的几种沉降、记录与撤职。

entries.definition: to put money or material somewhere; the material or money put down. It is the everyday member of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 存放钱或物质；被放下的物质或钱款。它是这个词族的日常成员。

entries.definition: relating to deposition, especially in geology. The -al suffix turns the process noun into an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 与沉积有关的，尤用于地质学。-al 把过程名词变成形容词。

entries.definition: to remove from office, or to testify under oath. It is the verb behind the political and legal senses.
entries.definitionCN: 罢免；宣誓作证。它是政治义与法律义背后的动词。

entries.definition: the process by which sediment settles; it overlaps with geological deposition but focuses on the settling of solids in a fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 沉积物沉降的过程；它与地质沉积重叠，但聚焦于固体在流体中的沉降。

entries.definition: a formal statement of evidence, usually in court; a deposition is one specific kind taken before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的证据陈述，通常在法庭上；deposition 是开庭前取得的特定一种。

entries.definition: the removal of a monarch from the throne; narrower than deposition, which also covers bishops and officials.
entries.definitionCN: 把君主从王座上撤下；比 deposition 窄，后者也涵盖主教与官员。

entries.definition: the gradual gathering of material; it stresses the growing pile rather than the act of laying each particle down.
entries.definitionCN: 物质的逐渐堆积；它强调堆头越来越大，而不是每颗粒被放下的动作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down' + ponere 'place': deposition is a placing down, whether sand, testimony or a crown.
normal.cn: de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”：deposition 就是放下——无论放的是沙、证词还是王冠。

normal.en: deposit, position, compose and expose all share ponere, so the family is a set of placements.
normal.cn: deposit、position、compose、expose 都共享 ponere，整个词族就是一组“放置”。

normal.en: The legal phrase is 'give a deposition', not 'make': the witness hands the record over.
normal.cn: 法律搭配是 give a deposition，而不是 make：证人把记录交出去。

normal.en: In geology, look for the pair deposition and erosion: one builds layers, the other removes them.
normal.cn: 地质学里记住 deposition 与 erosion 这对词：一个铺层，一个剥层。

normal.en: Vapour deposition is the same word at atomic scale: atoms settle on a surface just as sand settles on a riverbed.
normal.cn: 气相沉积是同一个词在原子尺度上：原子落在表面，正如沙落在河床。

abstract.en: Think of a hand opening and letting a fistful of sand fall onto a table in slow motion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手张开，让一把沙以慢镜头落到桌面上。

abstract.en: Think of dust forming a grey film on a windowsill over weeks of stillness.
abstract.cn: 想象几周无人打扰，灰尘在窗台上积成一层灰膜。

abstract.en: Think of a crown being lifted from a head and set down on a table: that downward move is the political sense.
abstract.cn: 想象王冠被从头上升起，再放到桌上：这个向下的动作就是政治义。

examples.en: Wind deposition created the long dunes along the coast.
examples.cn: 风的沉积作用在海岸边造出了长长的沙丘。

examples.en: The lawyer scheduled a deposition for the following Tuesday.
examples.cn: 律师把宣誓证词安排在下一个星期二。

examples.en: The deposition of the bishop was ordered by the council.
examples.cn: 主教被议会下令罢免。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地破zition”——地（de）上破（po）碎的沙一点点sit（沉积）下来 → deposition 沉积、证词

root: 拉丁 deponere“放下、存放”（de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”）；deposit- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one downward movement: something is taken from where it was and set down somewhere else, to stay.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个向下动作：某物从原处被取下，放到别处并留在那里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a current slowing and letting its load fall to the bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：水流放慢，让负载落到水底。

branches.en: PROCESS AND RESULT: laying particles down and the layer that results are the same event seen while happening and afterwards.
branches.cn: 过程与结果：把颗粒放下与由此形成的层，是同一事件在发生中与发生后的两种看法。

branches.en: REMOVAL: a ruler or bishop set down from a position of power.
branches.cn: 罢免：把统治者或主教从权力位置上撤下。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL LAYERS: vapour and electrodeposition build films atom by atom, the geological gesture repeated in a factory.
branches.cn: 工业镀层：气相沉积与电沉积逐原子造膜，是地质动作在工厂里的重复。

branches.en: ENVIRONMENT AND CEREMONY: pollutants falling on land and wreaths laid at a memorial both end with something resting where it was placed.
branches.cn: 环境与仪式：污染物落到土地上、花圈安放在纪念碑前，最终都是某物停在它被放下之处。

branches.en: THE LEGAL CORE: the deposition under oath is the most institutionalised form of 'putting something down so it cannot move'.
branches.cn: 法律核心：宣誓证词是“把东西放下、使其不能移动”最制度化的形式。

intro.en: Deposition is deposit plus -ion. The Latin parts de- and ponere are fused inside the base; English freely adds -ion, -al, -or and -ory to build the family.
intro.cn: deposition 是 deposit 加 -ion。拉丁成分 de- 与 ponere 已融合在词基内；英语可自由加 -ion、-al、-or、-ory 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ponere 'to place' yields deponere 'put down', depositio 'a laying down', and depositum 'something deposited'. English relatives include deposit, position, compose, expose and postpone.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ponere“放置”派生 deponere“放下”、depositio“放下”、depositum“存放物”。英语同族词包括 deposit、position、compose、expose、postpone。

items.meaning: to put down; material or money put down
items.meaningCN: 存放；沉积；存款（de-“向下”+ ponere“放置”）
items.example: The river deposits silt along its lower course.
items.exampleCN: 这条河在下游沿线沉积淤泥。

items.meaning: the act of laying down, or what is laid down
items.meaningCN: 沉积；沉积物（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The deposition of ash buried the old road.
items.exampleCN: 火山灰的沉积掩埋了旧路。

items.meaningCN: 沉积的；与沉积有关的（-al 构成关系形容词）
items.example: The rock shows clear depositional layers.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石显示出清晰的沉积层。

items.meaning: a person who deposits money or material
items.meaningCN: 存款人；沉积者（-or 构成施事者名词）
items.example: Each depositor received a receipt.
items.exampleCN: 每位存款人都拿到了一张收据。

items.meaning: a place where things are stored
items.meaningCN: 存放处；储藏所（-ory 构成处所名词）
items.example: The documents are kept in a secure depository.
items.exampleCN: 这些文件存放在一个安全的储藏所。

items.meaning: to remove from office; to testify
items.meaningCN: 罢免；宣誓作证（由“拿下”引申）
items.example: The council moved to depose the mayor.
items.exampleCN: 议会着手罢免市长。

items.meaning: to deposit again; to lay down a second time
items.meaningCN: 再次沉积；重新存放（re-“再次”+ deposit）
items.example: The eroded sand was redeposited further downstream.
items.exampleCN: 被侵蚀的沙子在下游更远处再次沉积。

items.meaning: a second laying down of material
items.meaningCN: 再次沉积；再沉积作用（re- + deposition）
items.example: Redeposition thickened the layer near the bend.
items.exampleCN: 再沉积使弯道附近的层变厚。

latinEntries.meaning: to put down; to lay aside; to store

definition_en: a row of columns supporting a roof or standing as a long line
core_image: 一排石柱撑起长廊，柱影整齐地落在地上
scene: 一排石柱撑起长廊，行人走在阴影里。 A long colonnade shaded the walkers from the sun.

senses.title: A row of columns
senses.definition: a long line of columns standing together
senses.definitionCN: 并排而立的一长列柱子
senses.example: The temple is fronted by a colonnade.

senses.title: A roofed walk along columns

senses.example: Shoppers strolled under the colonnade.

senses.why: A row of columns became a place to walk.

normal.en: Columns stand shoulder to shoulder.

abstract.en: Rhythm made of pillars.

definition_zh: 君主；国王或女王；世袭的国家元首；帝王蛱蝶；某个领域里的霸主；某一方天地中最宏大者
definition_en: a sole hereditary ruler such as a king or queen; also a large migratory butterfly and, figuratively, a dominant person or thing
core_image: 一顶王冠落在唯一的座位上，两侧的座椅都空着
scene: 礼仪厅里只有一张高背椅，椅背刻着王冠，两侧的座位都空着。 The monarch opened the session with a short address from the throne.
sceneCN: 这里 monarch 指「唯一的世袭君主」（第 1 个义项：由一人继承国家元首之位）；句意为君主在御座上为会议作简短开幕致辞。可辨识物件：高背椅、王冠、空座位、御座、礼袍。

pos.zh: 君主；国王；女王；帝王蛱蝶；霸主

derivatives.zh: monarch + -y（经拉丁 -ia、希腊 -ia 的状态后缀）→ 君主制，语义由人转为制度
monarch + -ic（希腊 -ikos、拉丁 -icus 形容词后缀）→ 君主的、君主制的
monarch + -ical（形容词后缀变体）→ 君主制的，与 monarchic 近义
monarch + -ism（主义后缀）→ 君主主义，主张保留君主制
monarch + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 君主主义者；拥护君主制的
monarch + -ess（阴性后缀）→ 女君主（较少用）

senses.title: A sole hereditary ruler
senses.definition: a king, queen or emperor who holds office by inheritance and stands alone at the head of the state
senses.definitionCN: 凭继承取得职位、独自居于国家顶端的国王、女王或皇帝
senses.example: The monarch opened the session with a short address from the throne.
senses.exampleCN: 君主在御座上为会议作了简短开幕致辞。
senses.why: Greek monarkhes joined monos 'alone' to arkhein 'rule', so the word begins with the idea of one person ruling.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 monarkhes 把 monos「单独」与 arkhein「统治」结合，词的核心从一开始就是「一人统治」。

senses.title: A constitutional king or queen
senses.titleCN: 立宪制下的国王或女王
senses.definition: a hereditary head of state whose powers are limited by a constitution and exercised through ministers
senses.definitionCN: 世袭的国家元首，其权力受宪法限制、由大臣行使
senses.example: In a constitutional system the monarch reigns but does not rule.
senses.exampleCN: 在立宪制度下，君主在位而不亲政。
senses.why: The title survived even when real power moved to parliament, so monarch now often means a ceremonial sovereign.
senses.whyCN: 即使实权移入议会，称号仍保留，因此 monarch 如今常指礼仪性的元首。

senses.title: An absolute ruler
senses.definition: a ruler who makes law and raises revenue without a representative body
senses.definitionCN: 不经代议机构便立法与征税的统治者
senses.example: The monarch could raise taxes without consulting a council.
senses.exampleCN: 这位君主无需咨询议事会便可加税。
senses.why: The original sense had no constitutional limit, and that older reading survives when historians discuss absolute rule.
senses.whyCN: 原义并无宪法限制，史家讨论专制统治时保留的正是这一较早读法。

senses.title: A migratory orange butterfly
senses.titleCN: 橙色的迁徙性帝王蛱蝶
senses.definition: a large orange-and-black butterfly, Danaus plexippus, famous for its long annual migration
senses.definitionCN: 橙黑相间的大型蛱蝶，以每年长距离迁徙著称
senses.example: A monarch drifted south along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一只帝王蛱蝶沿着海岸向南飘飞。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century naturalists called the most impressive local butterfly a monarch, borrowing the title of the grandest ruler.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪博物学者把当地最引人注目的蛱蝶称作君主，借用了最高统治者的称号。

senses.title: A dominant figure in a field
senses.definition: a person who dominates an activity or industry as though by royal authority
senses.definitionCN: 像凭王权般支配某项活动或行业的人
senses.example: She was the monarch of the city's concert halls.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这座城市音乐厅的霸主。
senses.why: The metaphor moves sole rule from a state to a social sphere, where one person sets the tone for everyone.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把「一人统治」从国家移到社会领域，一个人便为所有人定调。

senses.title: The ruler of a small state
senses.definition: a ruler of a small kingdom or princely state, especially in historical accounts
senses.definitionCN: 小王国或土邦的统治者，尤见于历史记述
senses.example: The monarch of the island state kept his own coinage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个岛国的君主保有自己的铸币权。
senses.why: Scale does not change the title: a ruler who holds sole hereditary power is a monarch whatever the size of the map.
senses.whyCN: 规模不改变称号：只要独自掌握世袭权力，无论地图多小都是君主。

senses.title: A magnate compared to a king
senses.definition: a wealthy or powerful magnate described as ruling an industry like a king
senses.definitionCN: 被形容为像国王一样统治某个行业的富有或有权势者
senses.example: The railway monarch travelled in a private carriage.
senses.exampleCN: 这位铁路巨头乘坐私人车厢出行。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century newspapers nicknamed industry barons 'monarchs' because their decisions moved whole regions.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪报纸把产业大亨戏称为「君主」，因为他们的决定能牵动整片地区。

senses.title: The grandest thing of its kind
senses.definition: the largest or most impressive example of a natural kind, imagined as ruling over the rest
senses.definitionCN: 某一自然类别中最大或最壮观的个体，被想象为统辖其余
senses.example: The old oak was called the monarch of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 那棵老橡树被称为林中之王。
senses.why: The same habit that names the biggest butterfly also crowns the biggest tree, so monarch can mean simply the grandest member.
senses.whyCN: 给最大蛱蝶命名的习惯也把最大的树加冕，因此 monarch 可仅指最宏大的那一个。

intro.en: Monarch comes through Latin and French from Greek monarkhes 'sole ruler', built on monos 'alone' and arkhein 'to rule'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monarch 经拉丁与法语来自希腊 monarkhes「唯一统治者」，由 monos「单独」与 arkhein「统治」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'; it is the same element found in monologue and monopoly.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独、唯一」，与 monologue、monopoly 中的成分相同。

items.en: Arkhein meant 'to begin, to rule'; its noun arkhe could mean both a starting point and an office of rule.
items.cn: arkhein 意为「开始、统治」；其名词 arkhe 既可指起点，也可指统治职位。

items.en: Monos plus arkhein produced monarkhes, 'one who rules alone', the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: monos 加 arkhein 构成 monarkhes「独自统治的人」，是英语该词的直接来源。

items.en: Latin monarcha kept the Greek meaning and passed it to French monarque and then to English.
items.cn: 拉丁 monarcha 保留了希腊含义，传给法语 monarque，再进入英语。

items.en: The butterfly name is a nineteenth-century naturalist borrowing, and the magnate and 'grandest tree' uses are journalistic extensions of the same image.
items.cn: 蝴蝶名是十九世纪博物学者的借用，巨头义与「林中最高大的树」义都是同一意象的报刊引申。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first use of monarch for the butterfly is not established, and the naming motive, whether royal colour or size, is a matter of conjecture.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：monarch 用于该蛱蝶的最早记录未有定论，命名动机是王室色彩还是体型，也属推测。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same Greek pair or accidental neighbours; group two holds words for a sole ruler.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊组合或偶然相邻的形式；第二组是表示唯一统治者的词。

entries.definition: The system or state of rule by one monarch, from Greek monarkhia; monarch is the person.
entries.definitionCN: 由一位君主统治的制度或国家，出自希腊 monarkhia；monarch 指人。

entries.definition: The relational adjective 'of a monarch or monarchy'.
entries.definitionCN: 「君主的、君主制的」关系形容词。

entries.definition: From Greek monazein 'to live alone', but with no arkhein element: a community of monks, not a ruler.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊 monazein「独居」，但无 arkhein 成分：是僧侣团体，不是统治者。

entries.definition: From hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein: rule by priests, later any ranked order. It shares the second element only.
entries.definitionCN: 由 hieros「神圣」加 arkhein 构成：最初指祭司统治，后指任何等级秩序。只共享第二个成分。

entries.definition: The male ruler of a kingdom; a specific rank, while monarch is the general category.
entries.definitionCN: 王国的男性统治者；是具体等级，而 monarch 是总类。

entries.definition: A ruler or state with supreme legal power; it stresses authority rather than heredity.
entries.definitionCN: 握有最高法律权力的统治者或国家；强调权威而非世袭。

entries.definition: The ruler of an empire, traditionally ranked above a king; an emperor is a kind of monarch.
entries.definitionCN: 帝国的统治者，传统等级高于国王；皇帝是君主的一种。

entries.definition: Anyone who governs, elected or not; the neutral word that need not imply a crown.
entries.definitionCN: 任何治理者，无论是否经选举；是不必含王冠的中性词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'alone' + arkhein 'rule': one person rules.
normal.cn: monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」：一个人统治。

normal.en: The family runs monarch, monarchy, monarchic, monarchical, monarchist, monarchism.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monarch、monarchy、monarchic、monarchical、monarchist、monarchism。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: constitutional monarch, absolute monarch, reigning monarch.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：立宪君主、专制君主、在位君主。

normal.en: The butterfly keeps the grand title, and so does the biggest tree in the wood.
normal.cn: 蝴蝶保留了这个宏大称号，林中最大的树也一样。

normal.en: monastery also starts with monos but has no arkhein, so it is not a relative.
normal.cn: monastery 也以 monos 开头，却没有 arkhein，因此并非同族词。

abstract.en: Picture one chair in a hall full of empty chairs.
abstract.cn: 想象一间满是空椅的大厅里只坐着一张椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a butterfly carrying a tiny crown across a whole continent.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蝴蝶戴着小小的王冠飞越整块大陆。

abstract.en: Picture an old tree that the village treats as its ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵老树，被全村当作君主。

examples.en: The monarch and the parliament disagreed over the new tax.
examples.cn: 君主与议会就新税发生分歧。

examples.en: Monarchs migrate thousands of kilometres every autumn.
examples.cn: 帝王蛱蝶每年秋天迁徙数千公里。

examples.en: In the trade, he was treated as a monarch whose word settled prices.
examples.cn: 在这一行里，他被当作一句话就能定下价格的君主。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono」单一 + 「arch」统治——一个人统治全场 → 君主

root: 希腊 monarkhes「唯一统治者」= monos「单独」+ arkhein「统治」；经拉丁 monarcha、法语 monarque 入英语。英语 monarch。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on one seat: a single ruler, whether crowned by a constitution, by absolute power, by a magnate's fortune, or only by being the grandest thing in the wood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都落在同一个座位上：唯一的统治者，无论是宪法所加冕、绝对权力所加冕、巨富所加冕，还是只因为它是林中最大者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one throne in a hall of empty chairs.
core.cn: 核心意象：满是空椅的大厅里只有一张御座。

branches.en: THE SEAT: one person holds the office by inheritance.
branches.cn: 座位：一人凭继承占据职位。

branches.en: TWO LIMITS: the same title covers a ceremonial sovereign and an unlimited autocrat.
branches.cn: 两种界限：同一称号既指礼仪元首，也指不受限的专制者。

branches.en: SMALL MAP: size does not change the title of a sole hereditary ruler.
branches.cn: 小地图：领土大小不改变唯一世袭统治者的称号。

branches.en: BORROWED GRANDEUR: a magnate, a butterfly or a great tree is crowned by metaphor.
branches.cn: 借来的宏大：巨头、蝴蝶或大树都被比喻加冕。

branches.en: THE CREATURE: the most striking local butterfly takes the grandest name.
branches.cn: 生物：当地最引人注目的蛱蝶取用了最宏大的名字。

intro.en: Monarch is a two-morpheme Greek compound, and both halves recur in English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: monarch 是双语素的希腊复合词，两半都在英语词中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek monos and arkhein give monarch, monarchy and monarchic; Latin monarcha and monarchia carried the forms westward.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 monos 与 arkhein 衍生 monarch、monarchy 与 monarchic；拉丁 monarcha 与 monarchia 把这些形式向西传。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根把统治与「领头」联系起来。

items.example: A monarkhes held the office by birth.
items.exampleCN: 唯一统治者凭出生取得职位。

items.example: The suffix turns the ruler into the system of rule.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把统治者转为统治制度。

items.example: The monarch opened the session.
items.exampleCN: 君主为会议开幕。

items.example: The monarchy survived two republics.
items.exampleCN: 这个君主国挺过了两个共和国时期。

items.example: The suffix built monarchic from monarch.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 monarch 构成 monarchic。

items.example: The monarchic title passed to the eldest son.
items.exampleCN: 君主称号传给了长子。

items.example: The monarchist opposed the referendum.
items.exampleCN: 这位君主主义者反对公投。

items.example: The monastery stood above the valley.
items.exampleCN: 僧院坐落在山谷之上。
