definition_zh: 土地利用；土地用途
definition_en: the way land is used, or the purpose for which a piece of land is managed
core_image: 一块地被划成不同颜色的区块，分别代表耕作、居住与林地
scene: 谷地被分成数块，颜色分别代表耕作、居住与保留林地。 The county maps land use every ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 land use 指「土地被派作何种用途」（第 1 个义项：一块地用于耕作、居住、工业或保留等的目的）；句意为该县每十年绘制一次土地利用图。图中可辨识物件：彩色地块、分界线、田块、林地。

pos.zh: 土地利用；土地用途（可数或不可数）

senses.title: The purpose land is put to
senses.definition: the function a piece of land serves, such as farming, housing, industry or conservation
senses.definitionCN: 一块地所承担的功能，如耕作、居住、工业或保护
senses.example: The county maps land use every ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该县每十年绘制一次土地利用图。
senses.why: land names the surface and use names its employment, so the compound simply asks what the ground is employed for.
senses.whyCN: land 指地表，use 指它的用途，因此这个复合词就是问这块地在被用来做什么。

senses.title: The pattern across a region
senses.definition: the arrangement of different purposes across a whole area
senses.definitionCN: 整个区域内不同用途的分布安排
senses.example: The valley's land use is a patchwork of fields and towns.
senses.exampleCN: 这个河谷的土地利用是田块与城镇拼成的拼图。
senses.why: one field has a use, but a region has a pattern, and planners speak of the pattern as the land use.
senses.whyCN: 一块田有一个用途，而一个区域有一种格局，规划者把这种格局也称作土地利用。

senses.title: Zoning and planning decisions
senses.definition: the rules that assign permitted purposes to parcels of land
senses.definitionCN: 给各地块分配允许用途的规则
senses.example: Land use rules kept the factory out of the village.
senses.exampleCN: 土地用途规则把工厂挡在村庄之外。
senses.why: a purpose becomes a rule when a council writes it into a zoning map.
senses.whyCN: 当议会把一种用途写进分区图，用途就变成规则。

senses.title: Change over time
senses.definition: the conversion of land from one purpose to another, tracked as land-use change
senses.definitionCN: 土地从一种用途转为另一种，作为土地利用变化来追踪
senses.example: Satellite images revealed rapid land use change at the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像显示海岸带发生了迅速的土地利用变化。
senses.why: once two maps exist, the difference between them becomes a process with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有两张地图，它们之间的差异就变成一个有自己的名字的过程。

senses.title: Farm and forest categories
senses.definition: the classification of land as cropland, pasture, orchard or woodland
senses.definitionCN: 把土地归为耕地、牧场、果园或林地
senses.example: The survey recorded agricultural land use acre by acre.
senses.exampleCN: 调查逐英亩记录了农业土地利用。
senses.why: statistics need buckets, so each purpose becomes a category in a land-use table.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要分类格，于是每种用途都成为土地利用表中的一类。

senses.title: An urban development label
senses.definition: the mix of residential, commercial and industrial purposes in a built-up area
senses.definitionCN: 建成区内居住、商业与工业用途的组合
senses.example: Mixed land use keeps shops within walking distance.
senses.exampleCN: 混合土地利用让商店保持在步行距离内。
senses.why: cities combine purposes in one block, and the label describes that combination.
senses.whyCN: 城市在同一个街区组合多种用途，这个标签描述的就是这种组合。

senses.title: A variable in impact analysis
senses.titleCN: 影响分析中的一个变量
senses.definition: the input to models of runoff, emissions, habitat loss or transport demand
senses.definitionCN: 径流、排放、生境丧失或交通需求模型中的输入项
senses.example: The model linked land use to phosphorus runoff.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型把土地利用与磷径流联系起来。
senses.why: researchers need a single word for what people do to the surface, and this compound is that word.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要用一个词概括人对地表所做的事，这个复合词就是那个词。

senses.title: Allocation of any space
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何空间的用途分配
senses.definition: the assignment of purposes to any limited space, physical or conceptual
senses.definitionCN: 给任何有限空间分配用途，无论是实体还是概念空间
senses.example: The studio reviewed land use inside the page layout.
senses.exampleCN: 工作室检视了页面版面内部的「土地利用」。
senses.why: the metaphor treats any layout as a territory to be zoned.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把任何版面都当作一块需要分区的领土。

intro.en: Land use joins the native Germanic noun land with use, a noun from Latin usus 'employment'. The compound is a modern planning term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: land use 把日耳曼本族名词 land 与 use 组合起来；use 来自拉丁 usus「使用」。这个复合词是现代规划术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Land is a Germanic word for ground, territory or country, with cognates across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: land 是日耳曼语中表示地面、领土或国家的词，在其他日耳曼语言中也有同源词。

items.en: The deeper root often proposed for land is a reconstruction; its exact shape and meaning are not attested directly.
items.cn: 常为 land 提出的更深词根属于重构形式，其确切形态与意义没有直接实证。

items.en: Uti meant 'to use, employ, enjoy'. Its past participle usus supplied the noun for use and practice.
items.cn: uti 意为「使用、运用、享有」。其过去分词 usus 提供了表示使用与惯例的名词。

items.en: Old French us carried the Latin noun into English, where use named both the act and the purpose of a thing.
items.cn: 古法语 us 把这个拉丁名词带入英语，use 既指行为，也指事物的用途。

items.en: Land use became a fixed term with twentieth-century town planning and resource surveys.
items.cn: land use 随 20 世纪的城镇规划与资源调查成为固定术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Germanic root of land and the pre-Latin root of uti are both unsettled, and the first printed use of the compound is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：land 的日耳曼语之前词根与 uti 的拉丁语之前词根都无定论，这个复合词的最早书证也没有定说。

note.en: Group one holds land terms that are constantly mistaken for land use; group two holds planning ideas that work alongside it.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误当作 land use 的土地术语；第二组是与之配合的规划概念。

entries.definition: The physical surface actually present, such as grass, concrete or water; land use is the purpose behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 实际存在的物理地表，如草地、混凝土或水；land use 是背后的用途。

entries.definition: The legal arrangement of who owns or occupies land, not what it is used for.
entries.definitionCN: 关于谁拥有或占有土地的法律安排，而非土地作何用途。

entries.definition: A natural feature of the surface such as a ridge or valley; it describes shape, not human purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 山脊、河谷等自然地表形态；描述形状，不描述人的用途。

entries.definition: The process of building on land, which changes its use but is not the same as the use itself.
entries.definitionCN: 在土地上建造的过程；它改变用途，但不等同于用途本身。

entries.definition: The division of land into zones with permitted uses; it is the instrument that enforces land use.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地划成有允许用途的区；它是执行土地利用的工具。

entries.definition: The day-to-day care of land, including soil, water and vegetation, rather than its assigned purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 对土地包括土壤、水与植被的日常照料，而非其被派定的用途。

entries.definition: The planning of activities across space, of which land use planning is one part.
entries.definitionCN: 对空间中的活动进行规划，土地利用规划是其中一部分。

entries.definition: How heavily a parcel is worked, such as yields per hectare; it measures intensity rather than purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 一块地被使用的强度，如每公顷产量；它衡量强度而非用途。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: land + use: the compound asks what the ground is employed for.
normal.cn: land + use：这个复合词问的是这块地被用来做什么。

normal.en: The family runs land, use, useful, usage, land-use planning, land cover.
normal.cn: 同族说法包括 land、use、useful、usage、land-use planning、land cover。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: land use planning, land use change, land use map.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：土地利用规划、土地利用变化、土地利用图。

normal.en: Land cover is what you see; land use is why it is there.
normal.cn: 土地覆盖是你看到的，土地利用是它为什么在那里。

normal.en: Latin usus 'use' also gives usage, usual and usury's older sense of use.
normal.cn: 拉丁 usus「使用」也衍生 usage、usual 以及 usury 较早的「使用」义。

abstract.en: Picture a quilt whose patches are labeled by what they do.
abstract.cn: 想象一床拼布被，每块布都标着它的用途。

abstract.en: Picture a map that colors the ground by intention, not by grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，按意图而不是按草色给土地上色。

abstract.en: Picture a desk divided into zones for writing, eating and sleeping.
abstract.cn: 想象一张书桌被划成写字、吃饭与睡觉的区域。

examples.en: Land use change is the main driver of habitat loss.
examples.cn: 土地利用变化是生境丧失的主要驱动因素。

examples.en: The council published a new land use plan for the valley.
examples.cn: 议会发布了这个河谷的新土地利用规划。

examples.en: Mixed land use reduces the need to drive.
examples.cn: 混合土地利用减少了开车的需要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「land（土地）+ use（用途）」——土地派什么用场 → 土地利用

root: land 为日耳曼本族词，更深词根属重构；use 经古法语 us 来自拉丁 usus「使用」，再上溯 uti「使用」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one surface: a purpose is assigned, patches form a pattern, rules fix it, maps track change, statistics classify it, cities mix it, models read it, and finally any space can be zoned.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个地表展开：用途被派定、地块形成格局、规则将其固定、地图追踪变化、统计将其分类、城市将其混合、模型读取它，最后任何空间都可被分区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a valley divided into colored patches, each standing for a purpose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片谷地被分成彩色地块，每块代表一种用途。

branches.en: PURPOSE AND CATEGORY: a parcel serves a function, and statistics sort those functions into buckets.
branches.cn: 用途与分类：地块承担功能，统计再把功能分进格子。

branches.en: PATTERN AND CHANGE: many parcels form a regional pattern, and two maps in time reveal its change.
branches.cn: 格局与变化：许多地块形成区域格局，两个时间点的地图揭示其变化。

branches.en: RULES AND MIX: zoning fixes permitted uses, and cities combine several in one block.
branches.cn: 规则与混合：分区固定允许用途，城市在同一街区组合多种用途。

branches.en: MODEL INPUT: runoff, emissions and transport models take land use as a variable.
branches.cn: 模型输入：径流、排放与交通模型把土地利用当作变量。

branches.en: METAPHOR: any limited layout can be treated as territory to be zoned.
branches.cn: 比喻：任何有限版面都可当作需要分区的领土。

intro.en: Land use is a compound of a native noun and a Latin-derived noun. Both halves are simple free forms rather than prefixes or suffixes, but each builds a large family.
intro.cn: land use 是日耳曼本族名词与拉丁来源名词的复合。两半都是简单的自由词形，而非前缀或后缀，但各自构成庞大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti 'to use' and usus 'use' give use, usage, useful, useless and misuse; land is native Germanic and has no Latin entry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 uti「使用」与 usus「使用」衍生 use、usage、useful、useless 与 misuse；land 是日耳曼本族词，没有拉丁条目。

items.example: The land rose toward the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 土地向山脊抬升。

items.example: The field's use is pasture.
items.exampleCN: 这块地的用途是牧场。

items.structure: Latin noun usus, usus (m., fourth declension)
items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语词的基底。

items.example: The map is useful for planning.
items.exampleCN: 这张地图对规划有用。

items.example: A map without a legend is useless.
items.exampleCN: 没有图例的地图毫无用处。

items.meaning: the manner or amount of use
items.example: Water usage fell after the meter was installed.

items.exampleCN: 土地使用者必须提交申报。

items.exampleCN: 坡地的误用造成了侵蚀。

items.example: The county maps land use every ten years.
items.exampleCN: 该县每十年绘制一次土地利用图。

definition_zh: 解释的；诠释性的；（艺术表演）演绎的；带解读性质的
definition_en: relating to interpretation; serving to explain or reveal meaning, especially in scholarship, law, exhibition texts, or performance
core_image: 一个人举着放大镜看画，把画里藏的线索引给旁边的人看
scene: 美术馆里，策展人指着画旁的小牌子。 The label is interpretative text that explains the symbols in the painting.
sceneCN: 这里 interpretative 是「诠释性的」（第 1 个义项：用于解释含义的）；句意：说明牌是诠释性文字，解释画中的象征。

pos.zh: 解释的；诠释性的（用于说明文字、研究、法律解释等）
演绎的；带个人解读的（用于表演、艺术处理）

forms.label: 形容词原级（英式常见形式）

derivatives.zh: 诠释主义（社会科学方法论）

senses.title: Serving to explain
senses.definition: describing writing, labels, or speech that explains the meaning of something to an audience
senses.definitionCN: 描述向受众解释某事物含义的文字、标签或话语
senses.example: Interpretative panels guide visitors through the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 解说牌引导观众参观这座旧工厂。
senses.why: Interpretative is interpret + -ative, an adjective of function: it names what a text or object is for. The Latin verb interpretari meant 'to expound', so the suffix makes the explaining into a purpose.
senses.whyCN: interpretative 是 interpret + -ative，一个表示功能用途的形容词：它命名一个文本或物件是用来做什么的。拉丁动词 interpretari 意为“阐明”，后缀把解释变成一种用途。

senses.title: Scholarly reading
senses.definition: describing research or criticism that proposes a reading of texts, events, or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 描述提出对文本、事件或证据之解读的研究或批评
senses.example: The book is more interpretative than descriptive.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书偏诠释而非描述。
senses.why: Scholarship distinguishes description from interpretation: the first records, the second argues for a meaning. The adjective marks work that takes that second step and therefore invites disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 学术区分描述与诠释：前者记录，后者为某种意义辩护。这个形容词标记迈出第二步的工作，因此也招来异议。

senses.title: Realized in performance
senses.definition: describing a performance that presents one chosen reading of a work rather than a neutral delivery
senses.definitionCN: 描述呈现某种选定解读、而非中性呈现的表演
senses.example: The production offered an interpretative reading of the final scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这版制作对最后一幕作了演绎性解读。
senses.why: Performance cannot avoid choice: tempo, casting, and staging all decide meaning. The adjective acknowledges that choice instead of hiding it behind 'faithful' delivery.
senses.whyCN: 表演无法回避选择：速度、选角与舞台调度都在决定意义。这个形容词承认这种选择，而不是把它藏在“忠实呈现”后面。

senses.title: Interpretative in law
senses.definition: describing a doctrine, ruling, or statement that sets out how a legal text should be understood
senses.definitionCN: 描述阐明法律文本应如何被理解的学说、裁决或声明
senses.example: The agency issued an interpretative rule rather than a binding regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构发布的是解释性规则，而非有约束力的法规。
senses.why: In law the adjective signals a distinction of force: an interpretative document explains the agency's reading but may not carry the same legal weight as a regulation.
senses.whyCN: 在法律中，这个形容词标记效力上的区别：解释性文件说明机构的解读，但其法律分量可能不等同于法规。

senses.title: Hermeneutic in philosophy
senses.definition: describing the view that understanding always involves interpretation by a situated observer
senses.definitionCN: 描述“理解总是涉及处于特定处境的观察者的解释”这一观点
senses.example: Interpretative theory holds that no observation is entirely neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 诠释理论认为没有哪种观察是完全中立的。
senses.why: Hermeneutics generalised the adjective: if all understanding is interpretation, then every description already carries a reading. The word becomes a claim about knowledge, not about texts.
senses.whyCN: 诠释学把这个形容词普遍化：如果一切理解都是解释，那么每一种描述都已带着解读。这个词由此成为关于知识的主张，而不只是关于文本。

senses.title: Subjective or personal reading
senses.definition: describing an account that reflects the observer's own perspective more than the object itself
senses.definitionCN: 描述更多反映观察者自身视角而非对象本身的叙述
senses.example: His interpretative account of the strike emphasized motives over dates.
senses.exampleCN: 他对罢工的解读性叙述更重动机而轻日期。
senses.why: This sense carries a warning as well as a description: interpretative work may be insightful or may simply project. The adjective leaves the judgement open, which is why it is often followed by 'rather than factual'.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项既描述也提醒：诠释性工作可能很有洞见，也可能只是投射。形容词把判断留空，所以常接 rather than factual。

senses.title: Interpretative with data or evidence
senses.titleCN: 对数据或证据作解读的
senses.definition: describing analysis that assigns meaning to findings rather than merely reporting them
senses.definitionCN: 描述赋予研究结果以意义、而不只是报告结果的分析
senses.example: The interpretative section of the report explains why the trend matters.
senses.exampleCN: 报告的解读部分说明这一趋势为何重要。
senses.why: Reports separate findings from interpretation so that readers can check the first against the second. The adjective marks the part where judgement enters the chain.
senses.whyCN: 报告把发现与解释分开，好让读者用前者核对后者。这个形容词标记判断进入链条的那一部分。

senses.title: Interpretative art form
senses.definition: describing a style such as interpretative dance that conveys meaning through expressive movement rather than literal narrative
senses.definitionCN: 描述表现性舞蹈这类通过富有意味的动作而非字面叙事传达意义的风格
senses.example: The festival opened with an interpretative dance about migration.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术节以一支关于迁徙的表现性舞蹈开幕。
senses.why: The arts use the adjective for works that translate an idea into another medium instead of describing it. The audience is asked to read the movement, so the word keeps its oldest meaning: carrying meaning across.
senses.whyCN: 艺术领域用这个形容词指把某个观念转换到另一种媒介、而非直接描述的作品。观众被要求去读这些动作，因此这个词保留了最古老的含义：把意义运送过去。

intro.en: Interpretative is interpret + -ative, formed in English on the Latin verb interpretari and its noun interpres 'go-between'. Interpretive is the shorter variant, and both are standard; interpretative is older in British usage.
intro.cn: interpretative 是 interpret + -ative，在英语中由拉丁动词 interpretari 及其名词 interpres“中间人”构成。interpretive 是较短的变体，两者都是标准形式；interpretative 在英式用法中更早。

items.en: Interpretari 'to explain, expound, translate' came from interpres, the go-between who carries words across. The past participle interpretatus supplied the stem for later adjectives.
items.cn: interpretari“解释、阐明、翻译”来自 interpres，即把话带过河的中间人。过去分词 interpretatus 为后来的形容词提供了词干。

items.en: The formation of interpres itself is disputed; a link with pretium 'price' is often proposed but not proven. The adjective therefore inherits a root whose second element cannot be stated with certainty.
items.cn: interpres 本身的构词有争议；与 pretium“价格”的联系常被提出但未获证明。因此这个形容词继承的词根，其第二个成分无法确定地说明。

items.en: English formed interpretative on the model of Latin -ativus adjectives. Early uses were scholarly: explaining Scripture, law, and dreams.
items.cn: 英语仿照拉丁语 -ativus 形容词的模式构成 interpretative。早期用法是学术性的：解释经文、法律与梦。

items.en: The word extended to performance and to any act of assigning meaning. Interpretive appeared as a shortened rival form, especially in American usage.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到表演以及任何赋予意义的行为。interpretive 作为缩短的竞争形式出现，尤其在美式用法中。

items.en: Hermeneutics and literary criticism made 'interpretative' a marker of method: work that argues for a reading rather than merely recording facts.
items.cn: 诠释学与文学批评使 interpretative 成为方法标记：为某种解读辩护、而非只记录事实的工作。

items.en: Modern usage ranges from museum labels and legal notices to dance and philosophy. The word always marks a step beyond description, toward meaning.
items.cn: 现代用法从博物馆说明牌、法律公告一直延伸到舞蹈与哲学。这个词总标记着超越描述、走向意义的那一步。

note.en: The look-alike group separates adjectives ending in -ative or -ive that come from different verbs; the near-meaning group separates explanatory, expressive, and analytical words.
note.cn: 形近组区分以 -ative 或 -ive 结尾但来自不同动词的形容词；近义组区分表示“解释”“表现”与“分析”的词。

entries.definition: the shorter form of the same adjective, now more common in American English. It carries the same meanings and differs only in style and frequency.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的较短形式，在美式英语中更常用。含义相同，只在语体与使用频率上有差别。

entries.definition: copying or reproducing something. It comes from imitari 'to copy', not from interpres; it describes resemblance, not explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 模仿或复制某物。它来自 imitari“模仿”，而非 interpres；描述相似，而不是解释。

entries.definition: serving as an example or clarification. Latin illustrare 'light up, make clear' is the source; the word shows by example rather than by construing meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 用作例证或说明的。拉丁语 illustrare“照亮、使清楚”是其来源；这个词通过举例来展示，而不是通过建构意义。

entries.definition: intended to make something clear. It is the plain functional word; interpretative adds that a particular reading is being offered.
entries.definitionCN: 意在使某事物清楚的。它是朴素的功能性用词；interpretative 额外表示所提供的是某一种解读。

entries.definition: conveying feeling or meaning through form. It is about the power of the medium, while interpretative is about the reading being presented.
entries.definitionCN: 通过形式传达情感或意义。它讲媒介的力量，而 interpretative 讲所呈现的解读。

entries.definition: breaking something into parts to understand it. It names a procedure, while interpretative names the goal of arriving at meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 把事物拆成部分以理解。它命名一种程序，而 interpretative 命名抵达意义的目标。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: the -ative adjective suffix on interpret, the rival shorter form interpretive, and the museum phrase interpretative panel.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：interpret 上的 -ative 形容词后缀、较短的竞争形式 interpretive，以及博物馆用语 interpretative panel。

normal.en: interpret + -ative: an adjective that says this thing is for explaining.
normal.cn: interpret + -ative：这个形容词表示“这个东西是用来解释的”。

normal.en: interpretive is the same word with a shorter tail; choose one and be consistent.
normal.cn: interpretive 是同一个词、尾巴更短；选一个并保持一致。

normal.en: An interpretative panel stands between the object and the visitor, carrying meaning across.
normal.cn: 解说牌站在展品与观众之间，把意义送过去。

normal.en: An interpretative ruling explains the agency's reading but binds less than a regulation.
normal.cn: 解释性裁决说明机构的解读，但约束力不如法规。

normal.en: Interpretative dance asks the audience to read movement as meaning.
normal.cn: 表现性舞蹈要求观众把动作读成意义。

abstract.en: The word marks the step after description: first record, then say what it means.
abstract.cn: 这个词标记描述之后的那一步：先记录，再说它意味着什么。

abstract.en: It admits that a reading is being offered, and that admission is what makes criticism possible.
abstract.cn: 它承认所提供的是一个解读，这份承认正是批评得以可能的原因。

abstract.en: To interpret is to stand between; the adjective keeps that position visible instead of pretending to be neutral.
abstract.cn: 解释就是站在中间；这个形容词让那个位置保持可见，而不假装中立。

examples.en: The exhibition relies on interpretative labels rather than long captions.
examples.cn: 这个展览依靠诠释性说明牌，而不是长篇图注。

examples.en: Her interpretative essay changed how scholars read the letter.
examples.cn: 她的诠释性论文改变了学者对这封信的读法。

examples.en: The agency's interpretative guidance does not have the force of law.
examples.cn: 该机构的解释性指引不具有法律效力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “因它扑来特提舞”——它扑过来，特别把意思“提”到你面前，还带着动作 → interpretative 诠释性的、演绎的

root: inter-（在……之间）+ 拉丁语 interpres“中间人、译者”（更早来源不确定）+ -ative；核心是“把意义带到听者面前、具有解释功能的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of interpretative all describe something that carries or proposes meaning: a label, a study, a performance, a legal notice, a philosophy, a personal account, an analysis, or a dance. The word always admits that a reading is being offered.
sensesIntro.cn: interpretative 的八个义项都描述携带或提出意义的东西：说明牌、研究、表演、法律公告、哲学主张、个人叙述、分析或舞蹈。这个词始终承认所提供的是一个解读。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass over a painting, with a guide pointing out the hidden symbols.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅画上悬着放大镜，有人把藏着的象征指给旁人看。

branches.en: EXPLANATION: labels, reports, and analyses exist to turn findings into meaning.
branches.cn: 解释：说明牌、报告与分析的存在，就是把发现变成意义。

branches.en: READING: scholarship and personal accounts both offer a viewpoint that can be contested.
branches.cn: 解读：学术与个人叙述都提供可被质疑的视角。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE: staging and dance realize one chosen reading in sound or movement.
branches.cn: 表演：舞台调度与舞蹈用声音或动作实现某一种选定解读。

branches.en: LAW: an interpretative document explains a reading without always binding like a regulation.
branches.cn: 法律：解释性文件说明一种解读，但不一定像法规那样具有约束力。

branches.en: PHILOSOPHY: if all understanding is interpretation, every description already carries a reading.
branches.cn: 哲学：如果一切理解都是解释，那么每种描述都已带着解读。

intro.en: Interpretative is interpret + -ative; interpretive is the shortened variant. Both descend from Latin interpretari and interpres. The family also includes the agent noun and the mis- and re- prefixed verbs.
intro.cn: interpretative 是 interpret + -ative；interpretive 是缩短的变体。两者都源自拉丁语 interpretari 与 interpres。家族还包括施动名词以及带 mis-、re- 前缀的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin interpres 'go-between' and interpretari 'explain, translate' are the base. The origin of interpres is uncertain, with a proposed link to pretium 'price' that is not proven; the -ativus suffix is a Latin adjectival pattern.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是拉丁语 interpres“中间人”与 interpretari“解释、翻译”。interpres 的来源不确定，与 pretium“价格”的联系只是推测、未获证明；-ativus 后缀是拉丁形容词构词模式。

items.meaning: serving to explain or offer a reading
items.meaningCN: 解释性的；诠释性的（-ative 构成形容词）
items.example: The signs are interpretative, not decorative.
items.exampleCN: 这些标牌是解说性的，不是装饰性的。

items.example: The park has an interpretive trail.
items.exampleCN: 这座公园有一条解说步道。

items.meaningCN: 解释；翻译（源自拉丁动词）
items.example: Readers interpret the ending differently.
items.exampleCN: 读者对结局有不同解读。

items.meaningCN: 解释；诠释（-ation 构成名词）
items.example: The interpretation was published separately.
items.exampleCN: 这份解释另行发表。

items.meaning: one who explains or translates speech
items.meaningCN: 口译员；解释者（-er 表施动者）
items.example: The interpreter sat beside the witness.
items.exampleCN: 口译员坐在证人旁边。

items.meaningCN: 以诠释的方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The gallery was interpretatively organized.
items.exampleCN: 展厅按诠释线索布置。

items.meaning: the methodological view that meaning must be interpreted
items.example: Interpretivism favours qualitative methods.
items.exampleCN: 诠释主义偏好质性方法。

items.example: Critics misinterpreted the title.
items.exampleCN: 评论者误解了这个标题。

items.meaning: to read in a new way
items.example: Later historians reinterpreted the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 后来的历史学家重新解释了这条约。

latinEntries.structure: interpres, interpretis (third declension); deeper origin uncertain
latinEntries.meaningCN: 中间人；译者（更早来源不确定）

latinEntries.structure: second-declension noun; proposed but unproven link
latinEntries.meaningCN: 价格；价值（与 interpres 的关联为推测，来源不确定）

definition_zh: 色谱（法）的；用色谱法分离、检测或分析的
definition_en: relating to chromatography, the technique of separating the components of a mixture by passing them through a medium at different speeds
core_image: 一滴植物浸液点在滤纸下缘，溶剂向上爬，颜色被拉成几条长短不一的横带，像有人用颜色写了一行字
scene: 实验台上，一片绿叶的浸液被点在滤纸下缘，溶剂沿着纸面往上爬，颜色慢慢分成几条深浅不同的横带。 The chromatographic separation revealed four pigments in the leaf extract.
sceneCN: 这里 chromatographic 指「用色谱法进行的分离」（第 1 个义项：与色谱分离方法相关）；句意为这次色谱分离在叶片提取液里显示出四种色素。图中可辨识物件：滤纸、点样毛细管、展开槽、四条色带。

pos.zh: 色谱（法）的；用色谱法分离或检测的

senses.title: Belonging to the separation method
senses.definition: relating to chromatography as a laboratory technique for separating mixtures
senses.definitionCN: 与作为分离混合物的实验室技术的色谱法有关
senses.example: The team chose a chromatographic method to separate the leaf pigments.
senses.exampleCN: 团队选择用色谱方法分离叶片中的色素。
senses.why: The adjective simply attaches the name of the technique to whatever it describes, so this is its plainest reading.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把技术名称挂到所修饰的对象上，因此这是它最朴素的用法。

senses.title: Produced by a chromatographic run
senses.titleCN: 由色谱分离得到的结果
senses.definition: obtained as a fraction or result of a chromatographic separation
senses.definitionCN: 作为色谱分离的馏分或结果而得到的
senses.example: The chromatographic fraction held a single sugar.
senses.exampleCN: 这一色谱馏分中只含一种糖。
senses.why: Once a mixture has been run through the medium, whatever comes out carries the name of the process that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 混合物一旦通过介质跑完一遍，出来的东西就带上产生它的那道工序之名。

senses.title: Naming the apparatus of the method
senses.titleCN: 指称色谱法所用装置的
senses.definition: describing a column, plate, detector or instrument built for chromatography
senses.definitionCN: 描述为色谱法而制造的柱、板、检测器或仪器
senses.example: She changed the chromatographic column before the next run.
senses.exampleCN: 在下一次进样前，她换掉了色谱柱。
senses.why: Apparatus takes the adjective because the column exists only in order to perform this one operation.
senses.whyCN: 装置带上这个形容词，是因为色谱柱存在的唯一目的就是完成这一道操作。

senses.title: Read as a pattern of peaks
senses.definition: describing a trace, profile or fingerprint that records the separated components as peaks
senses.definitionCN: 描述把已分离组分记成峰形的图谱、轮廓或指纹
senses.example: The chromatographic profile showed one unexpected peak.
senses.exampleCN: 色谱图谱上出现了一个意料之外的峰。
senses.why: The record left by the run is a picture of separation, so it inherits the adjective from the process.
senses.whyCN: 一次分离留下的记录就是分离本身的图像，因此它也从这一过程继承了该形容词。

senses.title: Spread out in visible bands
senses.titleCN: 呈层层展开色带的（视觉比喻）
senses.definition: used of a visual effect in which colours or layers spread apart in bands, like a developed chromatogram
senses.definitionCN: 用于颜色或层次像显影后的色谱图那样分成带状铺开的视觉效果
senses.example: The ink spread into a chromatographic fan across the wet paper.
senses.exampleCN: 墨水在湿纸上散成一个扇形的色带。
senses.why: The technique began with coloured pigments, so its visual signature of banded spreading became a ready comparison outside the lab.
senses.whyCN: 这门技术最初处理的是彩色色素，于是「分层铺开」的视觉特征就成了实验室之外的现成比喻。

senses.title: Of a grade fit for the method
senses.definition: describing a solvent or standard purified to the level that chromatography requires
senses.definitionCN: 描述纯化到色谱分析所要求程度的溶剂或标准品
senses.example: Only chromatographic grade solvent was used for the trace analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 痕量分析只使用了色谱级溶剂。
senses.why: A method sensitive to traces forces everything used in it to be cleaned to the same standard, and the adjective marks that standard.
senses.whyCN: 对痕量敏感的方法会迫使所用一切都被净化到同一标准，这个形容词就标出那一标准。

senses.title: Able to split a mixture into parts
senses.titleCN: 能把混杂局面拆开的（抽象义）
senses.definition: used figuratively of an approach that separates a tangled mixture of things into distinct parts
senses.definitionCN: 比喻把纠缠在一起的混杂局面拆成若干清楚部分的做法
senses.example: The committee took a chromatographic approach to the flood of complaints.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会用一种「色谱式」的办法处理涌入的投诉。
senses.why: The abstract use keeps only the core gesture of the method, namely sorting one mass into several separable parts.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法只保留方法的核心动作，即把一团东西分拣成几个可以分开的部分。

senses.title: Of the literal colour-writing name
senses.definition: referring to the literal sense of the coined name, writing or recording by means of colour
senses.definitionCN: 指这个新造名称的字面义，即借助颜色来书写或记录
senses.example: The name itself preserves a chromatographic idea: writing with colour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个名称本身就保留着「用颜色书写」的意象。
senses.why: The word was coined from a Greek noun for colour and a Greek verb for writing, and this literal layer still shows through the technical adjective.
senses.whyCN: 该词由希腊语中表示颜色的名词与表示书写的动词合成，这层字面意思至今仍透在这个技术形容词里。

intro.en: The adjective comes from the name of the technique, coined in the early twentieth century from Greek khrōma 'colour' and graphein 'to write'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个形容词来自技术名称本身，该名称于二十世纪初由希腊语表示「颜色」的名词与表示「书写」的动词合成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Khrōma meant 'colour', and also 'skin, surface'. It is generally connected with khrōs 'skin, complexion', though the exact pre-Greek shape is a reconstruction.
items.cn: khrōma 意为「颜色」，也指「皮肤、表面」。一般认为它与表示「肤色、面色」的 khrōs 相关，但其希腊语之前的确切形态属重构形式。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to scratch, draw, write', and gave the combining element -graphia 'writing, recording'. Its deeper origin is not settled.
items.cn: graphein 意为「刻、画、写」，并提供了表示「书写、记录」的组合成分。其更深来源没有定论。

items.en: A Russian botanist used the new Latin name chromatographia around the turn of the twentieth century for a method that separated plant pigments into coloured bands on paper. First date uncertain (exact year of coining): the first publication date is variously given, so the precise year is not fixed here.
items.cn: 一位俄国植物学家在二十世纪之交用新拉丁名称 chromatographia 指一种把植物色素在纸上分成色带的方法。首见年代不确定：首次发表的年份各家说法不一，此处不锁定具体年份。

items.en: English took the noun as chromatography, and within a few decades the derived adjective was in use in chemical writing.
items.cn: 英语以表示该技术的名词吸收了这个名称，几十年内其派生形容词就出现在化学文献中。

items.en: The adjective appears almost only in front of a noun naming a method, an apparatus, a record or a grade. Since the method now works on colourless substances, the colour element of the name is historical, and only the notion of banded separation survives in figurative use.
items.cn: 这个形容词几乎只出现在表示方法、装置、记录或纯度的名词之前。由于该方法如今处理的是无色物质，名称中的颜色成分已成历史，只有「分层分离」的观念在比喻用法中留存。

items.en: First date uncertain: the adjective is recorded from the early twentieth century onward, but no single first citation is agreed, and any earlier date offered would be a guess.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：该形容词自二十世纪初起有记录，但没有公认的唯一最早书证，凡给出更早年代者均属推测。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look close to the adjective but come from other roots; group two holds terms for neighbouring laboratory methods.
note.cn: 第一组是外形相近但词根不同的词；第二组是实验室里相邻的其他分析方法。

entries.definition: Built on the same Greek noun for colour, but with no writing element: it means 'of colour' in music and optics, not 'of the separation method'.
entries.definitionCN: 同样建立在希腊语「颜色」名词上，但不含「书写」成分：在音乐与光学中指「色彩的」，与分离方法无关。

entries.definition: A strand of a duplicated chromosome; the element here goes back to chromatin, and the resemblance to the colour noun is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制后染色体的一条；这里的成分源自染色质，与颜色名词的相似是偶然的。

entries.definition: From the Greek verb for writing, with no colour element: it means 'of drawing or visual presentation'.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语表示书写的动词，不含颜色成分：意为「绘图的、视觉呈现的」。

entries.definition: The noun for the machine that performs the separation; it differs from the adjective only by the final element, and the two are often confused in fast reading.
entries.definitionCN: 指执行分离的机器；它与形容词只差词尾成分，快速阅读时二者常被混淆。

entries.definition: Describes a separation driven by an electric field rather than by differential flow through a medium.
entries.definitionCN: 描述由电场驱动、而非靠流经介质的速度差实现的分离。

entries.definition: Describes the reading of a spectrum to identify substances; it analyses what is already mixed instead of splitting it.
entries.definitionCN: 描述通过读光谱来鉴定物质；它分析已经混在一起的东西，而不去拆分。

entries.definition: A general adjective for any method that determines what a sample contains; the chromatographic method is one member of that class.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何测定样品成分的方法，色谱法只是这一类中的一员。

entries.definition: Describes separation by spinning a sample so that heavier parts move outward; it sorts by mass, not by affinity for a medium.
entries.definitionCN: 描述靠旋转样品使较重部分外移的分离；它按质量分拣，而不是按对介质的亲和性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name joins a Greek noun for colour to a Greek verb for writing, so the technique is literally 'colour writing'.
normal.cn: 名称把希腊语的「颜色」名词与「书写」动词接在一起，这门技术字面上就是「颜色书写」。

normal.en: The family runs from the method to the machine to the picture: chromatography, chromatograph, chromatogram, chromatographic.
normal.cn: 同族词从方法到机器再到图像依次展开：表示方法的名词、表示仪器的名词、表示图谱的名词、以及这个形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: chromatographic separation, chromatographic column, chromatographic peak.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术用法：色谱分离、色谱柱、色谱峰。

normal.en: A single run leaves a profile of peaks, which is why the adjective also names the record rather than only the method.
normal.cn: 一次进样会留下峰形轮廓，因此这个形容词也用来修饰记录，而不只修饰方法。

normal.en: The method sorts by how fast each component travels, so speed difference is the whole trick.
normal.cn: 该方法按各组分移动的快慢来分拣，速度差就是全部诀窍。

abstract.en: Picture a race in which every runner is timed and the results are written out as lines of different length.
abstract.cn: 想象一场比赛，每位选手都被计时，成绩被写成长短不一的横线。

abstract.en: Picture a choir splitting into sections by voice, each section standing in its own row.
abstract.cn: 想象一支合唱团按声部分开，每个声部各站成一排。

abstract.en: Picture a letter written in invisible ink that only shows its separate colours when warmed.
abstract.cn: 想象一封用隐形墨水写的信，加热后才显出各自分开的颜色。

examples.en: The chromatographic run cleanly separated the two isomers.
examples.cn: 这次色谱分离把两种异构体干净地分开了。

examples.en: Air samples were checked by a chromatographic method sensitive to traces.
examples.cn: 空气样品用一种对痕量敏感的色谱方法检测。

examples.en: The chromatographic trace is stored as a series of peak heights.
examples.cn: 色谱曲线以一系列峰高的形式保存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 记作「颜色书写」：表示颜色的成分加表示书写的成分，就是把混合物写成一条条色带 → 色谱的

root: 希腊语 khrōma「颜色」+ graphein「书写」，字面为「颜色书写」，由二十世纪初的植物学家为新分离方法命名；颜色成分如今只是历史遗留，方法本身已用于无色物质。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses circle a single attributive role: the adjective names the method, then the result, the apparatus, the record, the visual signature, the purity grade, a figurative split, and finally the literal colour-writing name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个定语角色转：这个形容词先指方法，再指结果、装置、记录、视觉特征、纯度等级、比喻性的拆分，最后回到字面的「颜色书写」之名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of mixed liquid climbing up paper and coming apart into bands of different length.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴混合液沿纸面向上爬，分成几条长短不一的色带。

branches.en: Method and product: the adjective first names the technique, then whatever the technique yields.
branches.cn: 方法与产物：先指技术本身，再指技术所产出之物。

branches.en: Hardware and standard: a column is built for the method, and a solvent is purified to its demand.
branches.cn: 硬件与标准：色谱柱为该法而造，溶剂为该法的要求而纯化。

branches.en: The trace as picture: peaks on a chart and bands on wet paper are the same separation seen twice.
branches.cn: 记录即图像：图上的峰与湿纸上的带，是同一次分离的两次显形。

branches.en: The split without a lab: any tangle sorted into separable parts borrows the gesture.
branches.cn: 离开实验室的拆分：任何被分成可分开部分的乱局都借用了这个动作。

branches.en: The name read back: colour plus writing still shows through every later use.
branches.cn: 回读名称：颜色加书写仍透在后来每一层用法里。

intro.en: The adjective is built from a Greek noun, a Greek verb and two suffixes, and the same pieces build the whole technical family.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由希腊语名词、希腊语动词与两个后缀构成，同样的部件也构成整个技术词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies both halves of the name: khrōma for colour and graphein for writing; Latin contributes only the later New Latin coinage.
latinIntro.cn: 名称的两半都来自希腊语：一半是颜色，一半是书写；拉丁语只提供了后世的新拉丁造词。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the nature of
items.example: The suffix turns a noun of method into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把方法名词变成形容词。

items.example: The element marks any word built on the writing root.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分标记一切建立在书写词根上的词。

items.example: The colour element survives only in the history of the name.
items.exampleCN: 颜色成分只留在这个名称的历史里。

items.example: The writing element names the record left on the medium.
items.exampleCN: 书写成分指留在介质上的记录。

items.meaning: the technique of separating by differential travel
items.meaningCN: 按差速移动进行分离的技术
items.example: The noun is the base from which the adjective is formed.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的构词基础。

items.meaning: the instrument that performs the separation
items.example: The instrument suffix replaces the abstract noun ending.
items.exampleCN: 仪器后缀替换了抽象名词词尾。

items.meaning: the recorded trace of a run
items.meaningCN: 一次进样留下的记录曲线
items.example: The record suffix names the written result.
items.exampleCN: 记录后缀指书写出来的结果。

items.meaning: of the method or its products
items.meaningCN: 属于该方法或其产物的
items.example: The adjective is the form used in front of a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是置于名词前的形式。

items.example: The adverb modifies a verb of separating or measuring.
items.exampleCN: 副词修饰分离或测量的动词。

latinEntries.structure: New Latin coinage (early 20th century), from Greek stems
latinEntries.meaningCN: 色谱法，字面为颜色书写

definition_zh: 潮汐的；与潮汐有关的；受潮水涨落支配的
definition_en: relating to the tide, the regular rise and fall of sea level caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and the sun
core_image: 海水沿着同一道岸坡一天两次爬上来，又顺着同一个坡退回去，像有人在极慢地呼吸
scene: 沿海公路旁，测量员把潮汐表摊在引擎盖上，对照岸边的刻度说， Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 tidal 指「与潮汐这一自然现象有关的」（第 1 个义项：潮汐的、潮汐观测的）；句意为：这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。

pos.zh: 潮汐的；与潮汐有关的
受潮水涨落支配的；随潮汐节律的（多作定语，比较级罕用）

forms.label: 比较级（关系形容词，罕用）
最高级（关系形容词，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成：以潮汐的方式；随潮汐节律地
由「潮」加「陆地」构成的复合词：受潮水淹没的滩地
由「潮」加「线」构成的复合词：高潮退去后留下的杂物线、潮线
由「潮」加「水」构成的复合词：受潮水推动的水；潮水灌溉的低地
由「潮」加「闸门」构成的复合词：挡潮闸，退潮时放水、涨潮时挡住海水

senses.title: Of the tide as a phenomenon
senses.definition: relating to the tide as a physical phenomenon, including its timing, its height and the study of it
senses.definitionCN: 与潮汐这一物理现象有关的，包括其时刻、高度以及相关研究
senses.example: Records of tidal water levels from this bay go back two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个海湾的潮位记录可以追溯到两百年前。
senses.why: tide began as a word for 'time', and -al means 'of or belonging to'; tidal therefore says 'of the tide' before it narrows to any particular place.
senses.whyCN: tide 最初是「时间」之词，-al 表示「属于……的」；因此 tidal 首先只是「潮汐的」，之后才收窄到具体场合。

senses.title: A place the tide governs
senses.definition: of a harbour, bay or stretch of shore that is open to the tide and whose water level changes with it
senses.definitionCN: 指敞开迎潮、水位随潮水升降的港口、海湾或河岸
senses.example: The harbour is tidal, so boats leave before the water drops.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口受潮水支配，所以船只要在水位退下前离港。
senses.why: a place described by what controls it takes the relational adjective; a tidal harbour is one where the tide, not the harbour, sets the water level.
senses.whyCN: 用支配它的力量来描写一个地点时就用这个关系形容词；受潮港口的意思是潮水而非港口本身决定水位。

senses.title: Driven by the tide
senses.definition: using the rise and fall of the tide as a source of motion or electric power
senses.definitionCN: 把潮水的涨落当作动力或电力来源的
senses.example: A tidal scheme could light the island twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一套潮汐发电方案能一天两次为这座岛供电。
senses.why: the adjective of origin also marks the source of power: what belongs to the tide can be turned into what runs on the tide.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示来源的形容词也能标出动力来源：属于潮汐的东西，可以被改造成靠潮汐运转的东西。

senses.title: Of the intertidal strip
senses.definition: of the zone between the high and low water marks, covered at high tide and bare at low tide
senses.definitionCN: 指高水位线与低水位线之间、涨潮被淹、退潮露出的地带
senses.example: Crabs wait out the low water in tidal pools.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹在潮池里熬过退潮的那段时间。
senses.why: that strip has no everyday name of its own, so the adjective does the work: it is the part of the shore the tide owns.
senses.whyCN: 那条地带在日常生活里没有专门名称，于是由形容词承担：它是岸上归潮水所有的那一段。

senses.title: Reversing with the tide
senses.definition: of a current or stream whose direction turns with the flood and the ebb
senses.definitionCN: 指方向随涨潮与退潮而反转的水流
senses.example: Pilots time their entry to a favourable tidal stream.
senses.exampleCN: 引航员会掐着顺向的潮流水势进港。
senses.why: a stream that turns is 'of the tide' in direction as well as in schedule, and the adjective covers both at once.
senses.whyCN: 会掉头的水流在方向上和时间上都「属于潮汐」，一个形容词同时覆盖这两层。

senses.title: Keeping tidal time
senses.definition: of a rhythm in a living thing that is set by the tide rather than by daylight
senses.definitionCN: 指生物体内由潮汐而非日照设定的节律
senses.example: Shorebirds feed on a tidal clock rather than on the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 滨鸟按潮汐的钟点觅食，而不是按太阳的钟点。
senses.why: biology needed a word for clocks the moon winds, and the existing adjective supplied it without any new coinage.
senses.whyCN: 生物学需要为「月亮上弦的钟」找一个词，现成的形容词直接顶上，不必再造新词。

senses.title: Reached by the tide upstream
senses.definition: of the lower course of a river that salt water enters and pushes back twice a day
senses.definitionCN: 指海水每天两次灌入并顶托的河流下游段
senses.example: The lower river is tidal as far as the weir.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的下游一直到拦河堰都是感潮的。
senses.why: the tide does not stop at the coast; where it forces its way up a river, that reach becomes literally of the tide.
senses.whyCN: 潮水并不止于海岸；它顶进河流的那一段，字面上就成了「潮汐的」地盘。

senses.title: Of a gravitational tide
senses.definition: of the bulge or force raised in one body by another body's gravity, with or without water
senses.definitionCN: 指一个天体被另一个天体的引力拉出的隆起或作用力，无论表面有没有水
senses.example: The moon lifts a tidal bulge in the solid rock.
senses.exampleCN: 月球在坚硬的岩层里也拉起一个潮汐隆起。
senses.why: physics kept the water image and moved it to rock: what the moon raises in the earth is of the same nature as the sea's tide.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留水的意象又把它挪到岩石上：月球在地球里拉出的隆起，与海潮在性质上相同。

senses.title: Of one breath's volume
senses.definition: of the volume of air moved in or out in a single ordinary breath
senses.definitionCN: 指一次平静呼吸进出肺部的空气体积
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's tidal volume every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 护士每小时记录一次病人的潮气量。
senses.why: breathing repeats like the water's rise and fall, so respiratory physiology borrowed the adjective for the air moved in one cycle.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸像水的涨落一样往复，呼吸生理学于是借这个形容词，指一个周期里进出的空气量。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun fitted with a borrowed suffix: Old English tīd 'time' became tide, and English added -al to make an adjective from it. The word is recorded in tide-related writing from the eighteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tidal 是一个日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀的构造：古英语 tīd「时间」演变为 tide，英语再加 -al 构成形容词。这个词从 18 世纪的潮汐类写作中开始见于书证，年代均为约数。

items.en: Tīd meant 'time, hour, season, appointed time' and survives in eventide and Yuletide; the Germanic noun behind it is reconstructed as *tīdiz, the same word as German Zeit, so the sea sense grew out of the fixed hours at which high water was expected.
items.cn: tīd 意为「时间、时辰、季节、约定的时刻」，今仍存于若干表示时令的旧词中；其背后的日耳曼名词重构为 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同词，海潮义正是从「高潮到来的固定时刻」长出来的。

items.en: By the fourteenth century tide named the rise and fall of the sea itself, and high tide and low tide had become fixed phrases.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，tide 已指海水本身的涨落，「高潮」与「低潮」成为固定说法。

items.en: The adjective suffix -al goes back to Latin -alis by way of Norman French; English attaches it freely to nouns (tidal, coastal, legal) to mean 'of or belonging to'.
items.cn: 形容词后缀 -al 经诺曼法语上溯到拉丁 -alis；英语把它自由地加在名词后，表示「属于……的」。

items.en: Tidal appears in eighteenth-century writing on harbours and tide tables, where an adjective was needed for the phenomenon itself rather than for a particular tide.
items.cn: tidal 见于 18 世纪关于港口与潮汐表的写作，当时需要一个形容词来指这一现象本身，而不是某一次具体的潮。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the adjective spread to tidal power, tidal force in astronomy and tidal volume in physiology, each time keeping the core relation 'of the tide'.
items.cn: 19 与 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到潮汐发电、天文学中的引潮力、生理学中的潮气量，每次都保留「属于潮汐」这一核心关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest citation of tidal is generally placed in the eighteenth century but is not precisely dated; *tīdiz is a reconstruction, while the cognacy of tide and German Zeit is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：tidal 的最早书证一般定在 18 世纪，但没有确切年份；*tīdiz 是重构形式，而 tide 与德语 Zeit 同源这一点并无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like tidal or are built on the same stem, including two that end alike but come from different roots; group two holds words used about the same coastal setting.
note.cn: 第一组是与 tidal 形近或同出同一词干的词，其中两个结尾相同但词根不同；第二组是用于同一海岸情境的词。

entries.definition: the rise and fall of the sea itself; tidal only describes what belongs to it, so the noun cannot stand in for the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 海水本身的涨落；tidal 只描写属于它的东西，因此这个名词不能替代形容词。

entries.definition: tidal plus -ly, describing how something is done or driven, as in a tidally flushed lagoon.
entries.definitionCN: tidal 加 -ly，描写某事以何种方式发生或被驱动，如「靠潮水冲刷的潟湖」。

entries.definition: from Latin titulus 'inscription, label'; the shared ending is accidental and there is no tide in it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 titulus「铭文、标签」；相同的词尾纯属巧合，与潮汐无关。

entries.definition: from bride plus -al, meaning 'of a wedding'; it rhymes with tidal but is built on a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 由「新娘」一词加 -al 构成，意为「婚礼的」；它与 tidal 押韵，却建立在另一个名词上。

entries.definition: between the high and low water marks; it names one zone, while tidal can qualify anything connected with the tide.
entries.definitionCN: 位于高低潮线之间；它只指一个地带，而 tidal 可修饰任何与潮汐有关的事物。

entries.definition: of the shore, whether or not tides reach it; it is a wider term than tidal.
entries.definitionCN: 海岸的，无论潮水是否到达；它比 tidal 范围更宽。

entries.definition: of an estuary, the place where a river meets the tide; it names the setting rather than the tide's influence.
entries.definitionCN: 河口湾的，即河流与潮水相遇之处；它指这类地点，而非潮汐的影响。

entries.definition: recurring at regular intervals; tidal behaviour is one kind of periodic behaviour, so the general word is wider.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定间隔重复的；潮汐行为是周期性行为的一种，因此这个一般词的范围更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English tīd meant 'time', and the tide keeps its own clock: high water arrives at fixed hours.
normal.cn: 古英语 tīd 意为「时间」，潮水也自带时钟：高潮总在固定的时刻到来。

normal.en: The family runs tide, tidal, tidally, tideland, tideline, tidewater, tidegate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tide、tidal、tidally、tideland、tideline、tidewater、tidegate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the coastal sense: tidal flat, tidal pool, tidal current, tidal bore.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出海岸义：潮滩、潮池、潮流、涌潮。

normal.en: German Zeit 'time' is the cousin of tide; the two words split long before English existed.
normal.cn: 德语 Zeit「时间」是 tide 的表亲，两词在英语形成之前就已分开。

normal.en: A relational adjective rarely takes more or most: the comparative sounds awkward in ordinary use.
normal.cn: 关系形容词很少用比较级：在普通用法里，比较级听起来很别扭。

abstract.en: Picture the sea climbing a stone stair, one step every six hours.
abstract.cn: 想象海水在爬石阶，每六个小时上一级。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands are moved by the moon instead of by a spring.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，指针不靠发条，而由月亮推动。

abstract.en: Picture a river that briefly turns salty and flows backwards twice a day.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河一天两次短暂变咸，并倒着流。

examples.en: Tidal water reached the lower streets before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前，潮水已经漫到低处的街道。

examples.en: The tidal flat teems with worms and shells at low water.
examples.cn: 退潮时，潮滩上尽是沙蚕与贝壳。

examples.en: Engineers survey tidal currents before anchoring the turbine.
examples.cn: 工程师在固定涡轮之前先勘测潮流。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬陡」——潮水抬得又陡又快，一转眼漫上滩面 → 潮汐的、受潮水支配的

root: 古英语 tīd「时间、时辰」（日耳曼语重构 *tīdiz，与德语 Zeit 同源）→ 中古英语 tide 兼指海水的定时涨落 → tide + 形容词后缀 -al → tidal；*tīdiz 属构拟形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all keep one relation, 'of the tide': the phenomenon and its records, the places it governs, the power drawn from it, the strip it owns, the currents it turns, the clocks it winds, the rivers it pushes up, the rock it bulges, and finally the breath it resembles.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都守着同一个关系「属于潮汐」：现象及其记录、受它支配的地点、从它取用的动力、它拥有的地带、它反转的水流、它上弦的钟、它顶进的河流、它拉起的岩层，最后是它所比拟的一次呼吸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sea climbing and retreating along the same shore twice a day, on a schedule set by the moon.
core.cn: 核心意象：海水沿着同一道岸坡一天涨落两次，时刻由月亮定下。

branches.en: THE BASIC RELATION: first the phenomenon and its records, then the places and waters it governs.
branches.cn: 基本关系：先是现象及其记录，然后是受它支配的地点与水域。

branches.en: TIDE AS FORCE: the water that spins a turbine is the same water that reverses a channel.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为力：转动涡轮的水，与让水道掉头的水是同一股。

branches.en: THE STRIP THE TIDE OWNS: between the marks, the tide decides what may live and when.
branches.cn: 潮水拥有的地带：在两条水位线之间，潮汐决定谁能生存、何时生存。

branches.en: TIDE AS CLOCK AND AS INTRUSION: organisms keep its rhythm, and rivers feel its push upstream.
branches.cn: 潮汐作为时钟与侵入者：生物守着它的节律，河流感到它向上游的顶托。

branches.en: THE IMAGE EXTENDED: gravity raises rock, and breathing repeats like water.
branches.cn: 意象的延伸：引力拉起岩石，呼吸像水一样往复。

intro.en: Tidal is a native Germanic noun with a borrowed suffix: tide comes from Old English, while -al reached English through Latin and French and then became fully productive.
intro.cn: tidal 是日耳曼本族名词加外来后缀：tide 来自古英语，而 -al 经拉丁语与法语进入英语，随后成为能产后缀。

latinIntro.en: Only the suffix is Latin (-alis); tide itself has no Latin cognate, since it descends from Germanic *tīdiz. The Latin entries are therefore empty by design, and Latin-based look-alikes such as title belong to other roots.
latinIntro.cn: 只有后缀是拉丁的（-alis）；tide 本身来自日耳曼 *tīdiz，没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁条目按实情留空；像 title 这类拉丁系形近词属于别的词根。

items.example: High water came at the appointed tīd.
items.exampleCN: 高潮在约定的时辰到来。

items.example: The same suffix builds tidal from tide.
items.exampleCN: 同一个后缀把 tide 构成 tidal。

items.meaning: the rise and fall of the sea
items.example: The tide turned before noon.
items.exampleCN: 中午之前潮水转向了。

items.meaning: of or relating to the tide
items.example: Tidal water covered the road.
items.exampleCN: 潮水淹了这条路。

items.meaning: in a manner driven by the tide
items.example: The lagoon is flushed tidally.
items.exampleCN: 这片潟湖靠潮水冲刷。

items.example: Eelgrass grows on the tideland.
items.exampleCN: 大叶藻长在潮间地上。

items.meaning: the line of debris left by high water
items.meaningCN: 高潮退去后留下的杂物线
items.example: A tideline of plastic marked the beach.
items.exampleCN: 一道塑料垃圾的潮线划在海滩上。

items.meaning: water moved by the tide; low coastal land
items.meaningCN: 受潮水推动的水；沿海低地
items.example: Tidewater reaches the old mill pond.
items.exampleCN: 潮水能涨到那座旧磨坊的水塘。

items.meaning: a gate that keeps the tide out
items.example: The tidegate protects the low fields.
items.exampleCN: 挡潮闸保护低处的田地。

items.example: Intertidal rocks are bare at low water.
items.exampleCN: 退潮时潮间带的礁石裸露出来。

definition_zh: 恰恰相反；相反地；反之
definition_en: used to state that the opposite of something just said is true
core_image: 检测员把报告摊在桌上，指着梁上的裂缝，当场推翻「旧桥结实」的说法
scene: 有人断言旧桥还能承重，工程师翻开检测报告，指着裂缝否定了这个说法。 On the contrary, the inspection found cracks in three girders.
sceneCN: 这里用来直接否定刚提出的说法（第 1 个义项：恰恰相反）；句意为恰恰相反，检查发现三根主梁有裂缝。图中可辨识物件：检测报告、裂缝、钢梁、手电筒。

pos.zh: 副词性短语：恰恰相反；反之（用于否定刚提出的说法）

collocations.phrase: on the contrary, the opposite is true

derivatives.zh: 同一词根直接作形容词或名词，义为「相反的；反面」
由形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「相反地；固执地」
由形容词加方式词尾构成，义为「反之；相反地」
由形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「相反性；执拗」
由词根加表示人的词尾构成，义为「逆向行事者；唱反调的」

senses.title: Denying a statement just made
senses.definition: used to declare that the statement just made is false and the opposite is true
senses.definitionCN: 用来宣布刚提出的说法不成立，真实情况正相反
senses.example: The material is not brittle; on the contrary, it bends without cracking.
senses.exampleCN: 这种材料并不脆；恰恰相反，它能弯曲而不裂。
senses.why: The phrase does not add a difference, it cancels a claim and puts the opposite in its place.
senses.whyCN: 这条短语不是补充差异，而是取消一个说法，再把相反的说法放进去。

senses.title: Correcting a misconception
senses.definition: used to replace a widely held but mistaken belief with the opposite fact
senses.definitionCN: 用一个相反的事实替换普遍但错误的看法
senses.example: Most people think the desert is lifeless; on the contrary, it teems with insects after rain.
senses.exampleCN: 多数人以为沙漠没有生命；恰恰相反，雨后虫类成群。
senses.why: Correction works by naming the belief first, so the reversal has something to overturn.
senses.whyCN: 纠正先把错误看法说出来，反转才有东西可推翻。

senses.title: Strong disagreement in debate
senses.definition: used to reject an opponent's claim firmly and immediately
senses.definitionCN: 用来坚决而立即地否定对方的说法
senses.example: On the contrary, the witness gave a very different account.
senses.exampleCN: 恰恰相反，那名证人给出的说法完全不同。
senses.why: In debate the phrase carries emphasis, because it refuses the premise rather than arguing within it.
senses.whyCN: 辩论中这条短语带强调色彩，因为它拒绝前提，而不是在前提内争辩。

senses.title: After a negative clause
senses.definition: following not X, to supply Y as the true state of affairs
senses.definitionCN: 跟在「并非甲」之后，给出「实为乙」的真实情况
senses.example: The bridge was not strengthened; on the contrary, two lanes were removed.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥并未加固；恰恰相反，还拆掉了两条车道。
senses.why: The pattern not X but Y is the phrase's most common grammatical home.
senses.whyCN: 「并非甲，而是乙」是这条短语最常见的语法位置。

senses.title: A marker of formal argument
senses.definition: used in essays and reports to signal a reversal in the argument
senses.definitionCN: 在论文与报告中标记论证方向的翻转
senses.example: On the contrary, the figures show a steady decline.
senses.exampleCN: 恰恰相反，这些数字显示持续下降。
senses.why: Academic prose uses the phrase to steer the reader through a reversal, not to insult an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 学术文本用它引导读者穿过一次反转，而非攻击对手。

senses.title: Refuting an implied assumption
senses.definition: used when the claim being rejected was only implied or assumed
senses.definitionCN: 用在被否定的说法只是暗含或假定时
senses.example: On the contrary, the team had prepared for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 恰恰相反，团队早已为延误做了准备。
senses.why: An assumption can be reversed without being quoted, which makes the phrase feel sharper.
senses.whyCN: 假设不必被引用也能被反转，这使短语显得更锋利。

senses.title: Opening a paragraph
senses.definition: placed at the head of a paragraph to answer the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 放在段首，用来回应上一段
senses.example: On the contrary, later studies confirmed the earlier result.
senses.exampleCN: 恰恰相反，后来的研究证实了早先的结果。
senses.why: Paragraph-initial use turns the phrase into a hinge between two blocks of argument.
senses.whyCN: 放在段首时，这条短语成为两块论证之间的铰链。

senses.title: Asserting opposition, not mere difference
senses.titleCN: 主张相反，而非仅仅不同
senses.definition: used to insist on opposition, where a plain contrast marker would only note a difference
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调对立，而单纯的对比词只指出差异
senses.example: The old and new methods seem similar; on the contrary, they rely on opposite assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 新旧方法看似相近；恰恰相反，它们依据的假设正好相反。
senses.why: Contrast notes two things side by side, while this phrase says one cancels the other.
senses.whyCN: 对比词把两物并排，这条短语则说一方取消另一方。

intro.en: The phrase joins on and the noun contrary, from Latin contrarius, opposite, from contra, against. English took the word through Old French in the thirteenth century, and the phrase settled as a marker of reversal soon after.
intro.cn: 这条短语由介词与表示「相反」的名词组成。该名词来自拉丁语 contrarius「相反的」，源头是 contra「对着、反对」。英语在十三世纪经古法语引入这个词，整条短语随后定型为表示反转的标记。

items.en: Contra meant against or opposite, and it survives in English prefixes and legal phrases.
items.cn: 这个词意为「对着、反对」，在英语前缀与法律短语中仍有留存。

items.en: The adjective meant opposite or opposed, describing things that face each other.
items.cn: 这个形容词意为相反的、对立的，形容彼此相对之物。

items.en: French carried the adjective and noun into English, where contrary named the opposite of a thing.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词与名词带进英语，其中名词指某物的反面。

items.en: English used the word for a opposed fact as well as for a stubborn person.
items.cn: 英语用这个词指相反的事实，也用来形容固执的人。

items.era: THE PHRASE TAKES SHAPE, 14TH TO 16TH CENTURY
items.en: The prepositional phrase became a standard marker of reversal; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个介词短语成为标准的反转标记；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Later handbooks paired the phrase with its cousin to the contrary, which sits after a noun instead.
items.cn: 后来的手册把这条短语与近亲说法「相反的」并列，后者放在名词之后。

note.en: The first group shares the same root or the same frame; the second group names other ways of marking contrast.
note.cn: 第一组共享同一词根或同一框架；第二组是其他标记对比的说法。

entries.definition: A phrase that follows a noun, as in evidence to the contrary.
entries.definitionCN: 跟在名词之后的短语，如「相反的证据」。

entries.definition: Adjective or noun meaning opposite; also describing a stubborn person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，意为相反的；也形容固执的人。

entries.definition: In an opposite or perverse manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指相反地或执拗地。

entries.definition: An older adverb meaning on the other hand or in the opposite way.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的副词，意为反之或相反地。

entries.definition: A person who deliberately takes the opposite view.
entries.definitionCN: 指刻意持相反观点的人。

entries.definition: A marker that sets two things side by side without denying either.
entries.definitionCN: 把两物并置的标记，并不否定任何一方。

entries.definition: Introducing the reverse of a relation already stated.
entries.definitionCN: 引出已述关系的反向情况。

entries.definition: A balanced second view, not a denial of the first.
entries.definitionCN: 平衡地给出第二种看法，并不否定第一种。

entries.definition: In place of what was expected or proposed.
entries.definitionCN: 代替预期或提议的事物。

entries.definition: More precisely, introducing a corrected statement.
entries.definitionCN: 更准确地说，引出修正后的说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the root meaning of facing against, and the phrase's habit of cancelling a claim.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用词根「对着」的意思，以及这条短语取消说法的习惯。

normal.en: The root meant against, so the phrase puts a fact face to face with the claim it cancels.
normal.cn: 词根意为「对着」，所以这条短语让事实与它所取消的说法面对面。

normal.en: It usually follows a negative clause: not this, on the contrary that.
normal.cn: 它通常跟在否定小句之后：并非这个，恰恰相反，是那个。

normal.en: In debate it refuses the premise rather than arguing inside it.
normal.cn: 在辩论中它拒绝前提，而不是在前提里争辩。

normal.en: The cousin phrase to the contrary sits after a noun, as in evidence to the contrary.
normal.cn: 近亲短语表示「反之」，放在名词之后，例如「相反的证据」。

normal.en: A plain contrast marker only notes a difference; this phrase asserts an opposite.
normal.cn: 单纯的对比词只指出差异，这条短语则主张相反。

abstract.en: A denial that supplies a replacement is stronger than a denial that leaves a gap.
abstract.cn: 否定之后补上替代物的说法，比留下空缺的否定更有力。

abstract.en: The phrase works like a hinge: one paragraph turns on it and the next swings the other way.
abstract.cn: 这条短语像铰链：上一段绕着它转，下一段就转向另一边。

abstract.en: Opposition needs a shared subject: two claims must face each other before one can be reversed.
abstract.cn: 对立需要共同的主语：两个说法先面对面，其中一个才谈得上被反转。

examples.en: The soil is not poor; on the contrary, it is unusually rich in minerals.
examples.cn: 土壤并不贫瘠；恰恰相反，它富含矿物质。

examples.en: On the contrary, the second trial produced better results than the first.
examples.cn: 恰恰相反，第二次试验的结果比第一次更好。

examples.en: Critics expected a decline; on the contrary, demand rose sharply.
examples.cn: 批评者预料会下滑；恰恰相反，需求大幅上升。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「康雀瑞」——两个人面对面站着，各说反话，就是「恰恰相反」：恰恰相反、反之

root: 这个词经古法语来自拉丁语 contrarius「相反的」，源头是 contra「对着、反对」；这条短语在十四至十六世纪定型为反转标记，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses range from denying a statement, through correcting a belief and winning a debate, to opening a paragraph and asserting true opposition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从否定一句话，经过纠正误解、赢下辩论，走到开启段落与主张真正的对立。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an inspection report opened on a table, a crack circled in red, and a confident claim left in ruins.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开的检测报告、圈红的裂缝，以及被推翻的自信说法。

branches.en: THE CANCELLED CLAIM: after a negative clause, the phrase supplies the true opposite.
branches.cn: 被取消的说法：跟在否定小句之后，给出真正的相反情况。

branches.en: THE CORRECTED BELIEF: a misconception or an unspoken assumption is reversed.
branches.cn: 被纠正的看法：误解或未说出的假设被反转。

branches.en: THE DEBATE AND THE ESSAY: firm rejection in argument, formal reversal in writing.
branches.cn: 辩论与论文：论证中的坚决否定，写作中的正式反转。

branches.en: THE PARAGRAPH HINGE: the phrase opens a paragraph that answers the last one.
branches.cn: 段落铰链：短语开启一段，回应上一段。

branches.en: THE TRUE OPPOSITE: not a difference noted, but an opposition asserted.
branches.cn: 真正的相反：不是指出差异，而是主张对立。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin word for facing against, so its force is opposition rather than comparison.
intro.cn: 这条短语立在一个表示「对着」的拉丁词上，力量来自对立而非比较。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies contra and its adjective; Old French carried both into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「对着」的词及其形容词；古法语把两者带进英语。

items.example: It survives in English compounds and legal phrases.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语复合词与法律短语中留存。

items.example: The adjective describes things facing each other.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词形容彼此相对之物。

items.example: French carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带进英语。

items.example: The word names what stands against a claim.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指与某说法相对的东西。

items.example: It forms the adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: 它构成方式副词。

items.meaning: in the stated direction or way
items.example: It forms an older adverb meaning conversely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成较早的副词，意为反之。

items.example: It forms the word for a deliberate dissenter.
items.exampleCN: 它构成指刻意唱反调者的词。

items.example: It opens the fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它引出这条固定短语。

items.example: The cousin phrase follows a noun instead.
items.exampleCN: 近亲短语改为跟在名词之后。

items.example: The whole phrase cancels a claim.
items.exampleCN: 整条短语取消一个说法。

definition_zh: n. 鳄鱼；成队行走的人
definition_en: a large river reptile with a long body and strong jaws
core_image: 只露出眼睛和鼻孔的鳞背浮在水面
scene: 鳄鱼只把眼睛露出水面。 The crocodile showed only its eyes above the water.

pos.zh: 鳄鱼；成队行进的人

senses.title: The reptile
senses.definition: a large reptile that lives in rivers
senses.definitionCN: 生活在河里的大型爬行动物
senses.example: The crocodile waited by the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 鳄鱼在岸边等候。
senses.why: Two eyes above still water.
senses.whyCN: 静水上的一双眼睛。

senses.title: Its skin
senses.definition: the skin or leather of this animal
senses.definitionCN: 这种动物的皮或皮革
senses.example: Her bag is made of crocodile.

definition_zh: 受挫的；沮丧的；受阻的；未能实现的
definition_en: blocked in what one is trying to do, and therefore annoyed or discouraged
core_image: 木工第三次把榫头对着榫眼推去，总是差半毫米，木屑粘在手背上
scene: 车间里的老师傅第三次把同一块木料放回台面，榫头总是差半毫米塞不进去，他摘下护目镜揉了揉眼睛。 The frustrated carpenter set the chisel down when the joint refused to close.
sceneCN: 这里 frustrated 指「因反复受阻而恼火又无力」（第 1 个义项：计划在半路被挡住）；句意为榫头就是合不上，这位受挫的木工把凿子放了下来。

pos.zh: 受挫的；沮丧的；未能实现的；受阻的

senses.title: Stopped halfway in a plan
senses.definition: prevented from carrying out an intention that was already under way
senses.definitionCN: 已经着手进行的意图被阻止继续
senses.example: The team felt frustrated when the permit arrived a month late.
senses.exampleCN: 许可晚到一个月，团队感到受挫。
senses.why: The word is the past participle of a verb meaning 'to make vain', so it describes an effort already made vain.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是意为「使成徒劳」的动词的过去分词，因此描写一次已被弄成空的努力。

senses.title: Annoyed at being blocked
senses.definition: irritated and short-tempered because something keeps standing in the way
senses.definitionCN: 因为总有东西挡在路上而烦躁、易怒
senses.example: He grew frustrated with the same error appearing on every page.
senses.exampleCN: 每页都出现同一个错误，他越来越恼火。
senses.why: Repeated blocking turns the disappointment into temper, and the adjective carries both at once.
senses.whyCN: 反复受阻把失望变成脾气，而这个形容词同时带着两者。

senses.title: Unsuccessful, as an attempt
senses.definition: describing an effort that did not achieve what it set out to do
senses.definitionCN: 形容没有达到既定目标的努力
senses.example: Three frustrated attempts later, they changed the whole method.
senses.exampleCN: 三次未成功的尝试之后，他们换掉了整套方法。
senses.why: Here the participle modifies the attempt itself rather than the person, keeping only the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里分词修饰的是尝试本身而不是人，只保留结果这一层。

senses.title: Sexually unsatisfied
senses.definition: a polite or clinical way of saying that physical desire has no outlet
senses.definitionCN: 委婉或临床地表示生理欲望没有出口
senses.example: The counsellor asked whether either partner felt frustrated.
senses.exampleCN: 咨询师问双方是否有人感到需求未被满足。
senses.why: The core image of blocked energy is applied to the body, and the wording stays deliberately indirect.
senses.whyCN: 受阻能量的核心意象被用到身体上，措辞刻意保持间接。

senses.title: Made void by events, in law
senses.definition: describing an agreement that cannot be performed because circumstances have changed fundamentally
senses.definitionCN: 形容因情况根本改变而无法履行的协议
senses.example: The contract was held frustrated when the port closed for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 港口封闭一年，该合同被认定落空。
senses.why: The legal phrase keeps the oldest meaning: an obligation reduced to nothing without anyone's fault.
senses.whyCN: 法律说法保留了最古老的意思：在无人有过错的情况下义务化为乌有。

senses.title: Creatively stifled
senses.definition: describing an artist or writer whose ability is held back by conditions rather than by lack of skill
senses.definitionCN: 形容艺术家或写作者的能力被环境而非技艺所限
senses.example: A frustrated painter, he spent ten years drawing advertisements.
senses.exampleCN: 作为一个才华受压抑的画家，他画了十年广告。
senses.why: The block is no longer a single task but a whole career, and the adjective describes a person held in place.
senses.whyCN: 阻碍不再是单项任务，而是整个职业，形容词描写一个被按住不动的人。

senses.title: Impatient with slow progress
senses.definition: restless because improvement is arriving more slowly than expected
senses.definitionCN: 因改善比预期来得慢而焦躁
senses.example: Readers grew frustrated with the story's slow middle section.
senses.exampleCN: 读者对这故事缓慢的中段越来越不耐。
senses.why: Time itself becomes the obstacle, and impatience is the shape frustration takes when nothing is actively blocking.
senses.whyCN: 时间本身成了障碍；当没有谁在主动阻挡时，挫败就表现为不耐。

senses.title: With expectations unmet
senses.definition: disappointed because what was hoped for did not arrive
senses.definitionCN: 因为所希望的事没有到来而失望
senses.example: The audience left frustrated after the promised discussion was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 承诺的讨论被取消，观众失望地离开。
senses.why: Here the block is between hope and outcome, with no effort at all required.
senses.whyCN: 这里阻碍位于希望与结果之间，根本不需要付出努力。

intro.en: Frustrated is the past participle of the verb frustrate, used as an adjective. The verb goes back to a Latin participle meaning 'brought to nothing'.
intro.cn: frustrated 是动词 frustrate 的过去分词，被用作形容词。这个动词可上溯到拉丁语中意为「被弄成空」的分词。

items.en: The adverb meant 'in vain'; every later form in the family carries its verdict of wasted effort.
items.cn: 这个副词意为「徒然」；词族里后出的每个形式都带着它对努力的判决。

items.en: The past participle of the verb meant 'disappointed, deceived, made vain'. English took the participle stem and built its own verb on it.
items.cn: 该动词的过去分词意为「被使失望、被欺骗、被弄成空」。英语取了这个分词词干，在它之上造出自己的动词。

items.en: The English verb first meant 'to bring to nothing, to balk', and only later acquired the milder sense of causing annoyance.
items.cn: 英语动词最初意为「使成空、使受阻」，后来才获得「使人恼火」这个较轻的意思。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the participle settled into regular use as an adjective for a person whose plans are blocked.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，这个分词稳定地用作形容词，指计划被挡住的人。

items.en: Law fixed the phrase for a contract made impossible, and medicine adopted the word for unmet physical desire.
items.cn: 法律固定了「合同无法履行」的说法，医学则采用这个词指未被满足的生理欲望。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the 'in vain' adverb is not established, and its supposed link to the Latin word for fraud remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：意为「徒然」的那个副词的更早来源没有定论，它与拉丁语中指欺诈的词之间的所谓联系仍属假说。

note.en: The first group holds the forms of one verb that are constantly swapped; the second holds other words for being held back.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个动词的各种形式，常被互换；第二组是其他表示「被按住」的词。

entries.definition: It describes the task or situation that produces the feeling; saying 'I am frustrating' reverses the direction.
entries.definitionCN: 它描写产生感受的任务或处境；说「我很令人受挫」就把方向反了。

entries.definition: The state or the obstacle itself, where the adjective names the person who is in that state.
entries.definitionCN: 指状态或障碍本身，而形容词指处在那种状态中的人。

entries.definition: From a verb of uncertain origin meaning 'to make flushed or confused'; it is about agitation, not about a blocked goal.
entries.definitionCN: 来自一个来源不确定的动词，意为「使脸红、使慌乱」；它说的是慌乱，而不是目标受阻。

entries.definition: The base verb, active in form: it needs an object, as in 'the delay frustrated us'.
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词，形式上主动：需要宾语，例如「延误让我们受挫」。

entries.definition: It usually implies a person or force deliberately defeating the plan.
entries.definitionCN: 通常暗含有人或某种力量刻意破坏了计划。

entries.definition: It stresses loss of confidence rather than the barrier, and can exist with no obstacle at all.
entries.definitionCN: 强调信心丧失而非障碍，甚至可以毫无障碍地存在。

entries.definition: It pictures something pressed down so it cannot grow, close to the creative sense of frustrated.
entries.definitionCN: 画面是被按住而无法生长，接近 frustrated 的「才华受压抑」义。

entries.definition: A lighter, more general word for irritation, with no blocked effort behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 更轻、更泛的恼怒用词，背后没有受阻的努力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The ending marks a past participle, so the word says 'I have been made vain', not 'I make others vain'.
normal.cn: 词尾标明这是过去分词，所以它说的是「我被弄成空」，而不是「我让别人空」。

normal.en: The family runs frustrate, frustrated, frustrating, frustration, frustratedly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 frustrate、frustrated、frustrating、frustration、frustratedly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the target: frustrated with a person, frustrated by delays, left frustrated.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：对某人不满、因延误受挫、被弄得灰心。

normal.en: Law pairs the word with contract; medicine pairs it with an unmet physical need.
normal.cn: 法律把它与合同搭配；医学把它与未被满足的生理需求搭配。

normal.en: The base verb is active and takes an object, while the participle describes a state.
normal.cn: 基础动词是主动的、带宾语，而分词描写一种状态。

abstract.en: Picture a key that fits the lock but turns a quarter turn short.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙插得进去，却总差四分之一圈转不到底。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose last step is missing.
abstract.cn: 想象一段楼梯，最后一阶不见了。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of water that will not quite reach the boil.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅水，怎么也到不了沸点。

examples.en: She was frustrated that nobody had answered her email.
examples.cn: 没人回她的邮件，她感到很受挫。

examples.en: The frustrated passengers waited three hours on the platform.
examples.cn: 受挫的乘客在站台上等了三个小时。

examples.en: His frustrated ambition found an outlet in night classes.
examples.cn: 他那受压抑的抱负在夜校里找到了出口。

dict_mnemonic.text: frustr（徒然）+ ated（已经如此）＝ 力气使过、结果成空 → 受挫的、沮丧的。

root: 拉丁 frustratus「被使失望、被弄成空」，来自 frustrari，再上溯副词 frustra「徒然」；更深来源不确定。英语以这个过去分词为基础，既造出动词，也直接用作形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one blocked effort. What is blocked may be a plan, a temper, an attempt, a body, a contract, a career, an expectation of speed, or a hope, and each time the word reports that something was already set in motion and could not finish.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次受阻的努力展开。被挡住的可以是计划、脾气、尝试、身体、合同、职业、对速度的期待，或一份希望；每次这个词都说明某件事已经启动却没能走完。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that has already pushed, against a door that will not move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手已经推出去，门却不动。

branches.en: THE PUSH AND THE TEMPER: being stopped and being angry about it are two moments of one event.
branches.cn: 推与脾气：被挡住和为此发火，是同一件事的两个时刻。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF NOT ARRIVING: an effort that fails, and a hope that never lands.
branches.cn: 两种未抵达：失败的尝试，与从未落地的希望。

branches.en: BLOCKED IN THE BODY: the same picture applied to desire, and said as indirectly as possible.
branches.cn: 身体里的受阻：同一幅画面被用到欲望上，并尽可能说得间接。

branches.en: BLOCKED BY EVENTS: the law keeps the oldest reading, an obligation emptied without fault.
branches.cn: 被情势挡住：法律保留了最古老的读法，义务在无人有过错时被掏空。

branches.en: HELD DOWN OVER TIME: a career pressed flat, and impatience when the block is only slowness.
branches.cn: 在时间中被按住：被压平的职业，以及当阻碍只是「慢」时的不耐。

intro.en: Frustrated is a verb participle doing adjective work, so its ending tells the reader that the person is the one affected.
intro.cn: frustrated 是做形容词工作的动词分词，词尾告诉读者：受影响的是这个人。

latinIntro.en: The Latin participle ending marks something already done to the subject; the same stem also yields the noun of state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁分词词尾标明某事已经落在主语身上；同一词干还产出表状态的名词。

items.example: The adverb supplies the verdict of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词提供了整个词族的判决。

items.example: The ending shows that the state was imposed, not chosen.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾表明该状态是被加上的，而非自己选的。

items.example: The frustrated carpenter put down the chisel.

items.meaning: with a sense of being blocked

items.exampleCN: 她沮丧地摇了摇头。

scene: 入夏第三个星期，柏油路面整夜不凉，气象站连续多日测到异常高温。 The heat wave held the city for twelve days without a storm.
