senses.title: A spell of lasting heat
senses.definition: a period of abnormally hot weather that lasts several days and nights
senses.definitionCN: 连续数日数夜异常炎热的天气时段
senses.example: The heat wave lasted ten days and broke the July record.
senses.exampleCN: 这场热浪持续十天，打破了七月的纪录。
senses.why: The two halves of the compound simply name heat and a rolling swell, so the phrase begins as weather seen as something rolling in.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词的两半只是「热」与「涌动的浪」，所以它最初把天气看成一波涌来的东西。

senses.title: A recorded heat event
senses.definition: a heat wave that has been measured, dated and entered in climate records
senses.definitionCN: 已被测量、标注日期并录入气候记录的热浪
senses.example: The nineteen thirty-six heat wave is still the benchmark for the region.
senses.exampleCN: 一九三六年的那场热浪至今仍是该地区的基准。
senses.why: Once weather stations keep daily logs, a spell of heat becomes an event with dates and numbers.
senses.whyCN: 气象站一旦逐日记录，一段高温就变成有日期、有数字的事件。

senses.title: An official heat alert
senses.definition: a public warning issued when a heat wave is expected to endanger health
senses.definitionCN: 预计热浪将危害健康时发布的公共警报
senses.example: The weather service issued a heat wave alert for the whole province.
senses.exampleCN: 气象部门向全省发布了热浪警报。
senses.why: Forecasting made the phrase a trigger for action, so it now names the warning as well as the weather.
senses.whyCN: 预报使这个说法成为行动的信号，于是它既指天气，也指那条警报。

senses.title: Heat trapped in a city
senses.definition: the intensified heat that a city experiences because concrete, asphalt and traffic hold the day's warmth
senses.definitionCN: 城市因混凝土、柏油与车流存住白天的热量而承受的更强炎热
senses.example: The city heat wave kept night-time temperatures above thirty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 城市热浪使夜间气温一直高于三十度。
senses.why: The same phrase shifts from the air above a region to the air inside a built-up area, where surfaces store heat.
senses.whyCN: 同一个说法从区域上空转到建成区内部，那里的地表把热量存了下来。

senses.title: A warm spell in the sea
senses.definition: a prolonged period when sea surface temperatures stay far above the long-term average
senses.definitionCN: 海表温度长时间远高于长期平均值的时段
senses.example: A marine heat wave bleached the reef in a single season.
senses.exampleCN: 一场海洋热浪在一个季节里就使珊瑚礁白化。
senses.why: Oceanographers borrowed the weather phrase because warm water spreads and lingers like a dome of hot air.
senses.whyCN: 海洋学家借用了这个天气说法，因为暖水扩散、滞留的样子像一顶热空气罩。

senses.title: A sudden surge of anything
senses.definition: a short period in which an activity, feeling or rumour spreads widely and fast
senses.definitionCN: 某种活动、情绪或传闻在短时间内广泛迅速扩散的时期
senses.example: A heat wave of rumours swept the office before the audit.
senses.exampleCN: 审计之前，一阵传闻的热潮扫过办公室。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century usage let wave mean any surging movement, and the compound followed it into figurative weather.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的用法让「浪」可以指任何涌动的势头，这个复合词便跟着进入比喻性的天气。

senses.title: A summer remembered by its deaths
senses.definition: a heat wave so severe that a city or country names it and remembers its death toll
senses.definitionCN: 严重到被城市或国家命名、并被记住死亡人数的热浪
senses.example: The named heat wave killed hundreds of elderly residents.
senses.exampleCN: 那场被命名的热浪夺走了数百名老年居民的生命。
senses.why: Extreme events enter public memory with a name, the way storms do, so a deadly summer becomes a proper event.
senses.whyCN: 极端事件会像风暴一样带着名字进入公共记忆，于是致命的盛夏成了一个专名事件。

senses.title: A public health crisis period
senses.definition: a stretch of heat during which hospitals, power grids and emergency services are strained
senses.definitionCN: 医院、电网与急救系统都承受压力的一段高温时期
senses.example: During the heat wave hospitals admitted twice the usual number of patients.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪期间，医院收治的病人是平常的两倍。
senses.why: The phrase ends up naming not the temperature but the burden it places on a whole society.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法最终指的不是温度本身，而是它压在整个社会身上的负担。

intro.en: Heat wave is a native English compound. Its first half comes from Old English hǣtu, heat, and its second half from Old English wǣg, a moving swell of water. The compound itself is a mid-nineteenth-century formation; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这是英语本族复合词。前一半来自古英语「hǣtu」「热」，后一半来自古英语「wǣg」「移动的水浪」。复合词本身是十九世纪中叶的构造，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old English hǣtu named heat itself, a native Germanic word with no Latin ancestor.
items.cn: 古英语「hǣtu」指热本身，是日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先。

items.en: Old English wǣg first meant a moving swell of water, the ridge that rolls and lifts.
items.cn: 古英语「wǣg」最初指移动的水浪，即起伏涌起的那道浪脊。

items.en: In the nineteenth century wave extended from water to any surging movement, including a spell of weather.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个「浪」词从水面扩展到任何涌动的势头，包括一段天气。

items.en: Heat wave appeared as a compound in the mid-nineteenth century; the exact year of first use is uncertain.
items.cn: 「热浪」这个复合词在十九世纪中叶出现，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Weather services later turned the phrase into an official category with thresholds, forecasts and warnings.
items.cn: 气象部门后来把这个说法变成带有阈值、预报与警报的官方类别。

items.en: Climate research extended it to ocean heat waves, and everyday speech lent it to any sudden surge.
items.cn: 气候研究把它扩展到海洋热浪，日常说法又把它借给任何突然的涌潮。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like heat wave; the second group names neighbouring ideas of hot spells and heat warnings.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「heat wave」相近；第二组是与「酷热期、高温警报」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The same weather event written as one word, a spelling that became common in the twentieth century.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个天气事件的合写形式，这种拼法在二十世纪变得常见。

entries.definition: High temperature itself, the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 指高温本身，是复合词的前一半。

entries.definition: A raised ridge moving across water, and by extension any surging movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指在水面移动的浪脊，引申指任何涌动的势头。

entries.definition: Made warm, or made intense and angry, as in a heated argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指被加热的，也指激烈愤怒的，如激烈的争论。

entries.definition: A stretch of hot weather, usually shorter and less technical than a heat wave.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段炎热天气，通常比热浪短，也更口语。

entries.definition: A persistent high-pressure system that traps hot air beneath it and causes a heat wave.
entries.definitionCN: 指滞留的高压系统把热空气压在下方，从而造成热浪。

entries.definition: An informal word for an extremely hot day.
entries.definitionCN: 指极热一天的口语说法。

entries.definition: A public notice that dangerous heat is expected, close to the official sense of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 指预报危险高温的公共通告，接近这个词的官方义。

entries.definition: The ocean version of the phenomenon, with water instead of air as the hot medium.
entries.definitionCN: 指这一现象的海洋版本，热的介质是水而不是空气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two native halves of the compound, its real records and its real weather phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个复合词两个本族成分、真实记录与真实气象搭配。

normal.en: Heat plus wave: hot air arriving like a swell that rolls over a city and will not retreat.
normal.cn: 热加浪：热空气像一道涌浪压过城市，迟迟不退。

normal.en: Both halves are Old English, so the phrase is native rather than borrowed from Latin.
normal.cn: 两个成分都来自古英语，所以这个说法是本族的，不是从拉丁语借来的。

normal.en: A heat wave warning is the fixed phrase you hear on the radio before a dangerous summer day.
normal.cn: 热浪警报是危险夏日来临前收音机里会出现的固定说法。

normal.en: Marine heat wave is the scientific use, measuring warm ocean water rather than hot air.
normal.cn: 海洋热浪是科学用法，量的是温暖海水而不是热空气。

normal.en: The compound is only a mid-nineteenth-century formation, younger than the two words inside it.
normal.cn: 这个复合词只是十九世纪中叶才形成的，比它里面的两个词年轻得多。

abstract.en: A heat wave is weather with a lid on it: the air cannot rise and cannot leave.
abstract.cn: 热浪是被盖住的天气：空气既升不上去，也走不掉。

abstract.en: A city in a heat wave becomes an oven that keeps its own warmth after sunset.
abstract.cn: 热浪中的城市成了一口日落后仍存着自己热量的烤箱。

abstract.en: Any rumour can arrive as a heat wave: brief, wide, and impossible to escape while it lasts.
abstract.cn: 任何传闻都可能像热浪一样到来：短暂、广泛，在它持续时无处可躲。

examples.en: The heat wave forced the city to open cooling centres.
examples.cn: 这场热浪迫使城市开放避暑中心。

examples.en: Scientists counted a marine heat wave off the coast last summer.
examples.cn: 科学家去年夏天记录了近岸的一场海洋热浪。

examples.en: A heat wave of protest followed the announcement.
examples.cn: 公告发布之后，一阵抗议的热潮随之而来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「希特 威夫」——热到空气都翻起了浪：热浪，也用来说一阵突然涌来的热潮。

root: 英语本族复合词：前一半来自古英语「hǣtu」「热」，后一半来自古英语「wǣg」「移动的水浪」；「wave」在十九世纪扩展为「一阵涌动」，复合词于十九世纪中叶出现，确切首见年代不确定。两个成分皆属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a plain weather spell to the official alert, the city and the ocean, a figurative surge, a named deadly summer, and a period of public health strain.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的天气时段走向官方警报、城市与海洋、比喻性的涌潮、被命名的致命盛夏，以及公共卫生承压的时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broad dome of hot air sits over a city for days while the pavement never cools.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶宽大的热空气罩连日压在城上，路面始终不凉。

branches.en: THE SPELL: hot air arrives and stays, day and night, until records fall.
branches.cn: 高温时段：热空气来了就留下，日夜不退，直到纪录被打破。

branches.en: THE RECORD AND THE WARNING: the spell is measured, dated and then announced to the public.
branches.cn: 记录与警报：这段高温被测量、标注日期，随后向公众发布。

branches.en: THE BUILT AND THE WATERY: surfaces store heat in a city, and warm water spreads across a reef.
branches.cn: 建成区与水域：城市地表存住热量，暖水则铺过珊瑚礁。

branches.en: THE FIGURATIVE SURGE: rumour or feeling spreads like hot air, wide and fast.
branches.cn: 比喻涌潮：传闻或情绪像热空气一样广而快地散开。

branches.en: THE DEADLY SUMMER: a named event, its death toll, and the hospitals and grids under strain.
branches.cn: 致命盛夏：被命名的事件、它的死亡人数，以及承压的医院与电网。

intro.en: Heat wave is a Germanic compound, so its parts are native English words rather than Latin stems.
intro.cn: 这是一个日耳曼语复合词，各部分是本族英语词，而不是拉丁词干。

latinIntro.en: Both components are inherited Germanic words, so there is no Latin counterpart to list here.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都是日耳曼语继承下来的本族词，因此这里没有可列的拉丁同族。

items.example: The word named the feeling of fire and summer.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指火与夏天带来的那种感觉。

items.example: It described water lifting and rolling forward.
items.exampleCN: 它描述水面抬升、向前翻卷的样子。

items.example: The first half of the compound is this everyday noun.
items.exampleCN: 复合词的前一半就是这个日常名词。

items.meaning: a raised ridge on water; a surge
items.meaningCN: 水面上的浪脊；一阵涌动
items.example: The second half carries the idea of rolling movement.
items.exampleCN: 后一半带着翻滚移动的意思。

items.meaning: a lasting spell of hot weather
items.example: The compound is the ordinary name for the event.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是这一事件的日常名称。

items.meaning: the same event written as one word
items.meaningCN: 同一事件写成一词的形式
items.example: Newspapers often close the compound up.
items.exampleCN: 报纸常把这个复合词合写。

items.example: It marks the plural of the whole phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它标出整个词组里的复数。

items.structure: English adjective from Old English hāt
items.example: The adjective supplies the family word for hot days.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供了表示炎热日子的同族词。

items.example: It names the period that the heat fills.
items.exampleCN: 它指被高温填满的那段时期。

derivatives.zh: 由「热」与「浪」合写成一词构成，义为「热浪」
由「热」加已然词尾构成，义为「加热的；激烈的」
由「热」的动词加名词尾构成，义为「供暖；加热」
由同一名词转作动词构成，义为「加热」

definition_zh: 三角洲；希腊字母第四个字母；三角形物；变化量；三角翼
definition_en: the triangular land at a river's mouth, or a triangular shape, letter or amount of change
core_image: 河流入海处分成许多支流，泥沙堆出一个三角形
scene: 河流在入海处分成许多支流，铺开成三角洲。 The river splits into many arms across the delta.
sceneCN: 这里该词指「河流入海处由泥沙堆成的三角形陆地」（第 1 个义项：三角洲）；句意为河流分成许多支流，铺展成三角洲。

pos.zh: 三角洲；三角符号；变化量

senses.title: Triangular land at a river mouth
senses.titleCN: 三角洲：河流入海处的三角形陆地
senses.definition: the triangular area of sediment built where a river enters a sea or lake
senses.definitionCN: 河流入海或入湖处由沉积物堆成的三角形区域
senses.example: The river splits into many arms across the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 河流分成许多支流，铺展成三角洲。
senses.why: Greek geographers saw the triangular mouth of the Nile and named it after the fourth letter, which has the same shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊地理学者看到尼罗河口的三角形，便用形状相同的第四个字母为它命名。

senses.title: The fourth Greek letter
senses.titleCN: 希腊字母表的第四个字母
senses.definition: the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, written as a triangle
senses.definitionCN: 希腊字母表的第四个字母，写作三角形
senses.example: The symbol delta marks the change in a formula.
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号在公式中标记变化量。
senses.why: The letter itself is triangular, which is why it could name the landform.
senses.whyCN: 这个字母本身就是三角形，因此能给这种地形命名。

senses.title: A triangular object or mark
senses.definition: something shaped like a triangle or marked with one
senses.definitionCN: 三角形的东西或带三角标记之物
senses.example: A delta sign warns of a changing road surface.
senses.exampleCN: 三角标志提醒路面正在变化。
senses.why: The letter's shape became a general name for triangular marks.
senses.whyCN: 字母的形状成为三角形标记的通称。

senses.title: A triangular aircraft wing
senses.definition: a triangular wing shape used on some aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 某些飞机采用的三角形机翼
senses.example: The delta wing gives lift at high speed.
senses.exampleCN: 三角翼在高速时提供升力。
senses.why: Aviation named the wing after the letter's outline.
senses.whyCN: 航空按字母的轮廓命名这种机翼。

senses.title: A change in mathematics
senses.titleCN: 数学与物理中的变化量
senses.definition: a finite amount of change in a variable, shown by the letter
senses.definitionCN: 变量有限的变化量，用该字母表示
senses.example: The equation uses delta for a small change in time.
senses.exampleCN: 方程用该符号表示时间的微小变化。
senses.why: Mathematics adopted the letter as a standard sign for difference or change.
senses.whyCN: 数学采用这个字母作为差异或变化的标准符号。

senses.title: Delta wetlands
senses.definition: the wet, sediment-rich environment of a delta
senses.definitionCN: 三角洲含泥沙丰富的湿地环境
senses.example: The delta supports reeds, fish and nesting birds.
senses.exampleCN: 三角洲养育着芦苇、鱼类与筑巢的鸟。
senses.why: Fresh sediment and shallow water make a delta one of the richest habitats.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜泥沙与浅水使三角洲成为最富饶的栖息地之一。

senses.title: The delta plain
senses.definition: the low, built-up plain of sediment at a river mouth
senses.definitionCN: 河口处由沉积物堆高的低平原
senses.example: Farmers grow rice on the delta plain.
senses.exampleCN: 农民在三角洲平原上种稻。
senses.why: Geology treats the deposit as a body of sediment with its own layers and front.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把这片沉积当作有自身层次与前缘的沉积体。

senses.title: The delta region
senses.definition: the settled region around a delta
senses.definitionCN: 三角洲周边的居住地区
senses.example: Cities in the delta region are sinking as the ground compacts.
senses.exampleCN: 三角洲地区的城市因地面压实而下沉。
senses.why: Rich soil and water make deltas crowded, so the word also names a human region.
senses.whyCN: 肥沃土壤与水源使三角洲人口密集，因此这个词也指人文区域。

intro.en: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, named after a Phoenician letter shaped like a triangle; Greek geographers applied it to the Nile mouth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词是希腊字母表的第四个字母，得名于一个三角形形状的腓尼基字母；希腊地理学者把它用于尼罗河口。年代均为约数。

items.en: delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, and its capital form is a triangle.
items.cn: 这是希腊字母表的第四个字母，其大写形式是一个三角形。

items.en: The letter goes back to a Phoenician letter called daleth, meaning 'door', whose outline was triangular.
items.cn: 这个字母可追溯到腓尼基语中一个意为「门」的字母，其轮廓是三角形。

items.en: Greek geographers called the triangular mouth of the Nile the delta, and the name spread to similar river mouths.
items.cn: 希腊地理学者把尼罗河的三角形河口称为这个名称，它随后传播到类似的河口。

items.en: Mathematics adopted the letter as a standard sign for a finite change or difference.
items.cn: 数学采用这个字母作为有限变化或差异的标准符号。

items.en: Aviation named a triangular wing after the letter's outline.
items.cn: 航空按字母的轮廓命名三角形机翼。

items.en: Source uncertain (the Phoenician link): the deeper origin of the letter name is not fully settled, and dates are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（腓尼基环节）：字母名称的更早来历尚无定论，年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the same letter or triangle idea; group two holds the river-mouth landforms often compared with a delta.
note.cn: 第一组是来自同一字母或三角形观念的形近词；第二组是常与三角洲比较的河口地形。

entries.definition: A triangular shoulder muscle; the name comes from the letter's shape, not from a river.
entries.definitionCN: 指三角形的肩部肌肉；名称来自字母形状，与河流无关。

entries.definition: Relating to a river delta; it is the adjective while the noun names the landform.
entries.definitionCN: 指与河流三角洲有关的；它是形容词，而名词指地形。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun, used for more than one delta or letter.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，用于多个三角洲或字母。

entries.definition: The tidal mouth of a river where fresh and salt water meet; a delta is built of sediment, while an estuary is scoured by tides.
entries.definitionCN: 指淡水与咸水相遇的潮汐河口；三角洲由沉积物堆成，河口湾则受潮流冲刷。

entries.definition: A fan-shaped deposit where a stream leaves a mountain; it is built on land, not at the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 指溪流离开山地时形成的扇形沉积；它在陆上堆积，不在海边。

entries.definition: Flat land beside a river that floods; it is along the channel, not at its mouth.
entries.definitionCN: 指河边会泛滥的平地；它沿河道分布，不在河口。

entries.definition: The place where a river meets a larger body of water; it is the general term for the location.
entries.definitionCN: 指河流与较大水域相接之处；它是这个位置的通用说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The letter is a triangle, and the landform copies the letter.
normal.cn: 这个字母是三角形，而地形复制了这个字母。

normal.en: The family runs delta, deltas, deltaic, deltaic plain and delta wing.
normal.cn: 同族词包括本词、复数、三角洲形容词、三角洲平原与三角翼。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: the Nile Delta, a river delta, delta wing, a delta change.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：尼罗河三角洲、河流三角洲、三角翼、变化量。

normal.en: Mathematics uses the letter for a small change, which is why formulas are full of deltas.
normal.cn: 数学用这个字母表示微小变化，因此公式里常见它。

normal.en: A delta is built by sediment, while an estuary is carved by tides.
normal.cn: 三角洲由沉积物堆成，河口湾则由潮流冲刷。

abstract.en: Picture a triangle of sand spreading into blue water.
abstract.cn: 想象一片三角形沙地铺进蓝色水中。

abstract.en: Picture a river opening its hand into many fingers at the sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河在海边张开手掌，分成许多手指。

abstract.en: Picture a small change marked in the margin of an equation.
abstract.cn: 想象方程边注里标出的一个小变化。

examples.en: The delta grows every year as the river drops new sediment.
examples.cn: 河流每年带来新泥沙，三角洲因此不断扩大。

examples.en: The delta wing keeps the aircraft stable at high speed.
examples.cn: 三角翼让飞机在高速时保持稳定。

examples.en: A delta marks the difference between the two readings.
examples.cn: 这个符号标出两次读数之间的差值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「德尔塔」：希腊字母第几？第四，形状像三角形，正好像河口三角洲。

root: 希腊字母表第四个字母，其大写为三角形，源自腓尼基语意为「门」的字母；希腊地理学者用它命名尼罗河的三角形河口。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one triangle. The shape is a letter, a sign, a wing and a mark; the landform at a river mouth gives the wetland, the sediment plain and the settled region.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个三角形展开。这个形状是字母、符号、机翼与标记；河口的三角形地形则给出湿地、沉积平原与居住地区。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a triangle of sediment opening into water, the same outline as the fourth Greek letter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片三角形沉积物伸进水中，轮廓与希腊第四个字母相同。

branches.en: LANDFORM: the river mouth builds a wetland and a sedimentary plain.
branches.cn: 地形：河口堆出湿地与沉积平原。

branches.en: SYMBOL: the letter and any triangular mark share the shape.
branches.cn: 符号：字母与任何三角标记共享这个形状。

branches.en: WING: aviation copies the triangle for a wing plan.
branches.cn: 机翼：航空把三角形复制为机翼平面。

branches.en: CHANGE: mathematics uses the letter for a finite difference.
branches.cn: 变化：数学用这个字母表示有限差值。

branches.en: REGION: rich soil and water make the delta a settled place.
branches.cn: 地区：肥沃土壤与水源使三角洲成为居住地。

intro.en: Delta is a letter name of Phoenician origin, not a Latin root; most English uses are compounds or technical terms.
intro.cn: 该词是源自腓尼基语的字母名称，并非拉丁词根；英语用法多为复合词或技术术语。

latinIntro.en: There is no native Latin root: Latin only borrowed the Greek letter name, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 没有本族拉丁词根：拉丁语只借入了这个希腊字母名称，因此拉丁词条列表留空。

items.example: The old letter name described a triangular outline.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老字母名描述三角形轮廓。

items.example: The river splits into many arms across the delta.
items.exampleCN: 河流分成许多支流，铺展成三角洲。

items.example: The coast has three large deltas.
items.exampleCN: 这段海岸有三个大三角洲。

items.example: Deltaic sediment is fine and rich.
items.exampleCN: 三角洲沉积细而肥沃。

items.meaning: the low plain of a delta
items.example: Rice grows on the deltaic plain.
items.exampleCN: 稻米种在三角洲平原上。

items.meaning: the seaward edge of a delta
items.example: Waves rework the delta front.
items.exampleCN: 波浪改造三角洲前缘。

items.example: The delta wing gives lift at high speed.
items.exampleCN: 三角翼在高速时提供升力。

items.example: The delta variant spread quickly.
items.exampleCN: 这一变体传播得很快。

definition_zh: 时间顺序；按年代先后的排列顺序
definition_en: an arrangement of events or items according to the order in which they occurred in time
core_image: 一串纸牌按年份从左到右摊开，最早的摆在最左端，年号依次递增
scene: 修复师把散落的信件按年份从最早排到最晚，再依时间顺序装订成册。 The conservator laid the scattered letters out from the earliest year to the latest, then bound them into a volume in chronological order.
sceneCN: 这里 chronological order 指「按时间先后排列的次序」（第 1 个义项：依据发生时间的排列方式）；句意为修复师把散落的信件按年份从最早排到最晚，再依时间顺序装订成册。可辨识物件：按年摊开的纸牌、年份标签、装订线、信件堆。

pos.zh: 时间顺序；编年次序（不可数，指一种排列方式）

derivatives.zh: 精密计时器（同 chron- 词根）

senses.title: Arrangement by time of occurrence
senses.definition: the sequence in which items are placed from earliest to latest according to when they happened
senses.definitionCN: 按发生时间由早到晚摆放各项的次序
senses.example: The archive keeps the letters in chronological order, not by sender.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆按时间顺序保存信件，而不按寄信人。
senses.why: chronological is built on Greek chronos 'time', so the phrase names time itself as the sorting rule.
senses.whyCN: chronological 由希腊 chronos「时间」构成，因此这个短语以时间本身为排序规则。

senses.title: A narrative told in sequence
senses.definition: a story or account that follows events one after another rather than jumping about
senses.definitionCN: 按事件先后推进、不作跳跃的故事或叙述
senses.example: The film tells the war in chronological order, from the first telegram to the armistice.
senses.exampleCN: 影片按时间顺序讲这场战争，从第一封电报讲到停战。
senses.why: narrative can reorder time at will, so 'in chronological order' marks the choice not to.
senses.whyCN: 叙事本可任意重排时间，因此「按时间顺序」标记的是「不重排」这一选择。

senses.title: A dating sequence in science
senses.definition: the order of layers, specimens or events established by dating methods
senses.definitionCN: 用测年方法确定的层位、标本或事件的先后
senses.example: The cores were logged in chronological order from the surface down.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯自表层向下按年代顺序记录。
senses.why: stratigraphy assumes that deeper layers are older, which makes time the backbone of the record.
senses.whyCN: 地层学假定更深的层更古老，时间因此成为记录的骨架。

senses.title: A case record in sequence
senses.titleCN: 案件或病历的时序记录
senses.definition: the ordered record of events in a case, a patient's file or an investigation
senses.definitionCN: 案件、病历或调查中事件的按序记录
senses.example: The report sets out the accident in chronological order, minute by minute.
senses.exampleCN: 报告按时间顺序逐分钟还原这起事故。
senses.why: courts and clinicians need to show that nothing was skipped, and sequence is the proof.
senses.whyCN: 法庭与临床需要证明没有遗漏，而顺序就是证明。

senses.title: Reverse chronological order
senses.definition: the same ordering run backwards, newest first, standard in feeds and logs
senses.definitionCN: 同一排序反向运行，最新在前，常见于信息流与日志
senses.example: The blog lists posts in reverse chronological order so the newest sits on top.
senses.exampleCN: 博客按倒序时间排列文章，最新一篇在最上面。
senses.why: digital publishing made the reverse convention dominant, because readers want the latest first.
senses.whyCN: 数字出版使倒序成为主流，因为读者想先看到最新的。

senses.title: Relative versus absolute chronology
senses.definition: ordering by before-and-after relations, as opposed to fixed calendar dates
senses.definitionCN: 按先后关系排序，与固定的日历年代相对
senses.example: The site has a relative chronological order but no absolute dates.
senses.exampleCN: 该遗址有相对的时间顺序，却没有绝对年代。
senses.why: archaeology separates the two because sequence can be certain while dates remain unknown.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把两者分开，因为先后可以确定，而年代仍可能未知。

senses.title: An order that is not chronological
senses.definition: the phrase used as a standard against which thematic, spatial or random orders are judged
senses.definitionCN: 作为标准，用以衡量主题、空间或随机排列
senses.example: The exhibition groups the paintings by theme, deliberately ignoring chronological order.
senses.exampleCN: 展览按主题分组画作，有意不按时间顺序。
senses.why: a contrast term gains meaning from what it excludes, and here it excludes every non-temporal arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 对照性术语的意义来自它所排除的东西，这里它排除一切非时间的排列。

senses.title: Abstract: a logical sequence of steps
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：步骤的先后次序
senses.definition: loosely, the necessary sequence of steps in a process, as if each step had a date
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛指过程中必要的步骤次序，仿佛每一步都有日期
senses.example: The manual presents the repairs in chronological order, one after another.
senses.exampleCN: 手册按先后顺序逐一介绍各项修理步骤。
senses.why: the abstraction borrows time's irreversibility to say that one step must come before another.
senses.whyCN: 抽象用法借用了时间的不可逆性，来表达「一步必须先于另一步」。

intro.en: Chronological joins Greek chronos 'time' with logos 'word, reason, account' plus the adjective ending -ical. Order comes from Latin ordo 'row, series'. The phrase itself is a modern term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: chronological 把希腊 chronos「时间」与 logos「言词、理性、叙述」以及形容词词尾 -ical 结合在一起。order 来自拉丁 ordo「行列、次序」。短语本身是近代术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Chronos meant 'time' as a span or a period; its deeper origin is not established, so any proposed root is a hypothesis.
items.cn: chronos 意为作为跨度或时段的「时间」；其更远来源未得到证明，任何提出的词根都是假说。

items.en: Logos meant 'word, account, reason', from legein 'to gather, to say'; the link is generally accepted.
items.cn: logos 意为「言词、叙述、理性」，出自 legein「聚集、言说」；这一联系被普遍接受。

items.en: Latin chronologia, a Greek-Latin hybrid, named the science of dating events; it spread in sixteenth-century scholarship.
items.cn: 拉丁 chronologia 是希腊—拉丁混合词，指确定事件年代之学，在 16 世纪学术中流行。

items.en: Ordo meant 'row, line, rank, arrangement'; its own origin is disputed, possibly from a root for weaving a warp.
items.cn: ordo 意为「行列、等级、安排」；其自身来源有争议，可能出自表示「织经线」的词根。

items.en: Chronological order appears with the growth of archives, museums and scientific dating from the eighteenth century onward.
items.cn: 随着档案、博物馆与科学测年自 18 世纪起发展，chronological order 这一说法开始出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact earliest citation of the fixed phrase is agreed, chronos and ordo both lack settled pre-histories, and the weaving link for ordo is a suggestion only.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一固定短语的最早书证没有公认答案；chronos 与 ordo 均无定论的前史，ordo 与「织」的联系仅是推测。

note.en: Group one holds the words built on chronos that are easily mixed with the phrase; group two holds other ordering principles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 chronos、易与该短语混淆的词；第二组是其他排序原则。

entries.definition: A dated list or the science of dating; the order is the arrangement, the chronology is the list itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指带日期的年表或测年之学；order 是排列方式，chronology 是那份年表本身。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning arranged by time; the phrase needs the noun order to name the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为按时间排列；必须加名词 order 才指这种排列本身。

entries.definition: A precise clock used at sea; it shares the chron- root but measures time rather than arranging events.
entries.definitionCN: 海上使用的精密时钟；同为 chron- 词根，却用于计量时间而非排列事件。

entries.definition: A record arranged by date, from the same root; a chronicle is a document, chronological order is its principle.
entries.definitionCN: 按日期排列的记录，同出该词根；chronicle 是文献，chronological order 是其原则。

entries.definition: From Latin sequi 'to follow': any order of one after another, which need not be based on time.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sequi「跟随」：任何先后顺序，不一定以时间为依据。

entries.definition: A graphic line marked with dates; it displays chronological order rather than being the principle itself.
entries.definitionCN: 标有日期的图示直线；它展示时间顺序，而非顺序原则本身。

entries.definition: Arrangement by topic instead of date; exhibitions and essays often choose it over chronology.
entries.definitionCN: 按主题而非日期排列；展览与文章常选它而非时间顺序。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for what happened first; chronological order is its technical, formal label.
entries.definitionCN: 指「先发生了什么」的日常说法；chronological order 是其技术化、正式的名称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Chronos is time, logos is account, so chronological is 'time-account' ordering.
normal.cn: chronos 是时间，logos 是叙述，因此 chronological 就是「依时间叙述」的排序。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is 'in chronological order'; the preposition in marks the arrangement being used.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 in chronological order，介词 in 标记正在采用的排列方式。

normal.en: Reverse chronological order is the feed convention: newest first.
normal.cn: 倒序时间排列是信息流的惯例：最新在前。

normal.en: Keep chronology the noun apart from chronological the adjective.
normal.cn: 把名词 chronology 与形容词 chronological 分开。

normal.en: A timeline is the picture of chronological order, not the order itself.
normal.cn: timeline 是时间顺序的图示，而不是顺序本身。

abstract.en: Picture cards laid left to right with rising year numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象纸牌从左到右排开，年份数字依次递增。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of letters bound after being sorted by date.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠信件按日期分好之后被装订起来。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step is one day.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级是一天。

examples.en: List the sources in chronological order so that the argument's development is visible.
examples.cn: 按时间顺序列出资料，使论证的发展过程可见。

examples.en: The logs are kept in reverse chronological order, newest entry first.
examples.cn: 日志按倒序时间保存，最新一条在最前。

examples.en: Relative chronological order can be established without any absolute dates.
examples.cn: 无需任何绝对年代，也能建立相对的时间顺序。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「chrono（时间）+ logical（逻辑）+ order（顺序）」——按时间讲逻辑 → 时间顺序

root: chronological = 希腊 chronos「时间」+ logos「言词、叙述」+ -ical；order 来自拉丁 ordo「行列、次序」。chronos 与 ordo 的更深来源均不确定。英语短语 chronological order。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one rule of arrangement from the plain time sequence to narrative, scientific dating, case records, the reverse convention, relative chronology, non-temporal contrast and finally the logic of steps.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条排列规则展开：从纯时间序列到叙事、科学测年、案件记录、倒序惯例、相对年代、非时间对照，最后是步骤的逻辑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cards laid out by rising year numbers from left to right.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸牌按递增年份从左到右排开。

branches.en: TIME AS RULE: narration and arrangement both obey the clock unless they choose not to.
branches.cn: 以时间为规则：叙述与排列都服从时钟，除非刻意不服从。

branches.en: EVIDENCE ORDER: layers and case files prove completeness by their sequence.
branches.cn: 证据顺序：地层与案卷靠先后证明没有遗漏。

branches.en: REVERSAL: the same rule run backwards serves readers who want the newest first.
branches.cn: 反向：同一规则倒着运行，服务想先看最新内容的读者。

branches.en: WHAT IT EXCLUDES: relative dating and thematic shows are understood against this default.
branches.cn: 它所排除的：相对测年与主题展正是对照这一默认来理解。

branches.en: BORROWED LOGIC: step-by-step procedures borrow time's irreversibility.
branches.cn: 借用的逻辑：分步流程借用了时间的不可逆性。

intro.en: The phrase combines two Greek roots under one adjective ending with a Latin noun, so every piece can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个希腊词根组合的形容词与一个拉丁名词放在一起，每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek chronos gives chronology and chronometer; logos gives logic and -logy; Latin ordo gives order, ordinal and ordinary.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 chronos 构成 chronology 与 chronometer；logos 构成 logic 与 -logy；拉丁 ordo 构成 order、ordinal 与 ordinary。

items.example: Chronos is the first element.
items.exampleCN: chronos 是第一个成分。

items.example: Logos supplies the -logy ending.
items.exampleCN: logos 提供 -logy 词尾。

items.example: chronological means relating to time order.
items.exampleCN: chronological 意为与时间次序有关。

items.meaning: a dated list or the science of dating
items.example: The chronology runs to forty pages.
items.exampleCN: 这份年表长达四十页。

items.example: The chronometer survived the voyage.
items.exampleCN: 这只精密计时器经受住了航行。

items.example: The order follows the dates.
items.exampleCN: 顺序依日期而定。

items.example: First and second are ordinals.
items.exampleCN: first 与 second 是序数词。

items.example: An ordinary day follows its usual order.
items.exampleCN: 平常的一天按常规次序展开。

latinEntries.structure: chronologia, chronologiae (f., first declension, Greek-Latin hybrid)

definition_zh: 考古解释；依据物质遗存还原过去生活与意义的系统解读
definition_en: the systematic reading of material traces in order to explain past behaviour and meaning
core_image: 散落的陶片、灰坑与地层剖面被一条推理链重新串成一段可讲述的日常生活
scene: 探方清理完毕，学生把陶片、灰坑与炭屑逐层登记，再让三者互相印证。 The archaeological interpretation of the burnt layer rests on three independent lines of evidence.
sceneCN: 这里「考古解释」指依据物质遗存推断过去生活的系统解读（第 1 个义项：作为整体实践）；句意为对这一烧结层的考古解释建立在三条独立证据之上。

pos.zh: 考古解释（可数，指一项具体解读；亦可作不可数，指这类工作整体）

derivatives.zh: archaeo-（希腊 arkhaios「古老的」）+ -logy（希腊 -logia「学问」）→ 考古学：对古物的系统研究
拉丁 interpretari（解释、翻译）+ 英语动词化 → 解释；口译
interpret + -ation（动作或结果）→ 解释；解读
interpret + -ive（属性后缀）→ 解释性的
re-（重新）+ interpret → 重新解释（语义偏移：换一套框架重读旧证据）
mis-（错误）+ interpret → 误读（语义偏移：把证据读成它不支持的意思）

senses.title: The discipline at work
senses.titleCN: 作为整体实践：从遗存读出过去
senses.definition: the whole practice of drawing explanations about past life from material remains
senses.definitionCN: 从物质遗存中推断过去生活状况的整体工作
senses.example: The archaeological interpretation of the burnt layer rests on three independent lines of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 对这一烧结层的考古解释建立在三条独立证据之上。
senses.why: archaeo- comes from Greek arkhaios 'ancient', itself from arkhe 'beginning'; -logy is Greek -logia 'account, study'. Interpretation adds Latin interpres, the go-between who explains one party to another, so the phrase names the reasoned account that carries mute objects into words.
senses.whyCN: archaeo- 出自希腊 arkhaios「古老的」，其根为 arkhē「开端」；-logy 出自希腊 -logia「叙述、学问」。interpretation 又带来拉丁 interpres「居中传话者」的意思，因此整个短语指把沉默的物件翻译成人话的有据叙述。

senses.title: One stated reading of a site
senses.titleCN: 一项具体的解读：针对某遗址或某批遗存
senses.definition: a single explanation offered for one site, layer or group of finds
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一遗址、地层或一组出土物提出的具体解释
senses.example: Her archaeological interpretation of the pits as storage cellars was later challenged.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这些坑解释为储粮窖的考古解读后来受到质疑。
senses.why: This is the countable use: each reading is one answer put forward, and the phrase keeps the whole apparatus of evidence behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这是可数用法：每一种读法都是提出的一个答案，而短语仍带着背后整套证据的分量。

senses.title: Reading the layers
senses.titleCN: 读地层：按堆积顺序与相互关系判断先后
senses.definition: reading the order and mutual relations of deposits to establish sequence
senses.definitionCN: 通过堆积的顺序与相互关系确定时间先后
senses.example: The archaeological interpretation began with the section drawing, not with the artefacts.
senses.exampleCN: 这项考古解释从剖面图开始，而不是从器物开始。
senses.why: Stratum is Latin for a spread-out bed; because every layer buries what lies beneath it, the order of the layers is itself a clock, and reading a clock is the first act of interpretation.
senses.whyCN: stratum 在拉丁语里是「铺开的一层」；每一层都压住下面一层，因此层的顺序本身就是一只钟，读钟就是解释的第一步。

senses.title: Reading what happened after burial
senses.titleCN: 读埋藏后的经历：遗存如何被扰动、搬运、保存
senses.definition: reconstructing what happened to remains after they were deposited
senses.definitionCN: 重建遗存堆积之后所经历的扰动、搬运与保存过程
senses.example: Their archaeological interpretation treats the missing skull as a product of later disturbance.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的考古解释把头骨的缺失视为后期扰动的结果。
senses.why: Greek taphos 'burial' plus nomos 'law' gives taphonomy, the study of what burial does to a body or an object; interpretation must subtract that history before it can speak of the past.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 taphos「埋葬」加 nomos「法则」构成埋藏学，研究埋葬对遗体或器物做了什么；解释必须先扣掉这段经历，才能谈过去。

senses.title: Reading function
senses.titleCN: 读功能：推断器物曾经用来做什么
senses.definition: inferring from form, wear and context what an object was used for
senses.definitionCN: 由形制、使用痕迹与共存关系推断器物的用途
senses.example: Microwear on the blades supports an archaeological interpretation of them as sickles.
senses.exampleCN: 刀片上的微痕支持把它们解释为镰刀的考古解读。
senses.why: Function is the plainest thing a tool can be asked about: shape limits what a hand could do with it, and wear records what hands actually did.
senses.whyCN: 功能是工具最容易被追问的一件事：形状限定了手能拿它做什么，使用痕迹则记录了手实际做了什么。

senses.title: Reading society and meaning
senses.titleCN: 读社会与意义：身份、仪式与观念
senses.definition: inferring status, ritual and symbolic meaning from the arrangement of finds
senses.definitionCN: 由遗存的布置推断身份、仪式与象征意义
senses.example: An archaeological interpretation of the grave goods reads the imported beads as a claim to status.
senses.exampleCN: 对随葬品的考古解释把外来珠子读作对身份的宣告。
senses.why: Once function is settled, the same objects can be asked what they said: a bead far from its source is evidence of a trade route and of a person who wanted to be seen with it.
senses.whyCN: 功能确定之后，同一批物件还能被追问「它们说了什么」：一颗远离产地的珠子既证明贸易路线，也证明有人愿意戴着它被看见。

senses.title: The assembled narrative
senses.titleCN: 拼合的整体叙述：把零散证据写成一段生活
senses.definition: the coherent account of a settlement's life built from many separate readings
senses.definitionCN: 由许多单项解读拼成的、关于某聚落生活的连贯叙述
senses.example: The final archaeological interpretation describes a seasonal camp rather than a permanent village.
senses.exampleCN: 最终的考古解释描述的是一处季节性营地，而非永久村落。
senses.why: A narrative is what happens when single readings are set beside one another until they form a story; interpretation at this scale is composition, not a single inference.
senses.whyCN: 把单项解读彼此并置，直到它们成为一个故事，这就是叙述；这一层面的解释是「组稿」，而非一次单独推断。

senses.title: A rival reading
senses.titleCN: 修正性的对立解读：用新证据改写旧结论
senses.definition: a revised reading that replaces an earlier one after new evidence or new theory
senses.definitionCN: 因新证据或新理论而取代旧结论的修正读法
senses.example: The current archaeological interpretation reverses the earlier claim about who built the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 当前的考古解释推翻了早先关于谁修筑这道墙的说法。
senses.why: Interpres also meant a negotiator between two sides; when two readings negotiate, the older one does not vanish, it is recorded as superseded, which is why revision is itself a sense of the phrase.
senses.whyCN: interpres 也曾指居间谈判者；当两种读法谈判时，旧的并不消失，而是被记为已被取代——修正本身因此也是一个义项。

intro.en: Archaeological interpretation joins a Greek word for the study of ancient things to a Latin word for the act of explaining. The Greek deeper layer is only partly settled, and the second element of the Latin noun is openly disputed.
intro.cn: 「考古解释」把希腊语的「古物之学」与拉丁语的「解释之举」接在一起。希腊语更深一层只有部分定论，拉丁名词的第二个成分则公认有争议。

items.en: Arkhaios 'ancient, primitive' is formed on arkhe 'beginning, first cause', which comes from arkhein 'to begin, to rule'. The further Indo-European origin of arkhein is not established, and forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: arkhaios「古老的、原初的」由 arkhē「开端、首要原因」构成，而 arkhē 来自 arkhein「开始、统治」。arkhein 更早的印欧来源未定，凡为其拟出的形式都属重构。

items.en: -Logia 'account, study' derives from logos 'word, speech, reason', built on legein 'to gather, to say'. The common Indo-European root behind legein is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: -logia「叙述、学问」出自 logos「言词、理性」，后者由 legein「收集、说出」构成。legein 背后的印欧共同词根是重构，而非有记录的形式。

items.en: Interpres, interpretis meant 'go-between, negotiator, explainer'. It is built on inter 'between' plus an element of uncertain origin, sometimes linked to pretium 'price'; that link is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: interpres 意为「居间者、谈判者、解释者」，由 inter「在……之间」加一个来源不明的成分构成，该成分有时被联系到 pretium「价格」；这一联系只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Interpretatio 'explanation, translation, exposition' is the action noun of interpretari, the verb built on interpres. English took it through Old French at the end of the Middle Ages.
items.cn: interpretatio「解释、翻译、阐发」是动词 interpretari 的行为名词，而 interpretari 由 interpres 构成。英语经古法语在中世纪末吸收该词。

items.en: Archaeology entered English in the seventeenth century as a word for the description of antiquities, and only in the nineteenth century became a field with its own methods; the exact phrase archaeological interpretation belongs mostly to twentieth-century practice.
items.cn: archaeology 于 17 世纪进入英语，指对古物的描述，到 19 世纪才成为有自身方法的学科；「考古解释」这一确切搭配大体属 20 世纪的实践语言。

items.en: Source uncertain: no fixed first citation exists for the exact phrase, the second element of interpres has no agreed origin, and every Indo-European form proposed for arkhein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这一确切短语没有公认的最早书证；interpres 的第二成分没有一致来源；凡为 arkhein 拟出的印欧形式均为重构。

note.en: Group one holds the archaeological terms that are routinely mistaken for the interpretation itself; group two holds the general words for a reading or an account.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误当成「解释本身」的考古术语；第二组是泛指「读法、说法」的普通词。

entries.definition: The discipline that produces interpretations; it is the workshop, while an interpretation is one thing made in it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生各种解释的学科；它是作坊，而某项解释只是作坊里的一件成品。

entries.definition: The surviving material traces taken as a whole; it is what gets read, not what the reading says.
entries.definitionCN: 留存下来的物质遗存总体；它是被读的对象，而非读出的结论。

entries.definition: The formal publication of what was found and how; it carries interpretations but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 正式发表出土物及其发掘过程的文献；它承载解释，但本身不是解释。

entries.definition: The study of layer order; it supplies the sequence that any interpretation must respect.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地层顺序的学问；它提供任何解释都必须遵守的先后次序。

entries.definition: Any act of assigning meaning to signs; it is the everyday counterpart of interpretation.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指对符号赋予意义的行为；是 interpretation 的日常说法。

entries.definition: A statement that makes something intelligible, often by giving a cause; an interpretation may explain, but it reads meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事变得可理解的陈述，常给出原因；解释可以说明，但 interpretation 侧重读出意义。

entries.definition: A proposition put forward for testing; an interpretation is broader and need not be framed as a test.
entries.definitionCN: 为接受检验而提出的命题；interpretation 范围更广，未必写成可检验的形式。

entries.definition: An ordered account of events; an interpretation becomes a narrative when readings are composed into a story.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的有序叙述；当多项解读被组成故事时，interpretation 就成了 narrative。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arkhaios 'ancient' + -logia 'study': the reasoned account of ancient things.
normal.cn: arkhaios「古老」+ -logia「学问」：关于古物的有理据叙述。

normal.en: interpres is the go-between, so interpretation is the act of carrying a mute object's message across to a reader.
normal.cn: interpres 是居间传话者，因此解释就是把沉默物件的讯息运到读者这一边。

normal.en: The family runs archaeology, archaeologist, interpret, interpretation, interpretive, reinterpret, misinterpret.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 archaeology、archaeologist、interpret、interpretation、interpretive、reinterpret、misinterpret。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the work: interpretation of the site, competing interpretations, revise an interpretation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这项工作：对遗址的解释、相互竞争的解释、修正一项解释。

normal.en: Fieldwork order: layer, then disturbance, then function, then meaning, then a written account.
normal.cn: 田野里的顺序：先看层，再看扰动，再看功能，再看意义，最后写成文。

abstract.en: Picture an interpreter standing at a checkpoint between a heap of broken pots and a room of living readers.
abstract.cn: 想象一位译员站在关卡上，一边是碎陶堆，一边是活着的读者。

abstract.en: Picture a section drawing in which each coloured band is a sentence of a very slow book.
abstract.cn: 想象一张剖面图上每条色带都是一本极慢的书里的一句话。

abstract.en: Picture two maps of the same mound pinned side by side, each claiming to be the true one.
abstract.cn: 想象同一座土丘的两张图并排钉着，各自声称自己才是真的。

examples.en: Three teams produced the same archaeological interpretation of the walls from different evidence.
examples.cn: 三个团队从不同证据得出了相同的城墙考古解释。

examples.en: The archaeological interpretation of a single bead can carry a whole argument about trade.
examples.cn: 对一颗珠子的考古解释可以承载整套关于贸易的论证。

examples.en: Good practice states the archaeological interpretation separately from the evidence that supports it.
examples.cn: 规范的做法是把考古解释与支持它的证据分开陈述。

dict_mnemonic.text: archaeo（古老）+ logy（学问）+ interpretation（解释）＝ 把古物翻译成人话；记「先排队（地层），再看功能，最后谈意义」。

root: 考古：希腊 arkhaios「古老的」（源自 arkhē「开端」）+ -logia「学问、叙述」；解释：拉丁 interpretatio，来自 interpres「居中传话者」，其第二成分来源不确定，与 pretium「价格」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one move: mute traces are put back into a context, asked what they did, asked what they meant, and finally argued over in writing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把沉默的遗存放回情境，先问它做过什么，再问它意味着什么，最后落成文字并接受争论。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a broken pot, a hearth and a layer of ash are linked by one chain of reasoning into a day that can be told.
core.cn: 核心意象：碎陶、灶坑与一层灰被一条推理链连成一个可以讲述的日子。

branches.en: THE READING ITSELF: the practice as a whole, then one stated answer about one site.
branches.cn: 读法本身：先是整体工作，再是针对某遗址给出的一个答案。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: layer order turns a pile into a sequence before anything else can be said.
branches.cn: 时钟：地层顺序先把一堆东西变成有先后的序列，别的判断才谈得上。

branches.en: THE AFTERLIFE OF EVIDENCE: disturbance and decay must be subtracted before the past speaks.
branches.cn: 证据的来世：必须先扣掉扰动与腐朽，过去才开口。

branches.en: WHAT IT DID, THEN WHAT IT SAID: use-wear first, status and ritual afterwards.
branches.cn: 先做过什么，再说过什么：先看使用痕迹，后谈身份与仪式。

branches.en: COMPOSITION AND REVISION: single readings become a story, and a story can be replaced by a rival one.
branches.cn: 组稿与改写：单项解读合成故事，故事又会被对立的一版取代。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Greek prefix-root pair and a Latin verb family, so both halves can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个短语由希腊语的前缀与词根、以及拉丁语动词词族两部分构成，两半都可按语素读出。

latinIntro.en: Greek arkhaios and -logia supply the first word; Latin interpres and interpretatio supply the second, and the Latin family is the larger one in English.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 arkhaios 与 -logia 提供第一个词；拉丁 interpres 与 interpretatio 提供第二个词，而拉丁词族在英语中更庞大。

items.example: The archaeo- element appears in archaeology and archaeometry.
items.exampleCN: archaeo- 这一成分出现在 archaeology 与 archaeometry 中。

items.example: The suffix also builds biology and geology.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 biology 与 geology。

items.meaning: the study of ancient material remains
items.meaningCN: 考古学：研究古代物质遗存
items.example: Archaeology supplies the evidence that the phrase reads.
items.exampleCN: 考古学提供这个短语所读的证据。

items.meaningCN: 考古学的；属于该学科的
items.example: The adjective marks the kind of interpretation being offered.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词限定解释的类别。

items.example: The Latin noun names the person who carries a message across.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指把讯息运过边界的人。

items.example: Scholars interpret the same layer in different ways.
items.exampleCN: 学者们以不同方式解释同一层位。

items.meaning: the act or result of explaining
items.example: The written interpretation is kept apart from the raw finds.
items.exampleCN: 成文的解释与原始出土物分开保存。

items.example: The interpretive text hangs beside the display case.
items.exampleCN: 解释性文字挂在展柜旁。

items.meaning: to explain again in a new frame
items.example: Later scholars reinterpret the same walls as a boundary ditch.
items.exampleCN: 后来的学者把这些墙重新解释为界沟。

latinEntries.structure: archaeologia, -ae (New Latin, f., first declension, from Greek)
